```text
# Agent skill compatibility

This page records the cross-agent `SKILL.md` constraints this repo targets.
The goal is practical portability across coding agents, not the broadest set
of optional product-specific extensions.

## Baseline we target

Use the [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) as
the portable baseline:

| Field | Repo policy |
|---|---|
| `name` | Required, 1-64 chars, lowercase letters/digits with single hyphen separators, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, should match the skill directory |
| `description` | Required, 1-1024 chars, describes both what the skill does and when to use it |
| `SKILL.md` body | Keep under ~500 lines; move long detail into `references/` |
| Optional frontmatter | Allowed only when a target agent needs it; keep local skills portable by default |

Description budget tiers used by `skill-author`:

| Tier | Length | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to the body or references |
| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |

Also make the first 60 characters useful. The `npx skills` installer truncates
picker hints to 60 characters, and Codex may shorten descriptions when the
installed skill list is large.

## Agent notes

| Tool | Preference / constraint | Link |
|---|---|---|
| Agent Skills spec | Defines the portable directory layout, frontmatter fields, 64-char `name`, 1024-char `description`, optional `scripts/`, `references/`, and `assets/`. | [Specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) |
| Codex | Starts with each skill's name, description, and path, then loads full `SKILL.md` only when selected. The initial skills list has a context budget; descriptions should be concise and front-loaded. Codex can use optional `agents/openai.yaml` for UI metadata and invocation policy. | [Codex skills docs](https://developers.openai.com/codex/skills/create-skill) |
| Claude Code | Follows the open standard and adds fields such as `when_to_use`, `disable-model-invocation`, `user-invocable`, `allowed-tools`, `context`, and `hooks`. It truncates combined `description`/`when_to_use` listing text at 1,536 chars. | [Claude Code skills docs](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills) |
| Cursor | Uses `SKILL.md` skills with the same practical 64-char `name` and 1024-char `description` budget in its managed `create-skill` guidance. It also supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills. | [Cursor skills docs](https://cursor.com/docs/skills) |
| OpenCode | Recognizes `.opencode/skills`, `.claude/skills`, and `.agents/skills`; only specific frontmatter fields are recognized, unknown fields are ignored. It enforces 1-64 char names and 1-1024 char descriptions. | [OpenCode Agent Skills](https://opencode.ai/docs/skills/) |
| `npx skills` | Installer/distributor. Reads `name` and `description` from `SKILL.md`, shows only a 60-char description hint in the picker, and uses `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` for grouping. | [npx skills metadata model](npx-skills-metadata.md) |

## How this repo applies it

- Local skills should keep `description` in the green tier unless there is a
  concrete trigger-coverage reason to go longer.
- `skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh` enforces the portable hard
  limits: hyphen-case names, 64-char names, and 1024-char descriptions. It also
  reports yellow/orange tier notes without failing strict mode.
- `skills/local/skill-author/assets/SKILL.md.template` tells new authors to
  target 120-500 chars and never exceed 1024.
- Detailed trigger examples belong in `SKILL.md` body or `references/`, not in
  an oversized frontmatter description.
- Product-specific metadata is acceptable when needed, but should be deliberate:
  prefer portable frontmatter for local skills, leave vendored upstream metadata
  intact, and document any target-agent-only field in the skill body.

## Incident that set the policy

`mkdocs-site-bootstrap` previously had a 1106-character frontmatter

This skill is **consent-gated**. It records the user's preferences in
`.skills/preferences.yaml` and never repeats destructive actions without
asking. If the user changes their mind, `scripts/check-preferences.sh --reset
mkdocs_site_bootstrap` clears the recorded decision so the next invocation
starts fresh.

## When to trigger

- User asks to "set up docs", "create a docs site", "add a documentation
  site", "publish docs to GitHub Pages"
- User has loose markdown notes / a `docs/` directory and wants it browsable
- User wants the same docs stack as the `daviddwlee84/agent-skills` repo
  applied to a new project
- User says they want an LLM-friendly docs site (llms.txt, copy-to-LLM)
- User asks for "bilingual docs", "雙語 docs", "i18n", "multilingual",
  "add Traditional Chinese", "add zh-TW", "translate the docs", or to add
  any non-English language to an existing site → jump to step 7

## When NOT to trigger

- User just wants to write a single doc file → don't scaffold a whole site
- User explicitly opted out (preferences.yaml says `enabled: false`) → defer
  unless the user is now reversing that decision
- User wants to evaluate or benchmark a skill → use `skill-creator`
- User wants to author a new agent skill → use `skill-author`

## Workflow

### 1. Read preferences first

Before doing anything, check whether this repo already has a recorded
decision:

```bash
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
  --get mkdocs_site_bootstrap
```

Possible states:

| State | Meaning | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| File doesn't exist or key missing | Never asked | Proceed to step 2 (interview) |
| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: true` | Site is live | Skip to step 6 (ongoing helpers) |
| `enabled: true, pages_deployed: false` | Bootstrapped but not deployed | Skip to step 5 (deploy) |
| `enabled: false` | User opted out | Confirm they want to reverse that, then `--reset` and re-run |

### 2. Interview (only if no recorded decision)

Ask the user explicitly:

1. "Do you want a MkDocs Material documentation site for this project?
   (yes / no / I'll think about it)"
2. If yes: "Should it auto-deploy to GitHub Pages on push to main?
   (yes / no — I'll deploy manually)"

Record both answers immediately so an interrupted session doesn't lose them:

```bash
bash skills/local/mkdocs-site-bootstrap/scripts/check-preferences.sh \
  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.enabled=true \
  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.stack=mkdocs-material \
  --set mkdocs_site_bootstrap.auto_deploy=true
```

If the user said no, record `enabled: false` and stop. Don't pester on
future invocations.

### 3. Detect existing docs (consent gate)

Before scaffolding, scan the target repo. Read
`references/existing-docs-handling.md` for the full decision tree, but
the short version:

- If `mkdocs.yml` already exists → report "looks like an mkdocs site already
  exists at <path>; not overwriting" and stop.
- If `docs/` exists and is non-empty → list the files, ask the user one of:
  (a) skip — leave my docs alone, just create `mkdocs.yml` pointing at them;
  (b) wrap — create `mkdocs.yml` with my files included as-is in the nav;
  (c) manual — let me reorganize first, then re-run.
- If neither exists → safe to scaffold from scratch.

Record the decision under `mkdocs_site_bootstrap.existing_docs_decision`.

### 4. Scaffold

Run `init-docs-site.sh`. It writes (or refuses to overwrite) `mkdocs.yml`,
`pyproject.toml` (with `[project.optional-dependencies] docs = […]`), the
`docs/` skeleton, `.github/workflows/docs.yml`, and stub assets for
copy-to-llm. It also appends `/site/` (the `mkdocs build` output dir) to
```

# `npx skills` skips a skill: "YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings"

## Symptom

`npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills` clones fine, then
quietly drops skills from the picker:

```
⚠ Skipped /var/folders/.../skills/local/fastapi-ai-patterns/SKILL.md — YAML parse error: Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings at line 2, column 14:

description: Production patterns and gotchas for building FastAPI services, esp…
             ^

◇  Found 56 skills
```

The install still "succeeds" — the skipped skills simply never appear in the
selection UI, and no non-zero exit code is returned. Three skills were being
dropped this way (`fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold`,
`verifiable-surfaces`) before anyone noticed.

The caret points at column 14, i.e. the start of the *value* — misleading,
because the actual offending character is much further right.

## Root cause

An unquoted YAML value (a *plain scalar*) may not contain `": "`. YAML reads
the first colon-space as a key/value separator, i.e. a nested mapping inside a
value that is already a mapping value — which is illegal in flow ("compact")
context:

```yaml
description: Use when you build, review, or debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def
#                                                              ^ second mapping separator → parse error
```

All three broken descriptions used the same natural-English pattern —
`"…, or setting up a model-serving API with the production basics pre-wired: router/service…"`,
`"The invariant: a surface that cannot be exercised…"`. Colon-space is very
easy to write in a long description and there is no visual cue that it breaks

```yaml
---
name: skill-author
description: Author a new agent skill or refactor an existing one to follow agentskills.io best practices — gotchas sections, output templates, validation loops, calibrated specificity (fragility-based), and agentic script design (--help, --dry-run, structured stdout, stderr diagnostics, PEP 723 inline deps, pinned uvx/npx versions). Use whenever the user wants to create a new skill from scratch, scaffold a SKILL.md, write a reference file, design a script meant to be invoked by an agent, lint a draft skill for quality, or convert an ad-hoc workflow into a reusable skill. For evaluating skill output quality with test cases, benchmarking, or optimizing the description trigger rate, defer to the `skill-creator` skill instead — this skill focuses on authoring, not evaluation.
---
```

## Body structure

`# Skill Author` → `## When to use this vs skill-creator` (decision table) → `## Workflow` (6 numbered steps) → `## Available scripts` → `## Bundled assets` → `## Reference files` → `## Gotchas` → `## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)`.

### Frontmatter rules (hard)

- Only `name` + `description` are required; **keep them the only fields** for portability (agent-specific fields allowed but must be deliberate).
- `name`: lowercase letters/digits/single hyphens, no leading/trailing hyphen, no `--`, **≤64 chars**, **must match the directory basename** (mismatch = lint warning).
- `description`: **≤1024 chars hard**. Budget tiers (enforced/reported by `lint-skill.sh`):

| Tier | Length | Meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| Green | 120–500 | **Preferred for local skills** |
| Yellow | 501–900 | valid but context-heavy (note) |
| Orange | 901–1024 | valid, close to loader limits (note) |
| Red | >1024 | **error** — invalid for Codex/Cursor |

- Description must be **"pushy"** with concrete trigger phrases; the linter warns if it lacks `use when|use whenever|use this|trigger|invoke when`.
- **First 60 chars must be meaningful** — `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
- **QUOTING RULE (the biggest landmine):** a YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` and ` #` starts a comment. Wrap any description containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation in **single quotes**. Otherwise `npx skills` silently drops the skill with "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" *and still exits 0*. See `/Users/david/Documents/Program/agent-skills/pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md`. Live examples of correct quoting: `fastapi-ai-patterns`, `fastapi-ai-scaffold`, `verifiable-surfaces` (all single-quoted).

### File layout

```
skills/local/<name>/
├── SKILL.md      # required
├── references/   # long-form, loaded on demand
├── scripts/      # executable helpers (bash 3.2 compatible)
└── assets/       # templates copied into target projects
```
`tests/` is not in the canonical scaffold but two skills add it (see §6).

### Progressive disclosure (3 levels)

| Level | Loaded | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| Frontmatter | always | 120–500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
| `SKILL.md` body | on trigger | **<500 lines, <5000 tokens** |
| `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/` | on demand | unlimited |

Rule: every `references/*.md` must be cited **with a load condition** — "Read X **when** Y", not just "see X". Bare pointers get ignored or pre-loaded. `lint-skill.sh` warns on any `references/*.md` never mentioned in `SKILL.md`.

### Length limits (from `lint-skill.sh`)

- `<500` lines → ok
- `500–699` → **WARN** "move detail to references/"
- `≥700` → **FAIL** (exit 3)

### Authoring patterns to apply (`references/authoring-patterns.md`)

Spend context only on what the agent wouldn't know; **calibrated specificity** (prescriptive only where fragile, and always explain *why*); **defaults not menus**; **procedures over declarations**; **`## Gotchas` stays in SKILL.md** (never in a reference — by the time the agent loads it, the bug already happened); **output templates as literal pasted structures**; **checklists** for multi-step flows; **validation loops** (do→validate→fix→re-validate); **plan-validate-execute** for destructive ops.

Pre-commit checklist (verbatim from `references/authoring-patterns.md`): trigger contexts in description / 120–500 chars / first 60 chars useful / hyphen-case name ≤64 / <500 lines / every reference has a load condition / has `## Gotchas` / literal output templates / checklists with dependencies / `--dry-run` on destructive ops / scripts listed under `## Available scripts` with flags / **no caps-lock MUST/ALWAYS/NEVER without a why**.

### Script design (`references/script-design.md`)

- **Bash 3.2 compatible** (stock macOS): no `mapfile`, `${var,,}`, `${var^^}`, `[[ -v ]]`, `declare -A`, `wait -n`, `&>`.
- `#!/usr/bin/env bash` + `set -euo pipefail`, `chmod +x`.
- **No interactive prompts ever.** `--help` is the primary docs, must include Usage/Options/Examples/**Exit codes**.
- **Data → stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), diagnostics → stderr.**
- Errors: *what was wrong + what was expected + what to try* (include available alternatives).
- `--dry-run` on anything destructive; idempotent where possible.
- Python helpers: **PEP 723 inline deps** + `#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script`, not `requirements.txt`.
- **Pin `uvx`/`npx`/`pipx` versions** (`npx eslint@9.0.0`). `@latest` only if the skill says it tracks latest.
- Exit-code convention: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` missing input, `3` external failure, `4` validation failed, `≥10` skill-specific.

### Testing requirements

**There is no repo-wide testing requirement.** Nothing in `make validate` or CI runs tests. The only test wiring is `make test-skill`, hard-coded to `agent-history-hygiene`:
```make
test-skill:
	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/ -q
	bash skills/local/agent-history-hygiene/tests/test_scan_staged.sh
```
`pueue-job-queue` also ships `tests/` but is **not** in any Make target or CI — it documents its own invocation in `tests/README.md`. Bundling tests is a discretionary quality bar for script-heavy skills, not a gate.

# Pueue-Raycast-Extension — Reusable Lessons for a "Authoring Raycast Extensions" Skill

**Repo root:** `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension`

## 1. Repo shape: the extension IS the repo root

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/.claude/plans/users-david-src-tries-2026-07-09-transl-prancy-sprout.md` (§ "Repo layout") states the rule explicitly:

> Not a subdirectory: `ray build`/`develop`/`lint` all resolve `./package.json` and write `./raycast-env.d.ts` relative to cwd, and `npm run publish` copies the extension directory verbatim into `extensions/pueue/`.

Consequence noted in `backlog/store-publishing.md`: `npm run publish` uploads the whole directory, so `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `TODO.md`, `Justfile` ride along. Escape hatch (deliberately not built): a `just store-export` that rsyncs a clean subset to a temp dir.

Committed vs ignored (`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/.gitignore`): `node_modules/`, `.build/`, `.raycast-swift-build/`, `dist/`, `/site/`, `.venv/`. **`raycast-env.d.ts` and `package-lock.json` are committed** (lockfile is a store requirement; `npm ci` must work from a clean checkout).

## 2. The manifest (`package.json`) — every field earns its place

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/package.json`

### Top-level

```json
"$schema": "https://www.raycast.com/schemas/extension.json",
"name": "pueue", "title": "Pueue", "author": "da-wei_lee",
"license": "MIT", "categories": ["Developer Tools", "Productivity"],
"platforms": ["macOS"],
"dependencies": { "@raycast/api": "^1.104.23", "@raycast/utils": "^2.2.7" },
"devDependencies": { "@raycast/eslint-config": "^2.2.0", "@types/node": "^22.13.10",
  "@types/react": "^19.0.10", "eslint": "^9.0.0", "prettier": "^3.5.3",
  "react": "^19.0.0", "typescript": "^5.8.2" },
"scripts": { "build": "ray build", "dev": "ray develop", "lint": "ray lint",
  "fix-lint": "ray lint --fix", "publish": "npx @raycast/api@latest publish" }
```

- `"platforms": ["macOS"]` is **mandatory** when you ship a `menu-bar` command (menu bar is macOS-only).
- `@types/node ^22`, not 24: *"Raycast's runtime is Node 22 even though this shell has 24 via mise — typing against 24 lets you write APIs that throw at runtime."*
- ESLint 9 flat config is a 4-line passthrough — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/eslint.config.mjs`:
  ```js
  import { defineConfig } from "eslint/config";
  import raycastConfig from "@raycast/eslint-config";
  export default defineConfig([...raycastConfig]);
  ```

### The five `commands[]` — one per Raycast mode, deliberately

| `name` | `mode` | Notable manifest fields |
|---|---|---|
| `tasks` | `view` | `arguments: [{name:"query", type:"text", required:false}]` + per-command `preferences` (`showDetail` checkbox, `detailLogLines` textfield) |
| `add-task` | `view` | optional `command` text argument |
| `quick-add` | `no-view` | **required** `command` arg + optional `label` arg |
| `groups` | `view` | — |
| `queue-menu` | `menu-bar` | `"interval": "1m"` + 4 command-scoped prefs |

**Lesson — command arguments are the escape hatch from root search.** `tasks` takes a raw pueue query DSL string as an argument (`placeholder: "status=failed order_by id desc"`), so a power user never opens the UI to filter.

**Lesson — `no-view` is the highest value-per-line command.** From `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/quick-add.tsx` header: *"The highest value-per-line command in the extension: type the command as an argument, press return, done."* 86 lines total, exports `export default async function Command(props)` — **an async function, not a React component**.

### Preference design lessons

Per-command prefs vs extension-wide prefs is a real distinction (`raycast-env.d.ts` proves it: `Preferences.Tasks = ExtensionPreferences & {...}`).

Concrete preference-writing patterns worth stealing:

- **Preference descriptions carry the pitfall.** `pueuePath`'s description ends: *"Raycast runs under launchd with no shell rc, so a bare `pueue` is never on PATH."*
- **Descriptions state the cost.** `detailLogLines`: *"Higher values cost one extra `pueue log` call per selection change."*
- **Descriptions state the scaling risk.** `maxItemsPerSection`: *"Keeps a large queue from rendering hundreds of menu items every minute."*
- **Checkbox prefs need both `title` and `label`.** `confirmDestructive`: `title: "Confirmations"`, `label: "Confirm kill, remove, clean, and reset"`.
- **A `dropdown` pref uses `data: [{title, value}]`** — see `titleCounts`.
- **Multi-line config in a `textfield`**: the `connections` pref is "one per line", parsed by `parseConnections()` with **invalid lines surfaced in the UI, never silently dropped**.

### Never hand-write the `Preferences` type

From the plan doc: *"**Never hand-write a `Preferences` interface.** `ray build` generates globally-declared `Preferences.Tasks` / `Arguments.Tasks` etc. with *required* fields, so a code default drifting from the manifest becomes a compile error."*

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/raycast-env.d.ts` is generated and committed; it declares global `Preferences`, `Preferences.<Command>`, and `Arguments.<Command>` namespaces. Consumption sites:

```ts
const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.Tasks>();      // src/tasks.tsx:86
const prefs = getPreferenceValues<Preferences.QueueMenu>();  // src/queue-menu.tsx:64
function prefs(): Preferences { return getPreferenceValues<Preferences>(); }  // binary.ts:53
```

Note `titleCounts` is typed as a **string union** `"running" | "running-queued" | "active" | "none"` derived from the manifest `data`, and `menuTitle()` switches on `Preferences.QueueMenu["titleCounts"]`.

## 3. THE build-gate lesson: `ray build` does not typecheck

**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md`** — highest-value single pitfall for a generic Raycast skill.

Symptom: `ready  - built extension successfully` on a file with genuine type errors.
Cause: `ray build` bundles with esbuild, which **strips types without checking them**.

Two real bugs shipped past it:
1. A `MutatePromise<GroupMap>` passed to an `act()` typed for `MutatePromise<State>` — *"At runtime its optimistic update would have replaced the group map with a task state — the list would have emptied on every action."*
2. **`@raycast/api` bundles its own copy of `@types/react`**, so the root `React.ReactNode` is a structurally different type that silently fails to match `ActionPanel`'s children.

Fix for #2, applied at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/task-log.tsx:50`:
```ts
function logActions(task: Task, connection: Connection, extra?: React.JSX.Element | null)
```
> "When a prop needs to hold JSX, type it as an element rather than a node."

And: **`ray lint` doesn't typecheck either** — it runs ESLint + Prettier + manifest + icon checks. But it catches things `tsc` won't, *"including reserved-shortcut collisions (`⌘K` and `⌘P` are Raycast's own and are silently ignored if you bind them)"*. So all three are needed.

### The `Justfile` gate

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/Justfile`

```make
dev:   ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run dev
build: ([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && npm run build
lint / fix
typecheck: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json
verify:    rm -rf .build/verify && npx tsc --outDir .build/verify --module commonjs \
             --target ES2022 --lib ES2023 --esModuleInterop --resolveJsonModule \
             --skipLibCheck --strict src/lib/dev-check.ts && node .build/verify/dev-check.js
check: typecheck verify lint build     # the pre-commit gate
ci:    rm -rf node_modules && npm ci && just check
fixtures: pueue add 'sleep 120' / -s 'echo stashed' / 'false' / 'echo ok' / 'definitely-not-a-real-binary'
```

Two generalizable tricks:
- **Self-bootstrapping recipes**: `([ -d node_modules ] || npm install) && …`, because `ray` ships *inside* `@raycast/api`.
- **`just fixtures` seeds a live queue covering every status variant** so screenshots and manual verification have real data. This is a "seed the external system" recipe, not a unit-test fixture.

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/tsconfig.json`: `lib: ES2023`, `module: commonjs`, `target: ES2022`, `strict`, `isolatedModules`, `jsx: "react-jsx"`, `resolveJsonModule: true` (needed to import the JSON fixtures), `include: ["src/**/*", "raycast-env.d.ts"]`.

## 4. Testing without a test runner

**There is no test runner and that is a deliberate decision.** From `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/dev-check.ts:1-12`:

> "There is no test runner in a Raycast extension and adding one is store review noise, so this is a plain script: `just verify`, which compiles it with the already-installed tsc and runs it under node."

**977 lines of assertions**, structured as `check(name, actual, expected)` comparing `JSON.stringify`, printing `ok`/`FAIL`, setting `process.exitCode`.

The architectural precondition that makes this possible: **pure modules never import `@raycast/api`.** Stated in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/optimistic.ts:19-21`:

```ts
// Imported from the leaf modules rather than the `pueue` barrel on purpose:
// the barrel pulls in the transport and therefore @raycast/api, and this module
// must stay runnable outside Raycast so `just verify` can assert it.
```

Same discipline in `connections.ts` ("Deliberately free of Raycast imports so the parsing can be asserted"), `logfile.ts`, `argv.ts`, `normalize.ts`, `errors.ts`. `dev-check.ts` even re-probes for the binary itself because *"binary.ts can't be imported here because it pulls in @raycast/api"*.

### Fixtures

- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/fixtures/state.json` — 12 tasks, **one per status/result variant**, including task 5 = `Locked` wrapping `Done{ Failed: 127 }`, task 0 = `Stashed{enqueue_at: null}`, task 1 = `Stashed` with a future time, tasks 7–10 = FailedToSpawn / Killed / DependencyFailed / Errored, task 11 = `Locked` over `Queued`. Task 0 carries `"envs": { "SECRET_TOKEN": "must-never-be-cached" }` as a live reminder of the secret-stripping rule.
- `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/fixtures/stderr.json` — **7 failure shapes captured byte-exact from the real binary**, including raw `\x1b[91m` SGR escapes: `daemon-never-started`, `config-missing`, `clap-bad-argument`, `bad-query`, `plain-client-error`, `socket-absent`, `socket-refused`.

### The live `--help` conformance check

`dev-check.ts:471-488` — for all 16 mutation variants, it shells `pueue <subcommand> --help` and asserts every long flag `argvFor()` emits actually appears in it:

```ts
const missing = flags.filter((f) => !help.includes(f));
check(`${m.op}: ${flags.join(" ")}`, missing, []);
```

**Generalizable lesson:** if your extension wraps a CLI, assert your generated argv against the CLI's own `--help` at verify time — *"A flag in the wrong place, or one that doesn't exist, fails there instead of at runtime."*

## 5. Architecture: a transport seam, and layers that never leak

```
src/
  tasks.tsx  add-task.tsx  quick-add.tsx  groups.tsx  queue-menu.tsx   ← commands (manifest names)
  lib/
    actions.tsx          act() — mutation + optimistic + reconcile     (imports @raycast/api)
    optimistic.ts        pure predictors                               (NO raycast)
    error-states.tsx     describeError() + 3 renderers                 (imports @raycast/api)
    format.tsx           icons, colors, durations, section order       (imports @raycast/api Color/Icon)
    task-log.tsx         TaskLogView / TaskFollowView
    connection-ui.tsx    useConnection(), ConnectionSubmenu, banners
    group-dropdown.tsx   List.Dropdown searchBarAccessory
    dev-check.ts         the test script
    fixtures/            state.json, stderr.json
    pueue/
      index.ts           public barrel — views import from here and nowhere else
      transport.ts       TYPES ONLY — the seam (no runtime imports, no cycles)
      types.ts           1:1 with the CLI's serde output
      normalize.ts       pure flatteners                               (NO raycast)
      errors.ts          taxonomy + stderr cleaner                     (NO raycast)
      argv.ts            Mutation → string[]                           (NO raycast, NO child_process)
      cli-transport.ts   the ONLY file that knows it's a subprocess
      binary.ts          PATH resolution                               (imports @raycast/api for prefs)
      connections.ts     remote connection parsing                     (NO raycast)
      ssh.ts             quoting + multiplexing                        (NO raycast)
      logfile.ts         tail-from-disk                                (NO raycast)
```

### The seam is a *data union*, not argv

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/transport.ts:12-14`:

> "The seam only holds because mutations are modelled as *data*. If `mutate` took a `string[]` of argv, a socket transport would have to parse argv back into intent — which is not a seam, it is a shell."

```ts
export type Mutation =
  | { op: "add"; command: string; group?: string; label?: string; priority?: number;
      workingDirectory?: string; after?: number[]; delay?: string;
      stashed?: boolean; immediate?: boolean; escape?: boolean }
  | { op: "start" | "pause" | "kill"; ids?: number[]; group?: string; all?: boolean; … }
  | { op: "restart"; ids: number[]; inPlace?: boolean; … }
  | … 16 variants total

export interface PueueTransport {
  readState(o?: StatusOptions): Promise<State>;
  readGroups(o?): Promise<GroupMap>;
  readLogs(ids: number[], o?: LogOptions): Promise<LogMap>;
  mutate(m: Mutation, o?): Promise<number | void>;
  followLog(id, lines, h: FollowHandlers, o?): () => void;   // returns cancel
  probe(o?): Promise<{ version: string; major: number; reachable: boolean }>;
}
```

The factory + swap hook live in `index.ts`, deliberately **not** in `transport.ts`, so `transport.ts` stays types-only and `cli-transport.ts` can import it without a cycle:

```ts
let active: PueueTransport | undefined;
export function transport(): PueueTransport { return (active ??= createCliTransport()); }
export function setTransport(t: PueueTransport | undefined): void { active = t; }  // testing hook
```

### Types transcribed literally, ergonomics built on top

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/types.ts:5-8`:
> "These types are deliberately a literal transcription of the Rust structs rather than something ergonomic — the ergonomic view is built on top in `normalize.ts`. Keeping the transcription honest is what makes the normalizers trustworthy."

And `normalize.ts:5-6`: *"The whole point of this module is that no view should ever have to know that `status` is a two-level externally-tagged enum."*

## 6. Shelling out to a CLI from Raycast — the whole playbook

### 6a. The #1 hazard: launchd has no shell rc

**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-pueue-not-found.md`**

Symptoms: `Error: spawn pueue ENOENT`, "Pueue CLI not found" — *while `which pueue` in your terminal answers immediately.*

Cause: Raycast runs extensions in a managed Node process under **launchd**, which never sources `~/.zshrc` / `~/.zprofile`. The extension's `PATH` is roughly `/usr/bin:/bin`.

Fix — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/binary.ts`:
```ts
const PROBE_DIRS = [
  "/opt/homebrew/bin",              // Apple Silicon Homebrew
  "/usr/local/bin",                 // Intel Homebrew
  join(homedir(), ".cargo", "bin"),
  join(homedir(), ".local", "bin"),
  "/usr/bin", "/bin",
];
```
> "Both Homebrew prefixes must be probed. Hardcoding either breaks half of all Macs."

Resolution order in `resolvePueue()` — **preference first, `existsSync`-validated so a stale value falls through to the probe**, then the module cache, then the probe, then `throw new PueueError("binary-not-found", …)`.

**The meta-lesson (this is the expensive part):**
> "**A terminal hides the bug completely.** `npm run dev`'s console inherits your full interactive `PATH`, so anything you test from there works, including a `resolveBinary` that would fail in production. Every PATH-related change must be exercised **from Raycast** — root search or the menu bar — not from the dev terminal."

Corollary in `binary.ts:202-218` — `isBrewManagedDaemon()` gates a one-click "Start Daemon" action, because starting a daemon from Raycast makes it a launchd child that hands Raycast's stripped environment *to every task it ever runs*: *"the same PATH problem as above, except it silently poisons every future task instead of failing loudly once."*

Env for every spawn (`baseEnv()`): `{ ...process.env, HOME: process.env.HOME ?? homedir() }` — HOME passed through so the CLI finds its config dir.

### 6b. Every subprocess call funnels through one `run()`

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/cli-transport.ts`

```ts
const pexecFile = promisify(execFile);
const READ_TIMEOUT_MS  = 10_000;
const WRITE_TIMEOUT_MS = 15_000;
const SSH_TIMEOUT_MS   = 30_000;
const BIG_BUFFER = 64 * 1024 * 1024;   // execFile's default 1 MB truncates into a JSON parse error
```

- **Never `shell: true`.** `execFile` + argv array only.
- **`maxBuffer` must be raised** for any command whose output is unbounded. Here `status --json` embeds an env snapshot per task (~2 MB per 400 tasks) and `log --full` is unbounded by design.
- One `catch` → `fromExecError(e, [bin, ...argv])`, so all failures classify uniformly.

### 6c. Global flags precede the subcommand

**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/pueue-color-flag-must-precede-subcommand.md`**

```console
$ pueue status --color never --json    # exit 2, clap: "error: unexpected argument '--color' found"
$ pueue --color never status --json    # exit 0
```

Fix: `const argv = [...globalArgs(connection), ...args];` — *prepended, never appended*.

Two generalizable sub-lessons:
1. **Exit codes are 0, 1, AND 2** — not 0/1. Exit 2 with a leading `error:` classifies as `bad-arguments`, *"which is always an extension bug and is surfaced verbatim rather than dressed up."*
2. `--color never` does nothing for stderr because `color_eyre` writes SGR escapes even to a pipe and ignores both `--color` and `NO_COLOR`. It's still passed because it cleans up the *stdout* prose that reaches toasts.

### 6d. Argv discipline for user-supplied shell commands

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/argv.ts:26-29`:
```ts
a.push("--print-task-id");
// The command goes last, after `--`, as ONE argv element. pueue joins its
// variadic <COMMAND>... with spaces and hands the result to `sh -c`, so
// quoting it here would double-escape it. Never build a shell string.
a.push("--", m.command);
```

Asserted in `dev-check.ts`:
```ts
check("a command is never shell-quoted — pueue hands it to sh -c itself",
  argvFor({ op: "add", command: "echo 'it works'" }).at(-1), "echo 'it works'");
```

Related "Won't do" entry in `TODO.md`: `--escape` escapes spaces along with metacharacters, collapsing the whole line into one token — verified to turn `echo not-a-pipe | wc -l` into `sh: …: command not found`.

**Be explicit about flags whose default comes from the user's config:**
```ts
a.push(m.inPlace ? "--in-place" : "--not-in-place");
// "Being explicit means the action does what it says regardless of whose machine it runs on."
```

### 6e. Classify stderr into an actionable taxonomy

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/pueue/errors.ts`

```ts
export type PueueErrorKind =
  | "binary-not-found" | "config-missing" | "daemon-not-running"
  | "bad-query" | "bad-arguments" | "timeout" | "command-failed";

export class PueueError extends Error {
  readonly kind; readonly detail; readonly exitCode; readonly argv;
  constructor(kind, detail, opts) { super(firstLine(detail) || kind); … }
}
```

Pipeline: `fromExecError` → strip ANSI → drop noise → `classify(detail, exitCode)`.

- `cleanStderr()` breaks at `^Location:$`, drops `Run with RUST_BACKTRACE`, strips eyre's `   0: ` cause numbering — **but the regex requires a colon so the pest diagnostic gutter (`      1 | status=Nope`) survives**, because *"that alignment is the whole value of a bad-query message."* There's a `check()` for exactly that.
- **`NOISE_PATTERNS`** — `/^Different protocol version detected/i`. This is subtle and generalizable: a per-command warning is invisible on success but *lands first on failure*, so `firstLine()` would make it the toast title and hide the real error.
- `fromExecError` distinguishes: `code === "ENOENT"` → `binary-not-found`; `killed && (signal === "SIGTERM" || code === "ETIMEDOUT")` → `timeout` (*"execFile reports its own timeout as a SIGTERM kill, not as a distinct code"*).
- `PueueError.message` = `firstLine(detail)`, so a toast title is one line while `.detail` keeps the whole report for a `Detail` markdown fence.
- Predicates exported for the UI: `isBinaryMissing`, `isDaemonDown` (collapses `daemon-not-running` + `config-missing` because *"the remedy is identical"*), `isBadQuery`.
- The one eslint suppression in the codebase, with a reason:
  ```ts
  // eslint-disable-next-line no-control-regex -- color_eyre emits raw SGR even when stderr is a pipe
  const ANSI_SGR = /\u001b\[[0-9;]*m/g;
  ```

### 6f. Never infer capability from an exit code — parse the shape

`cli-transport.ts:327-340`:
```ts
async probe(o?) {
  const stdout = await run(["--version"], { timeout: 5_000, … });
  const m = /^pueue\s+(\d+)\.(\d+)/i.exec(stdout.trim());
  const major = m ? Number(m[1]) : 4;   // unparseable → assume current, don't block the user
  return { version, major, reachable: true };
}
```

### 6g. Strip secrets at the parse boundary, before anything can cache

`cli-transport.ts:178-194`:
```ts
/** `useCachedPromise` persists results to Raycast's disk-backed Cache, so keeping
 *  this field would write every secret in the submitting shell's environment to
 *  disk in plaintext. */
function stripEnvs(tasks: Record<string, RawTask>): Record<string, Task> { … delete lean.envs … }
export type Task = Omit<RawTask, "envs">;
```
Measured in `docs/pueue-json-contract.md`: *"six trivial tasks weigh 53,595 bytes with it and 2,509 without — 21×, at 120 variables per task."* An on-demand `taskEnvs(id)` re-reads it, explicitly *"never called from a render path."*

**This is a first-class Raycast lesson**: `useCachedPromise` → disk-backed `Cache` → any secret in a fetched payload is now on disk in plaintext.

### 6h. Guard against being handed the wrong shape

Two commands return *different* top-level shapes (`status --json` → `{tasks, groups}`; `group --json` → the inner map). `readState` explicitly guards:
```ts
if (!raw || typeof raw !== "object" || !("tasks" in raw))
  throw new PueueError("command-failed", "Unexpected `pueue status --json` payload");
```
and `readGroups` unwraps forward-compatibly: `parsed && "groups" in parsed ? parsed.groups : parsed`.

### 6i. Streaming: `spawn` + a cancel closure

```ts
followLog(id, lines, h: FollowHandlers): () => void {
  const child = spawn(bin, argv, { env: baseEnv() });
  child.stdout?.setEncoding("utf8");
  child.stdout?.on("data", (d: string) => h.onData(d));
  child.stderr?.on("data", (d: string) => (stderr += d));
  child.on("error", (e) => h.onError(e));
  child.on("close", (code) => {
    // exiting by itself is completion, not failure. Only non-zero is an error.
    if (code && code !== 0) h.onError(fromExecError({ code, stderr }, [bin, ...argv]));
    h.onDone(code);
  });
  return () => { if (!child.killed) child.kill("SIGTERM"); };
}
```

Consumer discipline in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/task-log.tsx:166-236`:
- `const FLUSH_MS = 200` — accumulate into a `useRef` and flush on an interval, because *"a render per chunk would be four re-renders a second for no benefit."*
- `const MAX_BUFFER_CHARS = 200_000` — trim the head with `"…earlier output trimmed…\n" + buffer.slice(-MAX)`.
- The `useEffect` cleanup calls `cancel()`: *"Leaving the view must kill the child, or a spawned `pueue follow` keeps tailing for as long as Raycast lives."*

## 7. Data fetching, caching, and the optimistic-update pitfall

### 7a. The single most transferable runtime lesson

**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/daemon-state-lags-one-poll-after-a-mutation.md`**

Symptom: *"kill a task → the row shows Killed → snaps back to Running → becomes Killed again a second later."*

Cause: **the backend acknowledges a request before its own update loop applies it**, and `useCachedPromise`'s `mutate()` **revalidates immediately on success by default**, so the follow-up read returns pre-change state and overwrites the optimistic update.

*Measured, not guessed* — five trials: `min 278 ms   median 284 ms   max 297 ms`, while the ack itself returns in ~22 ms.

Fix — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/actions.tsx:133-148`:
```ts
await state.mutate(runMutation(mutation, { connection: options.connection }), {
  optimisticUpdate: (data) => optimistic(data, mutation),
  rollbackOnError: true,
  shouldRevalidateAfter: false,      // the load-bearing line
});
setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);   // 400
setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_SETTLE_MS);  // 1500
```
> "Two reads rather than one pessimistic read: 400 ms clears the measured worst case and keeps actions feeling immediate, and 1500 ms covers a loaded daemon so a mis-tuned first delay never becomes visible."

And the menu-bar nudge is delayed by the same 400 ms, *"or a `launchCommand` fired immediately would have the menu bar re-read exactly the stale state we just worked around."*

### 7b. Optimistic updaters must refuse to guess

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/optimistic.ts` — *"Pure and total: no I/O, no React, and never throws."*

> "A mutation whose outcome cannot be predicted (a new task id, a queue reordering) returns the state unchanged rather than guessing — **a wrong prediction is worse than none**, because it flickers too."

Three unpredicted cases, each with a reason: starting a *queued* task needs the scheduler; a non-in-place restart mints an id only the daemon knows; `add` likewise. Asserted:
```ts
check("starting a queued task is NOT predicted — a free slot needs the scheduler", …, "queued");
check("a fresh restart is NOT predicted — the new id is unknowable", kinds(after), kinds(state));
check("the input state is never mutated in place", …, true);
```

### 7c. `act<T>()` is generic because different views cache different shapes

```ts
export async function act<T>(
  mutation: Mutation,
  state: { mutate: MutatePromise<T | undefined>; revalidate: () => void },
  options: ActOptions,
  optimistic: (data: T | undefined, m: Mutation) => T | undefined,
): Promise<boolean>
export const actOnTasks  = (…) => act(m, state, o, applyMutation);       // State
export const actOnGroups = (…) => act(m, state, o, applyGroupMutation);  // GroupMap
```
(The non-generic version of this is exactly the bug `ray build` shipped — see §3.)

`ActOptions` is a nice reusable shape: `{ verb: "Killing task 4" /* present continuous → toast title */, done: "Killed task 4" /* past tense */, confirm?: { title, message?, actionTitle?, destructive?, rememberChoice? }, connection? }`.

Confirmation flow:
```ts
if (options.confirm && prefs.confirmDestructive) {
  const ok = await confirmAlert({
    title, message,
    rememberUserChoice: options.confirm.rememberChoice,   // "Do not show this message again"
    primaryAction: { title: actionTitle ?? verb,
                     style: destructive ? Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive : Alert.ActionStyle.Default },
  });
  if (!ok) return false;
}
const toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: options.verb });
… toast.style = Toast.Style.Success; toast.title = options.done;
… catch → await showFailureToast(error, { title: options.verb, message: firstLine(error.detail) });
```
Note `rememberChoice` is deliberately omitted on `reset`: *"No rememberChoice: this one should ask every time."* And on failure it surfaces the CLI's own prose: *"pueue refuses some things outright — removing a running task, for one. Its prose is better than anything we'd write, so show it."*

### 7d. `useCachedPromise` argument keying and abort controllers

From `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/tasks.tsx:135-183`:

```ts
// Separate controllers: a superseded state read must not cancel an in-flight
// group read, and vice versa.
const stateAbort  = useRef<AbortController>(null);
const groupsAbort = useRef<AbortController>(null);

const state = useCachedPromise(
  // The connection is an argument rather than a closure capture so that
  // useCachedPromise keys its cache on it — switching daemons must not show
  // the previous one's tasks.
  (g: string, q: string, connectionName: string) => readStatus({ …, signal: stateAbort.current?.signal, … }),
  [group, query, conn.connection.name],
  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },
);
```

- **Pass everything the fetcher depends on as an *argument*, not a closure capture** — that's what keys the cache.
- **One `abortable` ref per independent read.**
- Conditional fetching with `execute`, and `keepPreviousData: false` when the value is per-selection:
  ```ts
  const preview = useCachedPromise(async (id, connectionName) => { … },
    [selectedId, conn.connection.name],
    { execute: showDetail && canHaveLog, keepPreviousData: false });
  ```
  *"Only the selected row, and only when the pane is open — one `pueue log` per selection change is fine, one per row would not be."*
- **Don't ask at all when you know the answer**: `hasEverRun(task)` gates the call, *"which also saves a subprocess spawn per selection change."*

`useCachedState` for UI state that should survive relaunch, **keyed by scope**:
```ts
const [group, setGroup] = useCachedState(`tasks.group:${conn.connection.name}`, …);
const [showDetail, setShowDetail] = useCachedState("tasks.showDetail", prefs.showDetail);
const [connectionName, setConnectionName] = useCachedState("connection.name", LOCAL_CONNECTION_NAME);
```
The comment on the first is a good general lesson:
> "a single shared key meant switching to another machine left the list filtered by a group that only exists elsewhere, showing nothing. Observed. Scoping the key makes the mistake unrepresentable instead of merely corrected."

Note `"connection.name"` is shared *deliberately* between the menu bar and the view commands so they never disagree.

`LocalStorage` (async, non-cache) for last-used form values, also scoped:
```ts
const lastGroupKey = (connection: string) => `add.group:${connection}`;
const lastCwdKey   = (connection: string) => `add.cwd:${connection}`;
await LocalStorage.setItem(lastGroupKey(connectionName), group);
await LocalStorage.getItem<string>(lastCwdKey(connectionName));
```
**`useCachedState` vs `LocalStorage`**: cached state for view state read synchronously during render; `LocalStorage` for values a *different command* must read (`quick-add.tsx` reads `add.group:Local` written by `add-task.tsx`).

### 7e. Cached data that has become a lie

**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/cached-list-renders-a-dead-queue-as-live.md`**

> "`useCachedPromise` keeps serving its last successful result when a fetch fails. That is the right default for a flaky read; it is the wrong default when the failure is *structural*, because then the cached data isn't a moment stale — it is a snapshot of a queue nobody can see any more."

Found by *actually running `brew services stop pueue` and looking*, not by reading code.

Three-tier error rendering, driven by one `ErrorDescriptor.structural` flag:

| Situation | Render |
|---|---|
| failed **first** read (no data at all) | `<List><ErrorEmptyView …/></List>` — the whole screen |
| structural failure **with** cached data | a `StaleBannerItem` row at the top of the list, same recovery actions |
| transient failure | the ordinary Raycast toast |

```tsx
const stale = error !== undefined && describeError(error, conn.connection).structural;
{stale ? <List.Section title="Connection"><StaleBannerItem …/></List.Section> : null}
```

**Sizing sub-lesson** — hence `ErrorDescriptor.shortTitle`:
> "With the detail pane open the list column is about a third of the window, and the full titles truncated to nonsense: `Pueu...  Showing...  Not...ected`"

---

## 8. Error/onboarding states: one descriptor, three renderers

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/error-states.tsx` — 393 lines, and the header states the motivating anti-pattern:

> "The reference extension this is modelled on grew two copies of an `errorMarkdown()` helper that drifted apart; one descriptor with three renderers avoids that. The menu bar needs the same information but cannot render a `List.EmptyView`, so it consumes `describeError()` directly."

```ts
export interface ErrorDescriptor {
  icon: Image.ImageLike;
  title: string;
  shortTitle: string;      // a few words, for the narrow list column
  description: string;     // one line, for List.EmptyView
  markdown: string;        // a full page, for Detail
  actions: ErrorAction[];  // declarative: { id, title, icon, copy? | url? | run? }
  structural: boolean;
}
export function describeError(error: unknown, connection?): ErrorDescriptor
```

Renderers: `ErrorEmptyView` (*"Must be rendered inside a `<List>` — `List.EmptyView` is not standalone"*), `StaleBannerItem` (a `List.Item`), `ErrorDetail` (a `Detail`), and `ErrorMenu` in `queue-menu.tsx` (a red-X `MenuBarExtra`).

The action list is **data**, so each renderer maps it to its own primitive:
```tsx
a.copy !== undefined ? <Action.CopyToClipboard content={a.copy}/>
: a.url !== undefined ? <Action.OpenInBrowser url={a.url}/>
: <Action onAction={() => a.run?.()}/>
// and in the menu bar: onAction={() => { if (a.copy) Clipboard.copy(a.copy); else if (a.url) open(a.url); else a.run?.(); }}
```

Onboarding content patterns worth copying:
- Copy-to-clipboard actions for the exact install/start commands (`INSTALL_BREW`, `INSTALL_CARGO`, `START_BREW`, `START_MANUAL` are exported consts).
- `openExtensionPreferences` as an action on every structural error.
- The markdown fences the raw stderr, with a `fence()` helper that neutralises embedded backticks: `text.replace(/```/g, "``\u200b`")` (zero-width space). Same trick in `task-log.tsx` and `tasks.tsx`.
- The markdown *explains the two error strings*: `"Did you start the daemon at least once?"` = never ran; `"while connecting to daemon"` = ran and stopped.
- Context-sensitivity: *"Never offer to start a daemon we aren't running. `brew services start` would start the *local* one, which is not the daemon that just failed."* → `const brewManaged = !remote && isBrewManagedDaemon();`
- A bad-query error renders the whole grammar inline.

## 9. Raycast API surface — everything actually used

### View commands

**`List`** — `isLoading`, `isShowingDetail={showDetail && tasks.length > 0}`, `onSelectionChange={setSelectedId}`, `searchBarPlaceholder` (dynamic: `` `Search ${tasks.length} task${…}…` ``), `searchBarAccessory={<GroupDropdown/>}`.
`List.Section` with `title` + `subtitle={String(items.length)}`. `List.EmptyView` with `icon/title/description/actions`. `List.Item` with `id`, `icon`, `title`, `subtitle`, `keywords`, `accessories`, `detail`, `actions`.

**Client-side search via `keywords`** — `src/tasks.tsx:1-10`:
> "Searching is client-side, through per-item `keywords`. The whole state is already in memory and pueue's own query DSL only matches `command` and `label`, so filtering here is both faster and broader."

`statusKeywords(t)` returns id, command, original_command, label, group, path, status kind, result kind, exit code, `"locked editing"` — `.filter(k => k.length > 0)` (asserted: *"keywords drop a null label rather than emitting empty"*).

**Accessories adapt to available width:**
```tsx
const accessories: List.Item.Accessory[] = props.showDetail
  ? [{ tag: { value: statusTag(task), color: statusColor(task) } }]
  : [ …label tag…, …group text…, { text: duration, icon: Icon.Clock }, …status tag… ];
```

**`List.Item.Detail`** with `markdown` + `metadata`: `Metadata.Label`, `Metadata.Separator`, `Metadata.TagList` / `TagList.Item`. Conditional rows via `{cond ? <…/> : null}`.

**`List.Dropdown`** as `searchBarAccessory` — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/group-dropdown.tsx`. Two behaviours the header calls out:
1. Seed with a static fallback list so it *never paints empty on first render* — *"an empty dropdown looks broken."*
2. **"Raycast silently resets a `Dropdown` whose `value` isn't among its children"** — so an unrecognised current value is preserved as a synthetic `<List.Dropdown.Item title={`${value} (gone)`} value={value}/>`. Same trick in the Add Task group dropdown.
3. Sentinel: `export const ALL_GROUPS = " all";` — *"Not a legal pueue group name, so it can't collide."*

**`Detail`** — `isLoading`, `navigationTitle`, `markdown`, `metadata={<Detail.Metadata>…}`, `actions`.

**`Form`** — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/add-task.tsx`. Controls used: `Form.TextArea`, `Form.TextField`, `Form.Dropdown` + `.Item`, `Form.FilePicker` (`canChooseDirectories`, `canChooseFiles={false}`, `allowMultipleSelection={false}` → `value: string[]`), `Form.TagPicker` + `.Item`, `Form.Separator`, `Form.Description`.
- `enableDrafts` on the Form.
- `info=` props carry the domain warnings (e.g. *"A trailing & detaches the process and the task finishes instantly"*).
- Inline validation via `error` + clear-on-change:
  ```tsx
  error={priorityError}
  onChange={(v) => { setPriority(v); if (priorityError) setPriorityError(undefined); }}
  ```
- **One dropdown instead of two checkboxes when the CLI flags are mutually exclusive**: *"`--stashed` and `--immediate` are mutually exclusive, and two checkboxes would let you tick both."*
- **Progressive disclosure**: `showAdvanced` state, `⌘⇧A` toggle, and an `<Form.Description title="More" text="⌘⇧A for dependencies, delay, and priority."/>` placeholder when collapsed.
- **The submit button names its target**: `title={remote ? \`Queue on ${name}\` : "Queue Locally"}` — *"A dropdown further up the form is easy to miss, and 'I queued it on the wrong machine' is a mistake you only notice much later."*
- Post-submit: `pop(); await popToRoot();`

**`ActionPanel`** — `ActionPanel.Section` (with optional `title`), `ActionPanel.Submenu`, `Action`, `Action.Push`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`, `Action.OpenInBrowser`, `Action.ShowInFinder`, `Action.SubmitForm`, `style={Action.Style.Destructive}`.

**Shortcuts** — mixes `Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.*` (`Refresh`, `Copy`, `Open`, `Remove`, `New`, `Duplicate`) with explicit `{ modifiers: ["cmd","shift"], key: "k" }`. Note the README documents `⌘⌥R` for the destructive restart and `⌘⇧R` for the safe one — *"Name the two restarts for what they actually do"* (a whole commit).

**Navigation** — `useNavigation()` → `push`/`pop`; `Action.Push target={<TaskLogView …/>}`.

**Cross-command launch** — `launchCommand({ name, type: LaunchType.UserInitiated | Background, arguments, context })`, always `.catch(() => {})`.

### Menu bar — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/queue-menu.tsx`

The file header is a four-point constraint list that is *the* generic menu-bar lesson:

> 1. **There is no badge API.** The count *is* the title, and `undefined` is what removes it — that's the idiom Homebrew's services-menu uses too.
> 2. **`isLoading` is a contract, not a hint**: leave it unset and Raycast renders then immediately unloads; leave it true and the whole React tree re-runs every tick.
> 3. On restart Raycast **restores the item from its database rather than by re-running the command**, so a stale render can outlive a restart. The "Updated HH:MM" row exists to make that visible instead of misleading.
> 4. **No `confirmAlert`.** It presents in the Raycast window, which is closed when the menu is open — a silently swallowed confirmation on a destructive action is not acceptable, so destructive items live behind ⌥ instead.

Concrete idioms:
- `menuTitle()` returns `string | undefined`; `undefined` hides the title entirely.
- `menuIcon()` — **one monochrome template SVG (`assets/pueue-menubar.svg`, 317 bytes), four `tintColor`s**: `Color.Red` on failure, `Color.Orange` when all paused, `Color.PrimaryText` normally, `Color.SecondaryText` while loading. *"the shape never moves in the menu bar, only its colour."*
- `MenuBarExtra` props: `icon`, `title`, `tooltip`, `isLoading`.
- `MenuBarExtra.Section` (with `title`), `MenuBarExtra.Item` (`title`, `icon`, `onAction`, `alternate`), `MenuBarExtra.Submenu`.
- **A `MenuBarExtra.Item` with no `onAction` is a disabled label** — used for `Updated ${clock(fetchedAt)}` and for the per-task status row.
- **`alternate` is the ⌥ affordance**: the visible item is titled `"Hold ⌥ to Clean Finished Tasks"` and its `alternate={<MenuBarExtra.Item title="Clean Finished Tasks" onAction={…}/>}` does the work.
- **Identical siblings misfire.** *"Every title is prefixed with the id, so no two items at the same level are identical — Raycast warns that identical siblings get their onAction handlers crossed."* → `` title={`${task.id} · ${oneline(task.command, 48)}`} ``
- **Cap the item count**: `perSection = Math.max(1, Number(prefs.maxItemsPerSection) || 7)`, trailing `…and ${hidden} more` that `launchCommand`s the full list. *"A 400-task queue must not become 400 menu items every minute."*
- **Never return `null` on error**: *"Returning null would remove the item entirely, which is the wrong answer for someone who deliberately enabled a pueue menu bar command."* Render `<ErrorMenu/>` instead.
- Feedback is `showHUD`, not a toast (no window).
- `updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle })` on every successful fetch, inside `useCachedPromise`'s `onData` callback, `.catch(() => {})`. *"Only affects this command's own subtitle in root search."*
- The timestamp is stored **in the same cache entry as the data** so the two can't drift:
  ```ts
  export async function snapshot(o?): Promise<Snapshot> { return { state: await status(o), fetchedAt: Date.now() }; }
  ```

### `no-view` command

```ts
export default async function Command(props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.QuickAdd }>) { … }
```
> "`no-view` means there is no window to show a toast in, so feedback is a HUD — `showToast` degrades to one automatically, but calling `showHUD` directly makes that explicit."

Error handling with no window to put instructions in:
```ts
const described = describeError(error);
await showHUD(described.structural ? `${described.shortTitle} — ${detail}` : detail || described.shortTitle);
```

### `launchContext` — passing data between commands

`tasks.tsx` types it inline on `LaunchProps`:
```ts
props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.Tasks; launchContext?: { group?: string; logTaskId?: number; connectionName?: string } }>
```
Two hard-won rules, both marked *"Observed, not theorised"*:
1. **Push only once** — `const pushedLog = useRef(false)`, because *"a re-render on every poll must not stack log views on the navigation stack."*
2. **Wait for dependent async state before acting on context** — *"Setting it is asynchronous, and task ids are per-daemon — pushing early opens whichever daemon was selected before, which looks like it worked and shows someone else's task with the same id."*
   ```ts
   if (contextConnection && conn.connection.name !== contextConnection) return;
   ```
3. **Context wins over remembered state**: *"The Groups view launches this command with a group in its context; that choice must win over the remembered filter, or 'Show Tasks in Group' would silently show a different group."*

### Markdown rendering of program output

`task-log.tsx:38-45`:
> "Program output is not markdown, so it goes in a fence — otherwise a build log full of `#` and `*` renders as headings and bullets. A fence inside the output would close ours early, so the backticks are broken with a zero-width space."

## 10. `pitfalls/` — the format, and every entry

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/README.md` defines the convention:

> "One file per trap, titled by the **symptom** you'd search for — not the root cause, which you don't know yet when you're looking. Each file opens with a "Symptoms (grep this section)" block containing the verbatim error text, so `grep -r` over this directory finds it."

Standard section order: **Symptoms (grep this section) → Cause → Fix → [Guard] → [Note] → Related**.

| File | Symptom / trigger | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| `raycast-launchd-path-pueue-not-found.md` | `spawn pueue ENOENT`, works in terminal | Raycast runs under launchd, no shell rc, PATH ≈ `/usr/bin:/bin` | Never invoke a bare binary; absolute path via preference + 6-dir probe (both Homebrew prefixes). **Test from Raycast, not the dev terminal.** |
| `ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md` | `ready - built extension successfully` on broken types | esbuild strips types without checking | `just check = typecheck verify lint build`; type JSX props as `React.JSX.Element` not `ReactNode` (`@raycast/api` bundles its own `@types/react`) |
| `daemon-state-lags-one-poll-after-a-mutation.md` | optimistic update visibly reverts, then re-applies | backend acks before its update loop applies (~280 ms measured) | `shouldRevalidateAfter: false` + two delayed `revalidate()`s (400 / 1500 ms); delay the menu-bar nudge equally |
| `cached-list-renders-a-dead-queue-as-live.md` | list shows Running tasks after the daemon stopped; `Failed to fetch latest data` | `useCachedPromise` serves last-good on failure — right for flaky, wrong for structural | `structural` flag on the error descriptor → in-list `StaleBannerItem` with a `shortTitle` and a `cached` accessory |
| `pueue-status-enum-is-externally-tagged.md` | `task.status.toLowerCase is not a function`; `"[object Object]"`; dates render `1/1/1970`; every finished task looks successful | serde external tagging; `Locked` recursive; `enqueue_at` vs `enqueued_at`; `new Date(null)` → 1970; `TaskResult` mixes strings and objects | All raw-enum access confined to `normalize.ts`; `underlyingKind`/`parseTs`/`enqueuedAt`/`resultKind`; **failure detection is an allowlist**; unknown tags → `"unknown"`, never throw |
| `pueue-log-json-hides-errors-in-output.md` | a Rust I/O error rendered as if the task printed it | `log --json` exits **0** and puts its own error in the `output` field | Two levels: `hasEverRun()` avoids asking; `cleanLogOutput()` **prefix**-checks `(Pueue error)` (not substring — there's an assertion for a build log containing the phrase mid-stream) |
| `pueue-color-flag-must-precede-subcommand.md` | `error: unexpected argument '--color' found`, exit 2 | global flags are rejected after the subcommand by clap | `[...globalArgs(), ...args]`, prepended. Exit codes are 0/1/**2**. `--color never` doesn't affect `color_eyre` stderr. Guarded by the live `--help` check |
| `remote-task-working-directory-fails-to-spawn.md` | `FailedToSpawn`, `Failed to canonicalize given working directory path` | cwd is canonicalised on whichever machine the *client* runs on; macOS silently rewrites `/tmp`→`/private/tmp` | Run the client on the far side over SSH; POSIX single-quote the whole command for the remote shell; UI refuses to submit when it can't work |

## 11. `backlog/` — decisions frozen with "what would have to be true"

`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/backlog/README.md`: *"Each answers: what, why it isn't done, and what would have to be true to do it."* Every file opens with `**Status:** \`P?\` · **Effort:** \`[M]\` · not started`.

| File | Decision |
|---|---|
| `ai-tools.md` | **AI Extensions (`tools[]`) deferred because they require Raycast Pro** (quoted from developers.raycast.com/ai/getting-started). Tools don't appear in root search; Raycast AI picks them by `description`. Since the transport already returns structured data, *"a tool is a thin wrapper — the work is prompt-shaped, not code-shaped."* **Caution: there is no confirmation surface in an AI tool call comparable to `confirmAlert`, so a first version must be read-only.** |
| `socket-transport.md` | **Don't reimplement the daemon's binary protocol** to save ~28 ms/read. Documents the protocol anyway (unix socket, shared-secret handshake whose reply is the version string, 8-byte BE length framing, CBOR). Kept because the `Mutation` data union makes it a one-file swap. Includes a "don't copy prior art's types, they're incomplete" note. |
| `callback-notifications.md` | **Document the backend's notification hook; never write to the user's config file.** Three reasons the tempting deeplink version isn't shipped, the third being Raycast-generic: *"Raycast prompts for confirmation on deeplinks triggered from outside the app … so a background nudge would pop a dialog every time a task finished."* |
| `store-publishing.md` | Store-ready except screenshots. Contains the full checklist (below), the reviewability argument (soft "avoid additional downloads" vs explicit "✅ Calling known system binaries", with precedents **brew / colima / orbstack / yabai**), and the publishing mechanics: *"`npx @raycast/api@latest publish` authenticates with GitHub and opens a pull request against `raycast/extensions`… This is closer to Homebrew core than to PyPI."* |

## 16. Cross-cutting authoring lessons (the ones I'd put at the top of a skill)

1. **`ray build` ≠ typecheck; `ray lint` ≠ typecheck.** The gate must be `tsc --noEmit && <verify> && ray lint && ray build`.
2. **Never invoke a bare binary name.** Raycast = launchd = no shell rc. Probe absolute paths, `existsSync`-validate the preference, probe both Homebrew prefixes.
3. **The dev terminal lies about PATH.** Any environment-dependent behaviour must be exercised from Raycast root search or the menu bar.
4. **Generate, never hand-write, `Preferences` / `Arguments` types.** A manifest/code drift then becomes a compile error.
5. **Strip anything secret-bearing at the parse boundary**, because `useCachedPromise` persists to a disk-backed `Cache`.
6. **`shouldRevalidateAfter: false` + a *measured* delayed reconcile** whenever the backend acks before it applies. Measure; don't guess. Two reads (fast + settle) beat one pessimistic read.
7. **Optimistic updates must return the input unchanged when the outcome is unknowable.** A wrong prediction flickers exactly like no prediction, but is also wrong.
8. **Cached-on-failure is right for flaky reads and wrong for structural ones.** Classify errors and give structural failures a visible in-list banner with a `shortTitle` short enough for a third-width column.
9. **One `ErrorDescriptor`, N renderers** (`List.EmptyView`, `List.Item`, `Detail`, `MenuBarExtra`). Actions as data, not JSX.
10. **Menu bar:** no badge API (title `undefined` hides it); `isLoading` is a contract; state is restored from a database across restarts so show an "Updated HH:MM"; no `confirmAlert` (use `alternate`/⌥); no two identical sibling items; cap the item count; never return `null` on error.
11. **Dropdowns silently reset when `value` isn't among the children** — always render a synthetic `(gone)` item, and seed a static fallback so the first paint isn't empty.
12. **Pass fetcher dependencies as arguments to `useCachedPromise`,** not closure captures — that's what keys the cache. One `abortable` ref per independent read.
13. **Scope `useCachedState` / `LocalStorage` keys by whatever the value belongs to** (connection, account, workspace). Share a key only when two surfaces must agree.
14. **Keep every pure module free of `@raycast/api`** so a plain `tsc && node` script can assert it. That single constraint is what makes testing possible at all.
15. **Assert generated argv against the wrapped CLI's own `--help` at verify time.**
16. **Model mutations as a data union, not argv strings** — it's what makes the transport a seam rather than a shell.
17. **Type JSX-holding props as `React.JSX.Element`, not `React.ReactNode`.**
18. **`⌘K` and `⌘P` are reserved** and are silently ignored if you bind them (only `ray lint` catches this).
19. **Fence untrusted text in markdown and neutralise embedded backticks** with a zero-width space.
20. **Confirmations must state what the verb doesn't say** — every destructive confirmation here quotes behaviour verified from `--help` (`kill --group` also pauses; `group remove` moves tasks to default; `restart --in-place` overwrites the log).
