Guard against being handed the wrong shape\n\nTwo commands return *different* top-level shapes (`status --json` → `{tasks, groups}`; `group --json` → the inner map). `readState` explicitly guards:\n```ts\nif (!raw || typeof raw !== \"object\" || !(\"tasks\" in raw))\n  throw new PueueError(\"command-failed\", \"Unexpected `pueue status --json` payload\");\n```\nand `readGroups` unwraps forward-compatibly: `parsed && \"groups\" in parsed ? parsed.groups : parsed`.\n\n### 6i. Streaming: `spawn` + a cancel closure\n\n```ts\nfollowLog(id, lines, h: FollowHandlers): () => void {\n  const child = spawn(bin, argv, { env: baseEnv() });\n  child.stdout?.setEncoding(\"utf8\");\n  child.stdout?.on(\"data\", (d: string) => h.onData(d));\n  child.stderr?.on(\"data\", (d: string) => (stderr += d));\n  child.on(\"error\", (e) => h.onError(e));\n  child.on(\"close\", (code) => {\n    // exiting by itself is completion, not failure. Only non-zero is an error.\n    if (code && code !== 0) h.onError(fromExecError({ code, stderr }, [bin, ...argv]));\n    h.onDone(code);\n  });\n  return () => { if (!child.killed) child.kill(\"SIGTERM\"); };\n}\n```\n\nConsumer discipline in `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/task-log.tsx:166-236`:\n- `const FLUSH_MS = 200` — accumulate into a `useRef` and flush on an interval, because *\"a render per chunk would be four re-renders a second for no benefit.\"*\n- `const MAX_BUFFER_CHARS = 200_000` — trim the head with `\"…earlier output trimmed…\\n\" + buffer.slice(-MAX)`.\n- The `useEffect` cleanup calls `cancel()`: *\"Leaving the view must kill the child, or a spawned `pueue follow` keeps tailing for as long as Raycast lives.\"*\n\n---\n\n## 7. Data fetching, caching, and the optimistic-update pitfall\n\n### 7a. The single most transferable runtime lesson\n\n**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/daemon-state-lags-one-poll-after-a-mutation.md`**\n\nSymptom: *\"kill a task → the row shows Killed → snaps back to Running → becomes Killed again a second later.\"*\n\nCause: **the backend acknowledges a request before its own update loop applies it**, and `useCachedPromise`'s `mutate()` **revalidates immediately on success by default**, so the follow-up read returns pre-change state and overwrites the optimistic update.\n\n*Measured, not guessed* — five trials: `min 278 ms   median 284 ms   max 297 ms`, while the ack itself returns in ~22 ms.\n\nFix — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/actions.tsx:133-148`:\n```ts\nawait state.mutate(runMutation(mutation, { connection: options.connection }), {\n  optimisticUpdate: (data) => optimistic(data, mutation),\n  rollbackOnError: true,\n  shouldRevalidateAfter: false,      // the load-bearing line\n});\nsetTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);   // 400\nsetTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_SETTLE_MS);  // 1500\n```\n> \"Two reads rather than one pessimistic read: 400 ms clears the measured worst case and keeps actions feeling immediate, and 1500 ms covers a loaded daemon so a mis-tuned first delay never becomes visible.\"\n\nAnd the menu-bar nudge is delayed by the same 400 ms, *\"or a `launchCommand` fired immediately would have the menu bar re-read exactly the stale state we just worked around.\"*\n\n### 7b. Optimistic updaters must refuse to guess\n\n`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/optimistic.ts` — *\"Pure and total: no I/O, no React, and never throws.\"*\n\n> \"A mutation whose outcome cannot be predicted (a new task id, a queue reordering) returns the state unchanged rather than guessing — **a wrong prediction is worse than none**, because it flickers too.\"\n\nThree unpredicted cases, each with a reason: starting a *queued* task needs the scheduler; a non-in-place restart mints an id only the daemon knows; `add` likewise. Asserted:\n```ts\ncheck(\"starting a queued task is NOT predicted — a free slot needs the scheduler\", …, \"queued\");\ncheck(\"a fresh restart is NOT predicted — the new id is unknowable\", kinds(after), kinds(state));\ncheck(\"the input state is never mutated in place\", …, true);\n```\n\n### 7c. `act<T>()` is generic because different views cache different shapes\n\n```ts\nexport async function act<T>(\n  mutation: Mutation,\n  state: { mutate: MutatePromise<T | undefined>; revalidate: () => void },\n  options: ActOptions,\n  optimistic: (data: T | undefined, m: Mutation) => T | undefined,\n): Promise<boolean>\nexport const actOnTasks  = (…) => act(m, state, o, applyMutation);       // State\nexport const actOnGroups = (…) => act(m, state, o, applyGroupMutation);  // GroupMap\n```\n(The non-generic version of this is exactly the bug `ray build` shipped — see §3.)\n\n`ActOptions` is a nice reusable shape: `{ verb: \"Killing task 4\" /* present continuous → toast title */, done: \"Killed task 4\" /* past tense */, confirm?: { title, message?, actionTitle?, destructive?, rememberChoice? }, connection? }`.\n\nConfirmation flow:\n```ts\nif (options.confirm && prefs.confirmDestructive) {\n  const ok = await confirmAlert({\n    title, message,\n    rememberUserChoice: options.confirm.rememberChoice,   // \"Do not show this message again\"\n    primaryAction: { title: actionTitle ?? verb,\n                     style: destructive ? Alert.ActionStyle.Destructive : Alert.ActionStyle.Default },\n  });\n  if (!ok) return false;\n}\nconst toast = await showToast({ style: Toast.Style.Animated, title: options.verb });\n… toast.style = Toast.Style.Success; toast.title = options.done;\n… catch → await showFailureToast(error, { title: options.verb, message: firstLine(error.detail) });\n```\nNote `rememberChoice` is deliberately omitted on `reset`: *\"No rememberChoice: this one should ask every time.\"* And on failure it surfaces the CLI's own prose: *\"pueue refuses some things outright — removing a running task, for one. Its prose is better than anything we'd write, so show it.\"*\n\n### 7d. `useCachedPromise` argument keying and abort controllers\n\nFrom `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/tasks.tsx:135-183`:\n\n```ts\n// Separate controllers: a superseded state read must not cancel an in-flight\n// group read, and vice versa.\nconst stateAbort  = useRef<AbortController>(null);\nconst groupsAbort = useRef<AbortController>(null);\n\nconst state = useCachedPromise(\n  // The connection is an argument rather than a closure capture so that\n  // useCachedPromise keys its cache on it — switching daemons must not show\n  // the previous one's tasks.\n  (g: string, q: string, connectionName: string) => readStatus({ …, signal: stateAbort.current?.signal, … }),\n  [group, query, conn.connection.name],\n  { keepPreviousData: true, abortable: stateAbort },\n);\n```\n\n- **Pass everything the fetcher depends on as an *argument*, not a closure capture** — that's what keys the cache.\n- **One `abortable` ref per independent read.**\n- Conditional fetching with `execute`, and `keepPreviousData: false` when the value is per-selection:\n  ```ts\n  const preview = useCachedPromise(async (id, connectionName) => { … },\n    [selectedId, conn.connection.name],\n    { execute: showDetail && canHaveLog, keepPreviousData: false });\n  ```\n  *\"Only the selected row, and only when the pane is open — one `pueue log` per selection change is fine, one per row would not be.\"*\n- **Don't ask at all when you know the answer**: `hasEverRun(task)` gates the call, *\"which also saves a subprocess spawn per selection change.\"*\n\n`useCachedState` for UI state that should survive relaunch, **keyed by scope**:\n```ts\nconst [group, setGroup] = useCachedState(`tasks.group:${conn.connection.name}`, …);\nconst [showDetail, setShowDetail] = useCachedState(\"tasks.showDetail\", prefs.showDetail);\nconst [connectionName, setConnectionName] = useCachedState(\"connection.name\", LOCAL_CONNECTION_NAME);\n```\nThe comment on the first is a good general lesson:\n> \"a single shared key meant switching to another machine left the list filtered by a group that only exists elsewhere, showing nothing. Observed. Scoping the key makes the mistake unrepresentable instead of merely corrected.\"\n\nNote `\"connection.name\"` is shared *deliberately* between the menu bar and the view commands so they never disagree.\n\n`LocalStorage` (async, non-cache) for last-used form values, also scoped:\n```ts\nconst lastGroupKey = (connection: string) => `add.group:${connection}`;\nconst lastCwdKey   = (connection: string) => `add.cwd:${connection}`;\nawait LocalStorage.setItem(lastGroupKey(connectionName), group);\nawait LocalStorage.getItem<string>(lastCwdKey(connectionName));\n```\n**`useCachedState` vs `LocalStorage`**: cached state for view state read synchronously during render; `LocalStorage` for values a *different command* must read (`quick-add.tsx` reads `add.group:Local` written by `add-task.tsx`).\n\n### 7e. Cached data that has become a lie\n\n**`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/cached-list-renders-a-dead-queue-as-live.md`**\n\n> \"`useCachedPromise` keeps serving its last successful result when a fetch fails. That is the right default for a flaky read; it is the wrong default when the failure is *structural*, because then the cached data isn't a moment stale — it is a snapshot of a queue nobody can see any more.\"\n\nFound by *actually running `brew services stop pueue` and looking*, not by reading code.\n\nThree-tier error rendering, driven by one `ErrorDescriptor.structural` flag:\n\n| Situation | Render |\n|---|---|\n| failed **first** read (no data at all) | `<List><ErrorEmptyView …/></List>` — the whole screen |\n| structural failure **with** cached data | a `StaleBannerItem` row at the top of the list, same recovery actions |\n| transient failure | the ordinary Raycast toast |\n\n```tsx\nconst stale = error !== undefined && describeError(error, conn.connection).structural;\n{stale ? <List.Section title=\"Connection\"><StaleBannerItem …/></List.Section> : null}\n```\n\n**Sizing sub-lesson** — hence `ErrorDescriptor.shortTitle`:\n> \"With the detail pane open the list column is about a third of the window, and the full titles truncated to nonsense: `Pueu...  Showing...  Not...ected`\"\n\n---\n\n## 8. Error/onboarding states: one descriptor, three renderers\n\n`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/error-states.tsx` — 393 lines, and the header states the motivating anti-pattern:\n\n> \"The reference extension this is modelled on grew two copies of an `errorMarkdown()` helper that drifted apart; one descriptor with three renderers avoids that. The menu bar needs the same information but cannot render a `List.EmptyView`, so it consumes `describeError()` directly.\"\n\n```ts\nexport interface ErrorDescriptor {\n  icon: Image.ImageLike;\n  title: string;\n  shortTitle: string;      // a few words, for the narrow list column\n  description: string;     // one line, for List.EmptyView\n  markdown: string;        // a full page, for Detail\n  actions: ErrorAction[];  // declarative: { id, title, icon, copy? | url? | run? }\n  structural: boolean;\n}\nexport function describeError(error: unknown, connection?): ErrorDescriptor\n```\n\nRenderers: `ErrorEmptyView` (*\"Must be rendered inside a `<List>` — `List.EmptyView` is not standalone\"*), `StaleBannerItem` (a `List.Item`), `ErrorDetail` (a `Detail`), and `ErrorMenu` in `queue-menu.tsx` (a red-X `MenuBarExtra`).\n\nThe action list is **data**, so each renderer maps it to its own primitive:\n```tsx\na.copy !== undefined ? <Action.CopyToClipboard content={a.copy}/>\n: a.url !== undefined ? <Action.OpenInBrowser url={a.url}/>\n: <Action onAction={() => a.run?.()}/>\n// and in the menu bar: onAction={() => { if (a.copy) Clipboard.copy(a.copy); else if (a.url) open(a.url); else a.run?.(); }}\n```\n\nOnboarding content patterns worth copying:\n- Copy-to-clipboard actions for the exact install/start commands (`INSTALL_BREW`, `INSTALL_CARGO`, `START_BREW`, `START_MANUAL` are exported consts).\n- `openExtensionPreferences` as an action on every structural error.\n- The markdown fences the raw stderr, with a `fence()` helper that neutralises embedded backticks: `text.replace(/```/g, \"``\\u200b`\")` (zero-width space). Same trick in `task-log.tsx` and `tasks.tsx`.\n- The markdown *explains the two error strings*: `\"Did you start the daemon at least once?\"` = never ran; `\"while connecting to daemon\"` = ran and stopped.\n- Context-sensitivity: *\"Never offer to start a daemon we aren't running. `brew services start` would start the *local* one, which is not the daemon that just failed.\"* → `const brewManaged = !remote && isBrewManagedDaemon();`\n- A bad-query error renders the whole grammar inline.\n\n---\n\n## 9. Raycast API surface — everything actually used\n\n### View commands\n\n**`List`** — `isLoading`, `isShowingDetail={showDetail && tasks.length > 0}`, `onSelectionChange={setSelectedId}`, `searchBarPlaceholder` (dynamic: `` `Search ${tasks.length} task${…}…` ``), `searchBarAccessory={<GroupDropdown/>}`.\n`List.Section` with `title` + `subtitle={String(items.length)}`. `List.EmptyView` with `icon/title/description/actions`. `List.Item` with `id`, `icon`, `title`, `subtitle`, `keywords`, `accessories`, `detail`, `actions`.\n\n**Client-side search via `keywords`** — `src/tasks.tsx:1-10`:\n> \"Searching is client-side, through per-item `keywords`. The whole state is already in memory and pueue's own query DSL only matches `command` and `label`, so filtering here is both faster and broader.\"\n\n`statusKeywords(t)` returns id, command, original_command, label, group, path, status kind, result kind, exit code, `\"locked editing\"` — `.filter(k => k.length > 0)` (asserted: *\"keywords drop a null label rather than emitting empty\"*).\n\n**Accessories adapt to available width:**\n```tsx\nconst accessories: List.Item.Accessory[] = props.showDetail\n  ? [{ tag: { value: statusTag(task), color: statusColor(task) } }]\n  : [ …label tag…, …group text…, { text: duration, icon: Icon.Clock }, …status tag… ];\n```\n\n**`List.Item.Detail`** with `markdown` + `metadata`: `Metadata.Label`, `Metadata.Separator`, `Metadata.TagList` / `TagList.Item`. Conditional rows via `{cond ? <…/> : null}`.\n\n**`List.Dropdown`** as `searchBarAccessory` — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/lib/group-dropdown.tsx`. Two behaviours the header calls out:\n1. Seed with a static fallback list so it *never paints empty on first render* — *\"an empty dropdown looks broken.\"*\n2. **\"Raycast silently resets a `Dropdown` whose `value` isn't among its children\"** — so an unrecognised current value is preserved as a synthetic `<List.Dropdown.Item title={`${value} (gone)`} value={value}/>`. Same trick in the Add Task group dropdown.\n3. Sentinel: `export const ALL_GROUPS = \" all\";` — *\"Not a legal pueue group name, so it can't collide.\"*\n\n**`Detail`** — `isLoading`, `navigationTitle`, `markdown`, `metadata={<Detail.Metadata>…}`, `actions`.\n\n**`Form`** — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/add-task.tsx`. Controls used: `Form.TextArea`, `Form.TextField`, `Form.Dropdown` + `.Item`, `Form.FilePicker` (`canChooseDirectories`, `canChooseFiles={false}`, `allowMultipleSelection={false}` → `value: string[]`), `Form.TagPicker` + `.Item`, `Form.Separator`, `Form.Description`.\n- `enableDrafts` on the Form.\n- `info=` props carry the domain warnings (e.g. *\"A trailing & detaches the process and the task finishes instantly\"*).\n- Inline validation via `error` + clear-on-change:\n  ```tsx\n  error={priorityError}\n  onChange={(v) => { setPriority(v); if (priorityError) setPriorityError(undefined); }}\n  ```\n- **One dropdown instead of two checkboxes when the CLI flags are mutually exclusive**: *\"`--stashed` and `--immediate` are mutually exclusive, and two checkboxes would let you tick both.\"*\n- **Progressive disclosure**: `showAdvanced` state, `⌘⇧A` toggle, and an `<Form.Description title=\"More\" text=\"⌘⇧A for dependencies, delay, and priority.\"/>` placeholder when collapsed.\n- **The submit button names its target**: `title={remote ? \\`Queue on ${name}\\` : \"Queue Locally\"}` — *\"A dropdown further up the form is easy to miss, and 'I queued it on the wrong machine' is a mistake you only notice much later.\"*\n- Post-submit: `pop(); await popToRoot();`\n\n**`ActionPanel`** — `ActionPanel.Section` (with optional `title`), `ActionPanel.Submenu`, `Action`, `Action.Push`, `Action.CopyToClipboard`, `Action.OpenInBrowser`, `Action.ShowInFinder`, `Action.SubmitForm`, `style={Action.Style.Destructive}`.\n\n**Shortcuts** — mixes `Keyboard.Shortcut.Common.*` (`Refresh`, `Copy`, `Open`, `Remove`, `New`, `Duplicate`) with explicit `{ modifiers: [\"cmd\",\"shift\"], key: \"k\" }`. Note the README documents `⌘⌥R` for the destructive restart and `⌘⇧R` for the safe one — *\"Name the two restarts for what they actually do\"* (a whole commit).\n\n**Navigation** — `useNavigation()` → `push`/`pop`; `Action.Push target={<TaskLogView …/>}`.\n\n**Cross-command launch** — `launchCommand({ name, type: LaunchType.UserInitiated | Background, arguments, context })`, always `.catch(() => {})`.\n\n### Menu bar — `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/src/queue-menu.tsx`\n\nThe file header is a four-point constraint list that is *the* generic menu-bar lesson:\n\n> 1. **There is no badge API.** The count *is* the title, and `undefined` is what removes it — that's the idiom Homebrew's services-menu uses too.\n> 2. **`isLoading` is a contract, not a hint**: leave it unset and Raycast renders then immediately unloads; leave it true and the whole React tree re-runs every tick.\n> 3. On restart Raycast **restores the item from its database rather than by re-running the command**, so a stale render can outlive a restart. The \"Updated HH:MM\" row exists to make that visible instead of misleading.\n> 4. **No `confirmAlert`.** It presents in the Raycast window, which is closed when the menu is open — a silently swallowed confirmation on a destructive action is not acceptable, so destructive items live behind ⌥ instead.\n\nConcrete idioms:\n- `menuTitle()` returns `string | undefined`; `undefined` hides the title entirely.\n- `menuIcon()` — **one monochrome template SVG (`assets/pueue-menubar.svg`, 317 bytes), four `tintColor`s**: `Color.Red` on failure, `Color.Orange` when all paused, `Color.PrimaryText` normally, `Color.SecondaryText` while loading. *\"the shape never moves in the menu bar, only its colour.\"*\n- `MenuBarExtra` props: `icon`, `title`, `tooltip`, `isLoading`.\n- `MenuBarExtra.Section` (with `title`), `MenuBarExtra.Item` (`title`, `icon`, `onAction`, `alternate`), `MenuBarExtra.Submenu`.\n- **A `MenuBarExtra.Item` with no `onAction` is a disabled label** — used for `Updated ${clock(fetchedAt)}` and for the per-task status row.\n- **`alternate` is the ⌥ affordance**: the visible item is titled `\"Hold ⌥ to Clean Finished Tasks\"` and its `alternate={<MenuBarExtra.Item title=\"Clean Finished Tasks\" onAction={…}/>}` does the work.\n- **Identical siblings misfire.** *\"Every title is prefixed with the id, so no two items at the same level are identical — Raycast warns that identical siblings get their onAction handlers crossed.\"* → `` title={`${task.id} · ${oneline(task.command, 48)}`} ``\n- **Cap the item count**: `perSection = Math.max(1, Number(prefs.maxItemsPerSection) || 7)`, trailing `…and ${hidden} more` that `launchCommand`s the full list. *\"A 400-task queue must not become 400 menu items every minute.\"*\n- **Never return `null` on error**: *\"Returning null would remove the item entirely, which is the wrong answer for someone who deliberately enabled a pueue menu bar command.\"* Render `<ErrorMenu/>` instead.\n- Feedback is `showHUD`, not a toast (no window).\n- `updateCommandMetadata({ subtitle })` on every successful fetch, inside `useCachedPromise`'s `onData` callback, `.catch(() => {})`. *\"Only affects this command's own subtitle in root search.\"*\n- The timestamp is stored **in the same cache entry as the data** so the two can't drift:\n  ```ts\n  export async function snapshot(o?): Promise<Snapshot> { return { state: await status(o), fetchedAt: Date.now() }; }\n  ```\n\n### `no-view` command\n\n```ts\nexport default async function Command(props: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.QuickAdd }>) { … }\n```\n> \"`no-view` means there is no window to show a toast in, so feedback is a HUD — `showToast` degrades to one automatically, but calling `showHUD` directly makes that explicit.\"\n\nError handling with no window to put instructions in:\n```ts\nconst described = describeError(error);\nawait showHUD(described.structural ? `${described.shortTitle} — ${detail}` : detail || described.shortTitle);\n```\n\n### `launchContext` — passing data between commands\n\n`tasks.tsx` types it inline on `LaunchProps`:\n```ts\nprops: LaunchProps<{ arguments: Arguments.Tasks; launchContext?: { group?: string; logTaskId?: number; connectionName?: string } }>\n```\nTwo hard-won rules, both marked *\"Observed, not theorised\"*:\n1. **Push only once** — `const pushedLog = useRef(false)`, because *\"a re-render on every poll must not stack log views on the navigation stack.\"*\n2. **Wait for dependent async state before acting on context** — *\"Setting it is asynchronous, and task ids are per-daemon — pushing early opens whichever daemon was selected before, which looks like it worked and shows someone else's task with the same id.\"*\n   ```ts\n   if (contextConnection && conn.connection.name !== contextConnection) return;\n   ```\n3. **Context wins over remembered state**: *\"The Groups view launches this command with a group in its context; that choice must win over the remembered filter, or 'Show Tasks in Group' would silently show a different group.\"*\n\n### Markdown rendering of program output\n\n`task-log.tsx:38-45`:\n> \"Program output is not markdown, so it goes in a fence — otherwise a build log full of `#` and `*` renders as headings and bullets. A fence inside the output would close ours early, so the backticks are broken with a zero-width space.\"\n\n---\n\n## 10. `pitfalls/` — the format, and every entry\n\n`/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/README.md` defines the convention:\n\n> \"One file per trap, titled by the **symptom** you'd search for — not the root cause, which you don't know yet when you're looking. # systemd-run vs pueue：一次性長任務與 shell job queue 的取捨

## TL;DR

`systemd-run --user`、`pueue`、`nohup`、`tmux` 都能讓 shell command 在背景或斷線後繼續跑；但它們的核心定位不同：

- `systemd-run --user`：把一個命令交給 user systemd 管。偏 OS supervision。
- `pueue`：把命令丟進 daemon-backed queue。偏 shell job queue。
- `nohup` / `disown`：讓一個 shell process 脫離 hangup。偏最低成本 workaround。
- `tmux` / `screen`：保留一個可重新 attach 的 interactive session。偏人工操作環境。

選法：

| 場景 | 建議 |
|---|---|
| 單個長任務，例如 archive、rsync、一次 backfill repair | `systemd-run --user` |
| 一批任務要排隊、限並行、挑失敗重跑 | `pueue` |
| 正式 daily/index/sweep 排程 | systemd `.timer` / `.path` / `.service` |
| 複雜 DAG、跨機器、UI backfill、集中 metadata | Airflow / Dagster / Prefect |
| 臨時 command，不太需要查狀態 | `nohup ... &` 或 `tmux` |

## systemd-run --user

適合把「一次性但重要」的命令交給 systemd：

```bash
systemd-run --user --unit=dongwu-archive-2026-06-30 --collect \
  nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 /tmp/archive-dongwu-through-2026-06-30.sh
```

查狀態：

```bash
systemctl --user status dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service --no-pager
journalctl --user -u dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service -f
```

停止：

```bash
systemctl --user stop dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service
```

常用選項：

| 選項 | 用途 |
|---|---|
| `--user` | 用 user systemd，不需要 root |
| `--unit=name` | 給 transient unit 一個可查的名字 |
| `--collect` | unit 結束後自動卸載 transient unit metadata |
| `--on-active=90m` | 延遲啟動，適合一次性 retry |
| `--setenv=K=V` | 傳環境變數 |
| `nice` / `ionice` | 降低 CPU / IO 優先級 |

### systemd-run 會自己清 log 嗎？

短答案：`--collect` 會清 transient unit，不等於清 journal log。

更精確地說：

- `--collect`：任務結束後，systemd 會卸載這個 transient unit 的 runtime metadata。之後 `systemctl status <unit>` 可能找不到它。
- journal log：仍由 `systemd-journald` 管理，依照 journald retention policy 清理，不是由 `systemd-run --collect` 立即刪除。
- 如果你把 stdout/stderr redirect 到檔案，例如 `>> archive.log 2>&1` 或 `StandardOutput=append:...`，那個檔案不會由 systemd 自動 rotate，需要自己用 logrotate 或手動清。

常見 journal retention 位置：

```bash
/etc/systemd/journald.conf
/etc/systemd/journald.conf.d/*.conf
```

常見設定：

```ini
SystemMaxUse=
RuntimeMaxUse=
MaxRetentionSec=
```

清 journal 的例子：

```bash
# 清到只保留最近 14 天
sudo journalctl --vacuum-time=14d

# 清到總量不超過 5G
sudo journalctl --vacuum-size=5G
```

注意：這是全 journal 層級，不是只清某個 unit。production 上要小心。


## systemctl / journalctl 常用法

以下以 user unit 為主；如果是 system-level unit，把 `--user` 拿掉，通常需要 root / sudo。

### 查 unit 狀態

```bash
# 單一 unit
systemctl --user status dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service --no-pager

# 目前所有 dongwu 相關 unit
systemctl --user list-units 'dongwu*' --all --no-pager

# failed units
systemctl --user --failed --no-pager
```

常見狀態：

| 狀態 | 意義 |
|---|---|
| `active (running)` | 正在跑 |
| `inactive (dead)` | 已結束或沒啟動 |
| `activating (start)` | 正在啟動 / oneshot 還在執行 |
| `failed` | 失敗，需要看 journal |

### 啟動 / 停止 / 重跑

```bash
systemctl --user start my-job.service
systemctl --user stop my-job.service
systemctl --user restart my-job.service

# 看 exit code / 最近狀態
systemctl --user show my-job.service \
  -p ActiveState -p SubState -p Result -p ExecMainStatus -p ExecMainCode
```

### timers / path units

```bash
# timer 列表和下一次觸發時間
systemctl --user list-timers --all --no-pager

# 啟用 timer/path
systemctl --user enable --now dongwu-tick-daily.timer
systemctl --user enable --now dongwu-tick-index.path

# 修改 unit file 後 reload
systemctl --user daemon-reload
```

### 看 journal log

```bash
# 看某 unit 的最近 log
journalctl --user -u dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service -n 100 --no-pager

# follow
journalctl --user -u dongwu-archive-2026-06-30.service -f

# 指定時間
journalctl --user -u dongwu-tick-sweep.service --since '2026-07-01 18:00' --no-pager
journalctl --user -u dongwu-tick-sweep.service --since '2 hours ago' --no-pager

# 只看錯誤級別以上
journalctl --user -u dongwu-tick-sweep.service -p warning..alert --no-pager
```

注意：如果 service 把 stdout/stderr 寫到檔案，例如：

```ini
StandardOutput=append:%h/log/dongwu-tick-daily.log
StandardError=append:%h/log/dongwu-tick-daily.log
```

那主要 log 會在檔案裡，不一定都在 journal 裡。這時要看：

```bash
tail -f ~/log/dongwu-tick-daily.log
```

### user systemd 的持久化

user timer 要在 logout 後仍然能跑，通常需要：

```bash
loginctl enable-linger "$USER"
```

否則 user manager 可能在登出後停止。


## nohup / disown / setsid / tmux

這些是更輕量的選項，適合臨時處理，但 observability 和管理能力比較弱。

### nohup

```bash
nohup ./long-job.sh > long-job.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > long-job.pid
```

優點：

- 幾乎任何 Unix 都有。
- 不需要 daemon、不需要 unit。
```
</details></tool-use>

- 不需要 daemon、不需要 unit。
- 對臨時命令很快。

缺點：

- 沒有 structured status；只能 `ps` / pid file。
- 沒有 restart / dependency / queue。
- log rotation 要自己處理。
- 如果忘了 redirect，會寫到 `nohup.out`。
- process 死掉後不一定容易知道 exit code。

常用查法：

```bash
ps -fp "$(cat long-job.pid)"
tail -f long-job.log
kill "$(cat long-job.pid)"
```

### disown

如果你已經在 shell 裡啟動了 job：

```bash
./long-job.sh > long-job.log 2>&1 &
disown
```

它只是把 job 從 shell job table 移除，避免 shell 退出時送 SIGHUP。適合救急，不適合作為可維護流程。

### setsid

```bash
setsid ./long-job.sh > long-job.log 2>&1 < /dev/null &
```

比 `nohup` 更明確地開新 session，但管理能力仍然和普通 process 差不多。

### tmux / screen

```bash
tmux new -s archive
./archive.sh
# detach: Ctrl-b d
# reattach:
tmux attach -t archive
```

適合：

- 需要 interactive 操作。
- 想回來看 full-screen progress。
- 不是正式 production job。

不適合：

- 要機器自動排程。
- 要可靠 status / alert / restart。
- 要讓別人用標準方式查狀態。

## pueue

`pueue` 是 daemon-backed shell queue。適合很多任務：

```bash
pueue group add archive
pueue parallel 2 --group archive

pueue add --group archive --label archive-2017 -- ./archive-year.sh 2017
pueue add --group archive --label archive-2018 -- ./archive-year.sh 2018
pueue add --group archive --label archive-2019 -- ./archive-year.sh 2019
```

查狀態：

```bash
pueue status
pueue status --json
pueue log 17
```

重跑 / 停止：

```bash
pueue restart --in-place 17
pueue kill 17
pueue remove 17
```

依賴：

```bash
fetch_id=$(pueue add --print-task-id --label fetch -- ./fetch.sh)
pueue add --after "$fetch_id" --label analyze -- ./analyze.sh
```

限制：

- 依賴是 AND-only、success-only。
- 不適合長期 daemon/service。
- 不負責正式 calendar scheduling。
- task history/log 會累積，需要定期 `pueue clean`。

## 對比

| 能力 | systemd-run --user | pueue | nohup/disown | tmux/screen |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 防 SSH 斷線 | 好 | 好 | 可以 | 好 |
| 單個 one-shot 長任務 | 很好 | 可以 | 可以 | 可以 |
| 大量 job queue | 勉強 | 很好 | 不適合 | 不適合 |
| 限制並行數 | 不方便 | 很好，group parallelism | 不適合 | 手動 |
| 延遲一次性 retry | `--on-active=90m` 很好 | `--delay` 可以 | 要自己 sleep | 手動 |
| 固定排程 | systemd timer 很好 | 不主打 | cron 才行 | 不適合 |
| file/output trigger | systemd path 很好 | 不主打 | 不適合 | 不適合 |
| 任務依賴 | 可以但笨重 | `--after` 很方便 | shell script 自己寫 | 手動 |
| 長期服務 | 很好 | 不適合 | 不適合 | 不適合 |
| log retention | journald policy / 自己 redirect | pueue daemon/log cleanup | 自己管 log file | scrollback / 自己 redirect |
| OS 整合 | 很強 | 中等，依賴 pueued | 弱 | 弱 |
| interactive 操作 | 不適合 | 不適合 | 不適合 | 很適合 |

## 建議模式

### 單次大 archive

用 `systemd-run --user`：

```bash
systemd-run --user --unit=dongwu-archive-2026-06-30 --collect \
  nice -n 10 ionice -c2 -n7 /tmp/archive.sh
```

理由：

- 只有一個主要任務。
- 要能用 systemctl/journalctl 查。
- 要降低 IO 優先級。
- 不需要 queue semantics。

### 多個 archive shard

用 `pueue`：

```bash
pueue group add archive
pueue parallel 2 --group archive

for y in 2017 2018 2019 2020 2021 2022 2023 2024 2025 2026; do
  pueue add --group archive --label "archive-$y" -- ./archive-year.sh "$y"
done
```

理由：

- 多個相似任務。
- 想限制同時跑 2 個。
- 失敗可以針對單一 year restart。

### 正式 Dongwu daily pipeline

用 systemd：

- `dongwu-tick-daily.timer`：固定 20:30 first attempt。
- `daily-pipeline.sh`：readiness gate，不 ready 就 `systemd-run --on-active=90m` retry。
- `dongwu-tick-index.path`：daily ready marker 更新後立刻跑 index。
- `dongwu-tick-sweep.timer`：晚間補缺口。
- `dongwu-tick-health.timer`：健康檢查與 Discord alert。

理由：

- package.json: author must be your Raycast username; license = MIT; use latest Raycast API; set platforms appropriately.  
- Use npm for deps and include package-lock.json (CI on Raycast uses npm).  
- Run npm run build locally (distribution build) and npm run lint as desired; open extension in Raycast to validate distribution build.  
- Naming: follow Apple Style Guide / Title Case for extension and command titles/subtitles; be specific and avoid generic names.  
- Icon: provide a 512x512 PNG icon (look good in light/dark); do not use default Raycast icon.  
- If extra setup required, include README at root and place media in a top-level media folder.

The distilled lessons (verify + expand from the files above):
1. `ray build` bundles with esbuild and does NOT typecheck; `ray lint` doesn't either. Gate must be `tsc --noEmit && <verify> && ray lint && ray build`.
2. Raycast runs extensions under launchd with no shell rc — PATH ≈ `/usr/bin:/bin`. Never invoke a bare binary. Probe both Homebrew prefixes. **The dev terminal hides the bug** — must exercise from Raycast root search.
3. Never hand-write `Preferences`/`Arguments` types — `ray build` generates `raycast-env.d.ts` with global `Preferences.<Command>` namespaces; manifest/code drift then becomes a compile error.
4. `useCachedPromise` persists to a disk-backed Cache — strip secrets at the parse boundary or they land on disk in plaintext.
5. Backends that ack before applying: `shouldRevalidateAfter: false` + two *measured* delayed revalidates (400/1500 ms here). Measure, don't guess.
6. Optimistic updaters must return input unchanged when the outcome is unknowable.
7. Cached-on-failure is right for flaky reads, wrong for structural ones → one `ErrorDescriptor` with a `structural` flag, N renderers (List.EmptyView / List.Item stale banner / Detail / MenuBarExtra), actions as data not JSX.
8. Menu bar constraints: no badge API (title `undefined` hides it); `isLoading` is a contract; state restored from a DB across restarts (show "Updated HH:MM"); no `confirmAlert` (use `alternate` = ⌥); no identical sibling items; cap item count; never return `null` on error.
9. Dropdowns silently reset when `value` isn't among children → render a synthetic `(gone)` item; seed a static fallback so first paint isn't empty.
10. Pass fetcher deps as *arguments* to `useCachedPromise` (that's what keys the cache), one `abortable` ref per independent read, `execute` for conditional fetching.
11. Scope `useCachedState`/`LocalStorage` keys by whatever the value belongs to (connection/account/workspace).
12. Keep pure modules free of `@raycast/api` so a plain `tsc && node` script can assert them — there is no test runner in a Raycast extension and adding one is store-review noise. `just verify` compiles one `dev-check.ts` and runs it under node.
13. Assert generated argv against the wrapped CLI's own `--help` at verify time.
14. Model mutations as a **data union**, not argv strings — that's what makes the transport a swappable seam rather than a shell.
15. Type JSX-holding props as `React.JSX.Element`, not `React.ReactNode` (`@raycast/api` bundles its own `@types/react`).
16. `⌘K` and `⌘P` are reserved and silently ignored; only `ray lint` catches this.
17. Fence untrusted program output in markdown, neutralise embedded backticks with a zero-width space.
18. Never `shell: true`; `execFile` + argv array; raise `maxBuffer` (default 1 MB truncates into a JSON parse error); classify stderr into an error taxonomy; global CLI flags must precede the subcommand for clap-based CLIs.
19. The extension IS the repo root (`ray build`/`develop`/`lint` resolve `./package.json`); `ray publish` copies the directory verbatim, so repo noise rides along.
20. Store checklist: registered Raycast username in `author`, MIT license + LICENSE file, categories, `platforms: ["macOS"]` when shipping a menu-bar command, committed `package-lock.json`, 512×512 PNG icon, monochrome template SVG for the menu bar, `CHANGELOG.md` starting `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}`, 3–6 screenshots at **2000×1250** in `metadata/`, `ray lint`+`ray build` clean.
21. `@types/node` must match Raycast's runtime (22), not the local shell's node.
22. AI Extensions (`tools[]`) require Raycast Pro; there is no `confirmAlert` equivalent in an AI tool call, so a first version must be read-only.

1	# Raycast surfaces, as they exist in 2026
2	
3	Why this extension is shaped the way it is. Written after checking the live
4	docs, because the answer to "can Raycast do X" is frequently no in a way that is
5	hard to confirm from search results.
6	
7	## There is no widget API
8	
9	The complete list of extension entry points:
10	
11	| Entry point | Manifest | Notes |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| View command | `"mode": "view"` | pushes a view onto the navigation stack |
14	| No-view command | `"mode": "no-view"` | runs and exits, no UI |
15	| **Menu bar command** | `"mode": "menu-bar"` | returns a `MenuBarExtra`. **macOS only** |
16	| AI tools | `"tools": [...]` | invoked by Raycast AI, **Pro-gated** |
17	| Script commands | separate repo | shell scripts, not TS extensions |
18	
19	That's it. No desktop widget surface, no Notification Center or Control Center
20	extension point, no Live-Activity equivalent, no floating window API. Nothing
21	widget-shaped shipped for extensions in "The New Raycast" (May 2026) or Glaze
22	(July 2026), and the "Widgets & Controls" pages on raycast.com are **iOS only**.
23	
24	**So a `mode: "menu-bar"` command is the only way to show something without
25	opening Raycast**, and that is what `src/queue-menu.tsx` is.
26	
27	## Menu bar constraints
28	
29	### There is no badge API
30	
31	The count *is* the `title`, and `undefined` removes it. Verified live: with
32	nothing running the number disappears and only the glyph remains.
33	
34	```tsx
35	title={running > 0 ? String(running) : undefined}
36	```
37	
38	This is the same idiom Homebrew's `services-menu` uses — the closest structural
39	precedent in the store, and worth reading.
40	
41	### `isLoading` is a contract
42	
43	From the docs, marked "danger": either never set it — in which case Raycast
44	renders and **immediately unloads** — or set it `true` during async work and
45	`false` when done. For a `menu-bar` command the whole React tree re-runs on
46	every tick until it goes false.
47	
48	### `interval` is manifest-only
49	
50	A preference cannot change it. Raycast renders its own refresh-interval control
51	in the command's settings. Brew hardcodes `"interval": "1m"` and ships no
52	interval preference; shipping one would be a lie.
53	
54	The docs contradict themselves on the floor — the background-refresh page says
55	`10s`, the manifest page says `1m`. `1m` is the safe value.
56	
57	Verified live: with three tasks started and **no** trigger from the extension,
58	the menu bar count updated on its own within 75 seconds.
59	
60	### Background refresh is off by default for store installs
61	
62	Until the user runs the command once or enables it in settings, a freshly
63	installed menu bar command shows **nothing**. This is the single most likely
64	"it's broken" report, so it's near the top of the README.
65	
66	### Restart restores from a database, not by re-running
67	
68	A stale render can outlive a Raycast restart, and there are open upstream issues
69	about stuck menu bar icons. The mitigation here is the `Updated HH:MM` row —
70	it makes staleness visible rather than misleading.
71	
72	### `confirmAlert` is unavailable in practice
73	
74	It presents in the Raycast window, which is closed when the menu is open. Rather
75	than risk a silently swallowed confirmation on a destructive action, destructive
76	menu bar items sit behind `⌥` and `Reset` / `Remove Group` aren't offered there
77	at all.
78	
79	### Identical sibling items misfire
80	
81	The docs warn that two identical `MenuBarExtra.Item`s at the same level get
82	their `onAction` handlers crossed. Every task row is prefixed with its id, which
83	makes collisions impossible.
84	
85	## Deeplinks prompt when triggered externally
86	
87	`open "raycast://extensions/<author>/<ext>/<command>"` shows:
88	
89	> **Request to open ‹Command›** — The command was triggered from outside of
90	> Raycast. If you did not do this, please cancel the operation.
91	
92	Per-command trust. It matters for two reasons: it's why an external nudge is a
93	poor substitute for `launchCommand` (see
94	[`../backlog/callback-notifications.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/blob/main/backlog/callback-notifications.md)),
95	and it's why some verification during development needs a real keypress rather
96	than a deeplink.
97	
98	`launchCommand` **from inside** an extension does not prompt, and
99	`LaunchType.Background` is the documented way to force a sibling command's
100	refresh — which is what every mutation does to the menu bar.
101	
102	## Reserved shortcuts
103	
104	`⌘K` (OpenActionPanel) and `⌘P` (OpenSearchBarDropdown) are Raycast's own. Bind
105	them and they are **silently ignored**. `ray lint` catches this; `tsc` does not.
106	
107	## What `ray` actually checks
108	
109	| Command | Checks |
110	| --- | --- |
111	| `ray build` | bundles with esbuild — **does not typecheck** |
112	| `ray lint` | ESLint + Prettier + manifest + icons — does not typecheck |
113	| `tsc --noEmit` | types |
114	
115	All three are needed. See
116	[`../pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/blob/main/pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md).

9	The skills CLI discovers skills by checking `skills/` one level deep for `SKILL.md`, then falls back to recursive search (up to 5 levels). The nested `local/`/`vendor/` structure works because of this fallback behavior — including vendor `series` subdirs (e.g. `skills/vendor/fullstack-nextjs/<name>/SKILL.md` at depth 4).
10	
11	## Commands
12	
13	```bash
14	# Sync all vendored skills from upstream
15	make sync
16	
17	# Check for upstream updates (dry-run)
18	make sync-check
19	
20	# Validate and render the repo backlog board
21	make kanban
22	
23	# Validate skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json (the catalog manifest
24	# that drives the grouped install UI of `npx skills add ...`).
25	make marketplace
26	
27	# YAML-parse every skills/**/SKILL.md frontmatter. A file that fails to parse
28	# is silently skipped by `npx skills add` — run this before publishing.
29	make lint-frontmatter
30	
31	# All publish gates at once (frontmatter + marketplace + TODO format).
32	# Same set as .github/workflows/validate.yml.
33	make validate
34	
35	# Install scripts/git-hooks/pre-push so `git push` runs `make validate` first.
36	make install-hooks
37	
38	# Add a new vendored skill (auto-syncs)
39	./scripts/add-vendor.sh owner/repo/path/to/skill
40	./scripts/add-vendor.sh https://github.com/owner/repo/tree/branch/path/to/skill
41	# Group under a series subdir (skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/)
42	./scripts/add-vendor.sh --series fullstack-nextjs vercel/vercel-plugin/skills/nextjs
43	
44	# Add a structured TODO entry (preferred over editing TODO.md by hand)
45	./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
46	  --title "Title" --description "Description"
47	
48	# Triage backlog/inbox.md (loose captures) into TODO.md
49	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh             # interactive
50	./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh --batch     # only formalize parseable key=value lines
51	
52	# Move an active TODO item to ## Done with the right syntax
53	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<shipped summary>"
54	
55	# Create a new local skill
56	cd skills/local && npx skills@latest init [skill-name]
57	
58	# Docs site (MkDocs Material + llmstxt + copy-to-llm)
59	uv sync --extra docs
60	make docs-serve     # http://127.0.0.1:8000/
61	make docs-build     # produces ./site/
62	```
63	
64	## Vendor System
65	
66	- `vendor.yaml` — manifest of upstream skill sources with `last_sync` tracking (date + commit SHA). Optional per-entry `series:` field groups skills under `skills/vendor/<series>/<name>/`; entries without `series` stay flat at `skills/vendor/<name>/`
67	- `scripts/sync-vendor.sh` — downloads skill files via GitHub API (`gh` + `yq` required); honors the `series` field for nested destinations, and skips any entry carrying a `frozen:` block (see below)
68	- `scripts/add-vendor.sh` — adds entries to `vendor.yaml`, verifies upstream exists, deduplicates; pass `--series <name>` to group into a series subdir
69	
70	Sync uses the git trees API to recursively download skill directories (SKILL.md + references/ etc.) and updates `vendor.yaml` with the latest commit SHA.
71	
72	Active series in this repo:
73	- `fullstack-nextjs` — Next.js + Supabase + shadcn/ui + Tailwind + design/testing skills (9 skills from vercel/vercel-plugin, vercel-labs/agent-skills, supabase/agent-skills, anthropics/skills)
74	
75	### When an upstream skill is renamed or removed
76	
77	Upstream repos reorganize; `make sync` fails hard if a tracked
78	`upstream.path` no longer exists (the download step finds no files).
79	Handle the two cases explicitly in `vendor.yaml`:
80	
81	- **Renamed upstream** — update `name` + `upstream.path` to the new
82	  values, `git mv` the vendored dir, fix that skill's `skills[]` path in
83	  `marketplace.json`, and add a `renamed_from: <old-name>` field so the
84	  history stays greppable. Renaming changes the *downstream* install id:
85	  the `npx skills` CLI has no lockfile, so users who installed the old
86	  name won't auto-map on `npx skills update`.
87	- **Removed upstream** — freeze it with a `frozen:` block (`reason:` +
88	  `since:`). `sync-vendor.sh` then skips the entry in both `make sync`
89	  and `make sync-check` while keeping the last-synced copy and its
90	  `marketplace.json` entry. Don't delete a vendored copy just because
91	  upstream did — unless you also mean to stop shipping it.
92	
93	Live examples in `vendor.yaml`: `diagnosing-bugs` (`renamed_from: diagnose`)
94	and `zoom-out` (`frozen:`), both from the 2026-07-05 mattpocock/skills reorg.
95	
96	## Marketplace Catalog
97	
98	`skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` defines the user-facing plugin
99	groupings shown by `npx skills@latest add daviddwlee84/agent-skills/skills`.
100	Located under `skills/` (not repo root) because the `/skills` subpath in
101	the install command makes the CLI read the manifest from
102	`<repo>/skills/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — see
103	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md)
104	for the full mechanism.
105	
106	When adding a new skill (local or vendored), also append its path to the
107	matching plugin's `skills[]` array in the manifest, or accept that it
108	will fall through to the **Other** group. Run `make marketplace` after
109	editing — the validator catches broken paths, duplicates, and reserved
110	marketplace names. Path format is `./local/<name>` or
111	`./vendor/<name>` (relative to `skills/`, not repo root).
112	
113	**Picker ordering is alphabetical-only.** `npx skills` sorts groups by
114	`plugins[].name` (A→Z) and skills within a group by their `SKILL.md`
115	`name` — the `plugins[]` / `skills[]` array order is ignored. To pin a
116	frequently-used group to the top, prefix its `name` with two digits: this
117	repo pins `01-project-memory`, `02-skill-authoring`, `03-infra-and-docs`,
118	`04-ml-workflow`, `05-notebooks`; the rest stay alphabetical. **These
119	`NN-` prefixes are deliberate — don't strip them.** Full mechanism +
120	within-group caveat in
121	[`docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md`](docs/reference/npx-skills-metadata.md).
122	
123	## SKILL.md Format
124	
125	Each skill is a directory containing a `SKILL.md` with YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) and markdown body with instructions, conventions, and examples. Vendored skills may include `references/` subdirectories.
126	
127	## Local Skill Discovery Symlinks (`.agents/skills/`, `.claude/skills/`)
128	
129	The `.agents/skills/<name>` and `.claude/skills/<name>` entries are
130	**discovery symlinks** that make a skill active in *this* repo's own agent
131	context (Cursor and Claude Code load whatever resolves under those dirs).
132	They are unrelated to distribution — downstream users get skills via
133	`npx skills add ...` + `marketplace.json` regardless of these links.
134	
135	`scripts/new-skill.sh --local` (run by the `skill-author` skill) creates
136	both links automatically. **Only keep them for skills that are genuinely
137	useful while working _on this repo_** — e.g. `skill-author`,
138	`mkdocs-site-bootstrap`. Skills authored here purely for downstream use
139	(e.g. `fastapi-ai-*`, `dvc-ml-workflow`, `mlflow-tracking`) should **not**
140	be symlinked: they would load into every in-repo agent session and just
141	bloat/pollute context without ever being exercised here. The canonical copy
142	under `skills/local/<name>/` is all that's needed for distribution.
143	
144	To author a downstream-only skill without the links, either:
145	
146	```bash
147	# Skip the symlinks at creation time
148	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh --local --no-symlinks <name>
149	
150	# …or remove them afterward
151	rm .agents/skills/<name> .claude/skills/<name>
152	```
153	
154	## Project Memory Workflow
155	
156	### Long-term backlog -> `TODO.md` + `backlog/`
157	
158	When work is explicitly deferred, add it to [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) using the
159	fixed section order `P1`, `P2`, `P3`, `P?`, `Done`.
160	
161	- Active items must use `- [ ] **[Effort] Title** — description`
162	- `P?` items must use `- [ ] **[?/Effort] Title** — description`
163	- Non-trivial research should be linked as `→ [research](backlog/<slug>.md)`
164	
165	`TODO.md` is parsed by [`scripts/todo-kanban.sh`](scripts/todo-kanban.sh), so
166	do not invent alternate headings, nested bullets, or ad hoc checkbox formats.
167	
168	#### Three ways to add a TODO entry (preferred order)
169	
170	1. **Structured CLI — `scripts/add-todo.sh`** (default):
171	
172	   ```bash
173	   ./scripts/add-todo.sh --priority P3 --effort M \
174	     --title "Title" --description "Description"
175	   # add --backlog to also scaffold backlog/<slug>.md
176	   ```
177	
178	   This inserts a canonically-formatted line into the right `## P*` lane
179	   and re-runs the validator. Refuses to write a malformed entry.
180	
181	2. **Quick capture — `backlog/inbox.md`** (when priority/effort unclear):
182	
183	   ```bash
184	   echo "- maybe add docs versioning with mike" >> backlog/inbox.md
185	   ```
186	
187	   When the user asks "sweep the inbox" or "clear inbox.md", run
188	   [`./scripts/sweep-inbox.sh`](scripts/sweep-inbox.sh). It prompts for
189	   priority/effort/title/description per loose line and calls
190	   `add-todo.sh`. Use `--batch` for non-interactive runs that only
191	   formalize lines with parseable `key=value` pairs.
192	
193	3. **Direct edit of `TODO.md`** — fine if the format is fresh in your
194	   head; run `make kanban` (or `./scripts/todo-kanban.sh --validate-only`)
195	   afterwards to catch drift.
196	
197	#### Promote a TODO when implementing it
198	
199	When implementing a TODO item, in the same commit run:
200	
201	```bash
202	./scripts/promote-todo.sh --title "<substring>" --summary "<one-line shipped summary>"
203	```
204	
205	That moves the matched active item into `## Done` with the dated `Done`
206	syntax and re-validates the file. If a `backlog/<slug>.md` exists for the
207	item, also mark it as shipped (don't delete — keep it as historical record).
208	
209	Keep `## Done` as the recent history buffer. Prune it into `CHANGELOG.md` only
210	when it contains items from a previous calendar year or grows past 20 entries.
211	
212	### External skill / MCP / domain catalog -> `docs/catalog/`
213	
214	`docs/catalog/` is the vendoring decision log + external-awareness
215	registry, separate from `Skills` (what we ship) and `Reference` (our
216	own conventions). It has three subareas:
217	
218	- `docs/catalog/domains/` — per-domain hub pages (one per professional
219	  domain: Finance, Quant Research, AI/ML Research, Web & Fullstack,
220	  Knowledge Work, Agent Harness). Each hub aggregates local + vendored
221	  + external skills + MCPs relevant to that domain. New hubs copy
222	  [`docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md`](docs/_snippets/domain-hub-template.md).
223	- `docs/catalog/skill-collections.md` — single curated index of all
224	  upstream skill collections (Anthropic, Vercel, Supabase, marimo,
225	  Warp Oz, Orchestra-Research, etc.) with status per entry. Replaces
226	  the historical `Collections.md` (kept as a stub).
227	- `docs/catalog/mcp/` — MCP wiki, modeled after Karpathy's
228	  [LLM Wiki pattern](docs/reference/llm-wiki-pattern.md). One markdown
229	  file per MCP with required YAML frontmatter
230	  (`name / slug / upstream_url / transport / auth / hosting / domain /
231	  status / license / last_verified`).
232	
233	Every external entry carries a status enum (single source of truth in
234	`docs/_snippets/external-install.md`):
235	
236	| Status | Meaning |
237	|---|---|
238	| `vendored` | In `vendor.yaml` — link to the entry. |
239	| `deferred` | Open `TODO P?` item — link to it. |
240	| `skipped` | Looked at, chose not to vendor — inline reason required. |
241	| `evaluated` | Read but no decision — 1-line note. |
242	| `wishlist` | Surfaced but not yet evaluated — default for fresh discoveries. |
243	
244	Status changes trigger existing scripts:
245	`wishlist → deferred` runs `add-todo.sh`; `deferred → vendored` runs
246	`add-vendor.sh` + optionally `promote-todo.sh`. Full recipe in
247	[`docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md`](docs/workflows/adding-catalog-entries.md).
248	
249	Every published catalog page is bilingual (`*.md` + `*.zh-TW.md`).
250	Snippets and `_template.md` are EN-only by convention.
251	
252	### Past pitfalls -> `pitfalls/`
253	
254	When a debugging session uncovers a non-obvious trap that could realistically be
255	hit again, write `pitfalls/<slug>.md` with:
256	
257	1. The verbatim symptom or error text
258	2. The root cause
259	3. The workaround
260	4. Prevention guidance or the hard invariant that supersedes it
261	
262	Use symptom-first titles so future agents can grep the failure they see, not
263	the explanation they do not know yet.
264
```

5	
6	# Skill Author
7	
8	Helps you write **new agent skills** that follow the best-practices documented at
9	https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/ — without you having to re-read those pages
10	every time. Pairs with `skill-creator` (which handles eval/iterate/optimize loops
11	once a draft exists).
12	
13	## When to use this vs `skill-creator`
14	
15	| Task | Use |
16	|---|---|
17	| "I want to make a new skill for X" | **skill-author** (scaffold + author) |
18	| "Scaffold the SKILL.md / a reference / a script" | **skill-author** |
19	| "Lint this skill draft" | **skill-author** |
20	| "My skill isn't triggering when I want it to" | `skill-creator` (description optimization) |
21	| "Run test cases against my skill, benchmark it" | `skill-creator` (eval loop) |
22	| "Compare two versions of my skill" | `skill-creator` (blind comparison) |
23	
24	If both apply, start here, then hand off to `skill-creator` once the draft is solid.
25	
26	## Workflow
27	
28	### 1. Capture intent (1 minute)
29	
30	Before scaffolding, get four answers — usually just by asking the user:
31	
32	1. **What does it do?** (one sentence)
33	2. **When should it trigger?** (specific user phrases / contexts)
34	3. **What does it output?** (file, command result, plan, prose)
35	4. **Is the output objectively verifiable?** (decides whether `skill-creator` evals are worth the effort later)
36	
37	Write these four down before touching files. They become the seeds for the
38	description, the workflow body, and the future eval set.
39	
40	### 2. Scaffold
41	
42	Use `scripts/new-skill.sh` to produce the directory layout. The script
43	auto-detects **scope** (where to put the skill) and fans out discovery
44	symlinks for non-universal agents so the skill is loadable immediately.
45	
46	```bash
47	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/new-skill.sh <skill-name>
48	```
49	
50	Three scopes (auto-detected; override with `--local` / `--project` / `--global`):
51	
52	| Scope | Canonical dir | Symlinks created |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| **LOCAL** (this publishing repo: vendor.yaml / skills/local/ found walking up) | `<repo>/skills/local/<name>/` (or `skills/vendor/<name>/` with `--vendor`) | `.agents/skills/<name>` + `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../skills/{local,vendor}/<name>` |
55	| **PROJECT** (inside another git repo) | `<repo>/.agents/skills/<name>/` (universal agents — Cursor / Codex / OpenCode / Warp — pick this up directly) | `.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any already-present non-universal agent dir at the repo root) |
56	| **GLOBAL** (no git repo found) | `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` | `~/.claude/skills/<name>` -> `../../.agents/skills/<name>` (+ any detected non-universal agent dir under `$HOME`) |
57	
58	The template's frontmatter has placeholders that lint will reject — this is on
59	purpose so the agent can't forget to fill them in.
60	
61	> **Important**: When the user's intent is ambiguous (they're inside a git repo
62	> but haven't said whether the skill should live with the project or be
63	> available everywhere), **ask** "system-wide (`--global`) or just this
64	> project (`--project`)?" before running the script. The script is
65	> non-interactive — once you've picked a scope, files land and symlinks fan
66	> out without further prompting.
67	
68	After running, the script emits a single JSON object on stdout with
69	`{skill, mode, canonical, symlinks[], next_steps[]}` so you can chain
70	follow-up actions deterministically.
71	
72	### 3. Author the SKILL.md
73	
74	Read `references/authoring-patterns.md` before writing the body. The patterns
75	that matter most:
76	
77	- **Description must be "pushy"** and include concrete trigger contexts. Naive
78	  descriptions cause undertriggering — the #1 failure mode of new skills. Keep
79	  this within the cross-agent budget: 120-500 chars is the preferred range,
80	  501-900 is valid but context-heavy, 901-1024 is valid but close to hard
81	  loader limits, and >1024 is invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned skills.
82	- **Gotchas section** — environment-specific facts that defy reasonable
83	  assumptions. The single highest-value section in most skills.
84	- **Output templates** — agents pattern-match against concrete structures more
85	  reliably than they follow prose descriptions of formats.
86	- **Calibrated specificity** — be prescriptive only where the task is fragile;
87	  give the agent freedom (and explain *why*) where multiple approaches are valid.
88	- **Defaults, not menus** — pick one tool/approach and mention alternatives as
89	  escape hatches.
90	
91	Keep `SKILL.md` under 500 lines. If you blow past that, move detail into
92	`references/<topic>.md` and tell the agent **when** to load it ("Read X if Y
93	happens"), not just that it exists.
94	
95	### 4. Design any scripts
96	
97	Before writing a script, read `references/script-design.md`. Skills script
98	design is meaningfully different from "regular" CLI script design because the
99	caller is an LLM reading your stderr to decide what to do next. The non-obvious
100	requirements:
101	
102	- No interactive prompts, ever (agents run in non-interactive shells)
103	- `--help` is the primary interface documentation — keep it concise but complete
104	- Errors must say *what was expected* and *what to try*, not just *what failed*
105	- Structured stdout (JSON/CSV/TSV), prose diagnostics to stderr — separate them
106	- `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
107	- Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
108	
109	For Python helpers, prefer **PEP 723 inline dependencies** + `uv run` over
110	`requirements.txt` — the script becomes self-contained and the agent doesn't
111	have to set up an environment first.
112	
113	### 5. Lint
114	
115	Run the linter before committing or handing off to `skill-creator`:
116	
117	```bash
118	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/<skill-name>
119	```
120	
121	It checks three things:
122	
123	1. **Frontmatter & length** — `name` and `description` exist; name is
124	   hyphen-case and <=64 chars; description has a "use when" trigger phrase,
125	   respects the 1024-char hard limit, and SKILL.md is under 500 lines.
126	2. **Script hygiene** — every `scripts/*.sh` has a shebang, is executable, and
127	   responds to `--help` (presence of the flag handler, not necessarily a working
128	   script).
129	3. **Reference reachability** — every file in `references/` is mentioned at
130	   least once from `SKILL.md` (no dead reference docs).
131	
132	Fix every error. Warnings are advisory but usually worth addressing.

135	
136	Once lint passes and the skill *looks* right, the next questions are
137	quantitative: does it trigger reliably? does it produce good output? That's
138	`skill-creator` territory. Tell the user: "skill-author got the structure

198	  `skills/local/<name>/SKILL.md` works because of the recursive fallback. Don't
199	  nest skills more than 5 deep or they become invisible.
200	- **`bash 3.2` compatibility** is required for any script that might run on
201	  stock macOS. No `mapfile`, no `${var,,}` lowercasing, no `[[ -v var ]]`.
202	  See `references/script-design.md` for the safe subset.
203	- **`description` is always-on context and has agent-specific hard limits.**
204	  Put concrete trigger phrases in frontmatter, but keep local skills in the
205	  120-500 char preferred range when possible. Treat >1024 chars as invalid:
206	  Codex and Cursor/spec-aligned validators can skip the skill entirely.
207	- **Quote any `description` containing `:`, `#`, or leading punctuation.** An
208	  unquoted YAML plain scalar cannot contain `": "` — `npx skills` fails with
209	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings" and drops the skill
210	  from the picker without a non-zero exit. ` #` is worse: it parses, but YAML
211	  treats the rest as a comment and silently truncates your trigger string.
212	  Single quotes need no escaping except `'` itself. Run
213	  `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` to catch both; see
214	  `pitfalls/skill-description-colon-breaks-yaml-frontmatter.md` in this repo.
215	- **Don't write a skill that wraps something the agent already does well.**
216	  If a stock Claude session handles the task in one turn without help, a skill
217	  adds context-window cost for no gain. Test the no-skill baseline before
218	  investing in authoring.
219	- **Scope auto-detect can surprise you.** `new-skill.sh` walks up looking for
220	  a publishing-repo anchor (`vendor.yaml` / `skills/local/` /
221	  `skills/.claude-plugin/`) *first*, then a `.git`. If you ran it from inside
222	  a clone of this repo while meaning to add a skill to your *other* project,
223	  it'll silently land in `skills/local/`. Pass `--project` or `--global`
224	  explicitly when intent isn't obvious, and prefer asking the user
225	  system-wide-vs-project-wide before running.
226	- **Discovery symlinks must be `../../`-relative**, not repo-root-relative —
227	  POSIX resolves symlink targets relative to the link's own directory. The
228	  script enforces this and verifies each link with `test -e <link>/SKILL.md`;
229	  if you ever hand-create one, see
230	  [`pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md`](../../../pitfalls/symlink-target-relative-to-symlink-not-cwd.md).
231	
232	## When the user is updating an existing skill (not creating new)
233	
234	Same workflow, but skip step 2 (scaffold). Read the existing SKILL.md first,
235	identify which patterns from `references/authoring-patterns.md` are missing or
236	weakly applied, and propose edits one section at a time so the user can sanity
237	check. After edits, run lint, then offer the `skill-creator` handoff for
238	quantitative validation.

1	# Authoring patterns
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/best-practices>. Read this
4	before writing or editing a SKILL.md body.
5	
6	## Table of contents
7	
8	1. [Spending context wisely](#spending-context-wisely)
9	2. [Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility](#cross-agent-frontmatter-compatibility)
10	3. [Calibrating control](#calibrating-control)
11	4. [Gotchas sections](#gotchas-sections)
12	5. [Output templates](#output-templates)
13	6. [Checklists for multi-step workflows](#checklists-for-multi-step-workflows)
14	7. [Validation loops](#validation-loops)
15	8. [Plan-validate-execute](#plan-validate-execute)
16	9. [Bundling reusable scripts](#bundling-reusable-scripts)
17	10. [Quick checklist before commit](#quick-checklist-before-commit)
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Spending context wisely
22	
23	Every token in `SKILL.md` competes with the conversation history, the system
24	prompt, and every other active skill. Spend tokens on what the agent **wouldn't
25	know without you**:
26	
27	- Project-specific conventions (table names, repo layout, internal jargon)
28	- Domain-specific procedures with non-obvious steps
29	- Edge cases the agent will misjudge by default
30	- Specific tools/APIs to prefer (with the *why*, briefly)
31	
32	Don't spend tokens on:
33	
34	- Explaining what well-known things are (PDF, HTTP, REST, JSON)
35	- Generic "best practices" the agent already applies (handle errors, write tests)
36	- Comprehensive option enumerations — give a default and one escape hatch
37	
38	**Test:** for each paragraph, ask "would the agent get this wrong without it?"
39	If no, cut it.
40	
41	### Progressive disclosure
42	
43	Three loading levels:
44	
45	| Level | Loaded | Budget |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| Frontmatter (`name`, `description`) | always | 120-500 chars preferred, 1024 max |
48	| `SKILL.md` body | when skill triggers | <500 lines, <5000 tokens |
49	| `references/*.md`, `assets/*`, `scripts/*` | on demand | unlimited |
50	
51	If `SKILL.md` is creeping past 500 lines, move sections to `references/<topic>.md`
52	and reference them with **load conditions** ("Read X if Y happens"), not just
53	"see X for details". Conditions let the agent load on demand; bare pointers tend
54	to either get ignored or get pre-loaded out of caution.
55	
56	---
57	
58	## Cross-agent frontmatter compatibility
59	
60	Use this as the portable baseline for coding agents that consume Agent Skills:
61	
62	- `name`: required, lowercase letters/digits/hyphens only, no leading/trailing
63	  hyphen, no `--`, <=64 characters.
64	- `description`: required, non-empty string, <=1024 characters. Include both
65	  what the skill does and concrete trigger contexts. Keep the first 60
66	  characters meaningful because `npx skills` truncates picker hints there.
67	- **Quoting**: a YAML plain (unquoted) scalar may not contain `": "`, and ` #`
68	  starts a comment. Long English descriptions hit both constantly
69	  (`"…debug a FastAPI app: choosing def vs async def"`). Wrap such values in
70	  single quotes — the whole skill is otherwise skipped at install time with
71	  "Nested mappings are not allowed in compact mappings", or installs with a
72	  silently truncated description. `scripts/lint-frontmatter.sh` gates this.
73	- Keep `name` and `description` as the only required frontmatter fields for
74	  portability. Agent-specific fields are allowed when needed, but isolate them
75	  intentionally: Cursor uses `disable-model-invocation`, Codex can read
76	  `agents/openai.yaml`, and some vendored skills carry upstream-only metadata.
77	
78	Description budget tiers:
79	
80	| Tier | Length | Meaning |
81	|---|---:|---|
82	| Green | 120-500 chars | Preferred for local skills: enough trigger surface without context bloat |
83	| Yellow | 501-900 chars | Valid, but context-heavy; move details to `SKILL.md` body |
84	| Orange | 901-1024 chars | Valid, but close to hard loader limits |
85	| Red | >1024 chars | Invalid for Codex/Cursor/spec-aligned validators |
86	
87	Agent notes:
88	
89	- **Codex** skips invalid `SKILL.md` files; OpenAI's validator enforces the
90	  64-char name and 1024-char description limits.
91	- **Cursor** managed `create-skill` guidance matches the same 64/1024 limits
92	  and supports `disable-model-invocation` for explicit-only skills.
93	- **Claude Code** uses descriptions for discovery and tolerates additional
94	  frontmatter in practice, but long descriptions still consume always-on
95	  context and are poor picker hints.
96	- **OpenCode** follows the Agent Skills convention and uses descriptions for
97	  invocation; stay within the portable baseline unless a target agent's docs
98	  say otherwise.
99	- **Claude.ai upload** may impose stricter UI limits. Treat that as a separate
100	  packaging target, not the default coding-agent baseline for this repo.
101	
102	---
103	
104	## Calibrating control
105	
106	Match instruction specificity to **task fragility**, not to "we should be thorough".
107	
108	### Be prescriptive when:
109	
110	- The operation is destructive or has side effects
111	- A specific sequence of steps must hold (migration, release, deploy)
112	- An external system requires exact format (API contract, parser input)
113	
114	```markdown
115	## Database migration
116	
117	Run exactly this sequence:
118	
119	    python scripts/migrate.py --verify --backup
120	
121	Do not modify the command or add flags. The `--verify` step seeds an
122	integrity check that later phases depend on.
123	```
124	
125	The trailing sentence is the trick — even when prescriptive, **explain why**.
126	Agents that understand the reason follow it more reliably than agents that just
127	see "DO NOT" in caps.
128	
129	### Give the agent freedom when:
130	
131	- Multiple valid approaches exist
132	- The output is judgment-driven (code review, refactor proposal)
133	- You'd be hand-coding policy if you wrote it all out
134	
135	```markdown
136	## Code review process
137	
138	1. Check database queries for SQL injection (use parameterized queries)
139	2. Verify auth checks on every endpoint
140	3. Look for race conditions in concurrent code paths
141	4. Confirm error messages don't leak internals
142	```
143	
144	Notice: *what to look for*, not *how to look for it*. The agent picks the
145	approach.
146	
147	### Defaults, not menus
148	
149	When several tools could work, pick one default and mention alternatives as
150	escape hatches.
151	
152	```markdown
153	Use pdfplumber for text extraction.
154	
155	For scanned PDFs requiring OCR, fall back to pdf2image with pytesseract.
156	```
157	
158	…not:
159	
160	```markdown
161	You can use pypdf, pdfplumber, PyMuPDF, or pdf2image depending on...
162	```
163	
164	### Procedures over declarations
165	
166	Teach the agent *how* to approach the class of problem, not *what* to produce
167	for one instance.
168	
169	```markdown
170	Bad — only useful for this exact query:
171	  Join `orders` to `customers` on `customer_id`, filter region='EMEA',
172	  sum `amount`.
173	
174	Good — works for any query:
175	  1. Read schema from `references/schema.yaml` to find relevant tables.
176	  2. Join via the `_id` foreign key convention.
177	  3. Apply user-requested filters as WHERE clauses.
178	  4. Aggregate numeric columns and format as a markdown table.
179	```
180	
181	Specifics still belong in the skill (output format templates, "never output
182	PII", tool-specific quirks) — but the *approach* should generalize.
183	
184	---
185	
186	## Gotchas sections
187	
188	Often the single highest-value section in a skill. **Concrete corrections to
189	mistakes the agent will make without being told.** Not generic advice.
190	
191	```markdown
192	## Gotchas
193	
194	- The `users` table uses soft deletes. Queries must include
195	  `WHERE deleted_at IS NULL` or results will include deactivated accounts.
196	- The user ID is `user_id` in the database, `uid` in the auth service, and
197	  `accountId` in the billing API. All three refer to the same value.
198	- The `/health` endpoint returns 200 if the web server is up, even if the
199	  database is down. Use `/ready` to check full service health.
200	```
201	
202	Keep gotchas in `SKILL.md`, not in a separate reference. The whole point is
203	that the agent reads them **before** hitting the situation — by the time it
204	realizes it should load `references/gotchas.md`, the bug has happened.
205	
206	**Iteration tip:** every time you correct the agent during a real run, add the
207	correction here. Most skills' gotchas sections grow over weeks, not get written
208	all at once.
209	
210	---
211	
212	## Output templates
213	
214	Agents pattern-match against concrete structures more reliably than they
215	follow prose descriptions. When the output has a fixed shape, paste the shape:
216	
217	````markdown
218	## Report structure
219	
220	Use this template, adapting sections as needed:
221	
222	```markdown
223	# [Analysis Title]
224	
225	## Executive summary
226	[One paragraph]
227	
228	## Key findings
229	- Finding 1 with supporting data
230	- Finding 2 with supporting data
231	
232	## Recommendations
233	1. Specific actionable recommendation
234	2. Specific actionable recommendation
235	```
236	````
237	
238	Long templates or templates that only apply in some cases should live in
239	`assets/<name>.template` and be loaded on demand from `SKILL.md`.
240	
241	---
242	
243	## Checklists for multi-step workflows
244	
245	Make dependencies and validation gates visible:
246	
247	```markdown
248	## Form processing workflow
249	
250	Progress:
251	- [ ] 1. Analyze the form  → `scripts/analyze_form.py`
252	- [ ] 2. Create field mapping  → edit `fields.json`
253	- [ ] 3. Validate mapping  → `scripts/validate_fields.py`
254	- [ ] 4. Fill the form  → `scripts/fill_form.py`
255	- [ ] 5. Verify output  → `scripts/verify_output.py`
256	```
257	
258	The agent treats the checkboxes as state and won't skip to step 4 without
259	ticking 1-3. Dependency arrows make the wiring explicit.
260	
261	---
262	
263	## Validation loops
264	
265	For tasks where output quality is testable, instruct the agent to validate
266	and re-try, not "do your best and stop":
267	
268	```markdown
269	## Editing workflow
270	
271	1. Make your edits.
272	2. Run validation: `python scripts/validate.py output/`
273	3. If validation fails:
274	   - Read the error message.
275	   - Fix the issues.
276	   - Run validation again.
277	4. Only proceed when validation passes.
278	```
279	
280	The validator can be a script, a reference checklist, or a self-check prompt.
281	The pattern is identical: **do → validate → fix → re-validate → proceed**.
282	
283	---
284	
285	## Plan-validate-execute
286	
287	For batch or destructive operations, force the agent through an intermediate
288	**plan artifact** that gets validated before any side effects happen:
289	
290	```markdown
291	## PDF form filling
292	
293	1. Extract form fields:
294	   `python scripts/analyze_form.py input.pdf`  → `form_fields.json`
295	2. Create `field_values.json` mapping each field name to its intended value.
296	3. Validate:
297	   `python scripts/validate_fields.py form_fields.json field_values.json`
298	   (checks every field exists, types match, required fields present)
299	4. If validation fails, revise `field_values.json` and re-validate.
300	5. Fill the form:
301	   `python scripts/fill_form.py input.pdf field_values.json output.pdf`
302	```
303	
304	The magic is step 3. A validator that catches "field 'signature_date' not
305	found — available: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed" lets the
306	agent self-correct **before** the destructive step 5.
307	
308	This pattern eliminates an entire class of "oops, ran the wrong thing on prod"
309	failures. Use it any time the actual operation is hard to undo.
310	
311	---
312	
313	## Bundling reusable scripts
314	
315	When you iterate on a skill (with `skill-creator`), watch the agent transcripts
316	across test runs. If the agent independently reinvents the same logic each run
317	— building the same chart, parsing the same format, validating the same way —
318	that's a signal to write the script once and bundle it in `scripts/`.
319	
320	Heuristic: if you see the same ~20-line helper appearing in 2+ runs, bundle it.
321	
322	See `references/script-design.md` for **how** to design bundled scripts so an
323	agent can call them reliably.
324	
325	---
326	
327	## Quick checklist before commit
328	
329	Before considering a SKILL.md "done":
330	
331	- [ ] Description includes specific trigger contexts ("use when X, Y, Z"),
332	      not just a one-line summary
333	- [ ] Description is "pushy" but within budget: 120-500 chars preferred,
334	      <=1024 chars required
335	- [ ] First 60 description chars are useful in picker UIs
336	- [ ] Name is hyphen-case and <=64 chars
337	- [ ] SKILL.md is under 500 lines (move overflow into `references/`)
338	- [ ] Every `references/*.md` is mentioned with a load condition, not just
339	      listed at the bottom
340	- [ ] Has a `## Gotchas` section (or an honest reason it's empty)
341	- [ ] Output format, if structured, is shown as a literal template
342	- [ ] Multi-step procedures use checklists with dependencies marked
343	- [ ] Destructive operations go through plan-validate-execute or have
344	      `--dry-run` support
345	- [ ] Bundled scripts are listed under `## Available scripts` with their flags
346	- [ ] No "MUST" / "ALWAYS" / "NEVER" in caps without an accompanying *why*
347
```
