```text
1	# Script design for agent skills
2	
3	Condensed from <https://agentskills.io/skill-creation/using-scripts>. Read this
4	before adding anything to `scripts/` in a skill.
5	
6	The headline difference from "regular" CLI design: **the caller is an LLM that
7	reads your stderr to decide what to do next.** Optimize for that.
8	
9	## Table of contents
10	
11	1. [One-off commands vs bundled scripts](#one-off-commands-vs-bundled-scripts)
12	2. [Pin versions for `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx`](#pin-versions)
13	3. [Self-contained scripts (PEP 723 etc.)](#self-contained-scripts)
14	4. [Agentic CLI design rules](#agentic-cli-design-rules)
15	5. [Error message style](#error-message-style)
16	6. [Structured output](#structured-output)
17	7. [Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes](#idempotency-dry-run-exit-codes)
18	8. [Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)](#bash-32-compatibility-macos)
19	9. [Quick script checklist](#quick-script-checklist)
20	
21	---
22	
23	## One-off commands vs bundled scripts
24	
25	If a published tool already does the job and the invocation is short, **don't
26	bundle a script** — reference the tool directly:
27	
28	```bash
29	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
30	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
31	```
32	
33	Bundle a script when:
34	
35	- The invocation grows past ~3 flags or needs computed arguments.
36	- You need to compose multiple tools.
37	- The logic must be tested independently.
38	- You want to give the agent a stable interface even if the underlying tool
39	  changes.
40	
41	State runtime prerequisites in `SKILL.md` ("Requires Node 18+", "Requires
42	`uv`"). Don't assume the agent's environment.
43	
44	---
45	
46	## Pin versions
47	
48	Unpinned `uvx`, `npx`, `pipx` invocations behave inconsistently as upstreams
49	release new versions. Always pin:
50	
51	```bash
52	# Good
53	uvx ruff@0.8.0 check .
54	npx eslint@9.0.0 --fix .
55	pipx run 'black==24.10.0' .
56	
57	# Bad — silently breaks when upstream ships a breaking change
58	uvx ruff check .
59	npx eslint --fix .
60	```
61	
62	`@latest` is fine **if** the skill explicitly says "tracks upstream latest" and
63	the user understands that.
64	
65	---
66	
67	## Self-contained scripts
68	
69	When a script needs dependencies, prefer **inline declarations** over a
70	sibling `requirements.txt` / `package.json`. The agent can run the script with
71	one command and no setup.
72	
73	### Python — PEP 723
74	
75	```python
76	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
77	# /// script
78	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
79	# dependencies = [
80	#   "beautifulsoup4>=4.12,<5",
81	# ]
82	# ///
83	"""Extract <p class="info"> from an HTML file."""
84	import sys
85	from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
86	
87	with open(sys.argv[1]) as f:
88	    html = f.read()
89	print(BeautifulSoup(html, "html.parser").select_one("p.info").get_text())
90	```
91	
92	Run with `uv run scripts/extract.py file.html`. `uv` creates an isolated
93	environment, installs declared deps, and runs — every time, deterministically.
94	
95	For full reproducibility, `uv lock --script scripts/extract.py` produces
96	`scripts/extract.py.lock`.
97	
98	### Deno
99	
100	```typescript
101	#!/usr/bin/env -S deno run
102	import * as cheerio from "npm:cheerio@1.0.0";
103	// ...
104	```
105	
106	### Bun
107	
108	```typescript
109	#!/usr/bin/env bun
110	import * as cheerio from "cheerio@1.0.0";
111	// ...
112	```
113	
114	If a `node_modules/` exists anywhere up the tree, Bun's auto-install is
115	disabled. Mention this in the skill if relevant.
116	
117	### Ruby
118	
119	```ruby
120	require 'bundler/inline'
121	gemfile do
122	  source 'https://rubygems.org'
123	  gem 'nokogiri', '~> 1.16'
124	end
125	# ...
126	```
127	
128	---
129	
130	## Agentic CLI design rules
131	
132	### No interactive prompts, ever
133	
134	Agents run in non-interactive shells. A script that calls `read`, `input()`,
135	or any TTY prompt **hangs indefinitely**. There is no recovery.
136	
137	```
138	# Bad
139	$ python scripts/deploy.py
140	Target environment: _
141	
142	# Good
143	$ python scripts/deploy.py
144	Error: --env is required. Options: development, staging, production.
145	Usage: python scripts/deploy.py --env staging --tag v1.2.3
146	```
147	
148	Accept all input via flags, env vars, or stdin (non-blocking — check `isatty`).
149	
150	### `--help` is the primary documentation
151	
152	The agent reads `--help` to learn the script. Make it concise but complete:
153	
154	```
155	Usage: scripts/process.py [OPTIONS] INPUT_FILE
156	
157	Process input data and produce a summary report.
158	
159	Options:
160	  --format FORMAT    Output format: json, csv, table (default: json)
161	  --output FILE      Write output to FILE instead of stdout
162	  --verbose          Print progress to stderr
163	  --dry-run          Show what would happen without doing it
164	
165	Examples:
166	  scripts/process.py data.csv
167	  scripts/process.py --format csv --output report.csv data.csv
168	
169	Exit codes:
170	  0  success
171	  1  invalid arguments
172	  2  input file not found
173	  3  processing failed
174	```
175	
176	The exit-codes block matters — the agent uses them to branch retry behavior.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## Error message style
181	
182	When an agent gets an error, the message **directly shapes its next attempt**.
183	Opaque errors waste turns.
184	
185	```
186	# Bad
187	Error: invalid input
188	
189	# Good
190	Error: --format must be one of: json, csv, table.
191	       Received: "xml"
192	```
193	
194	Pattern: **what was wrong + what was expected + what to try.**
195	
196	For "field not found" style errors, include the available alternatives in the
197	message — this lets the agent self-correct without re-querying the system:
198	
199	```
200	Error: Field 'signature_date' not found.
201	       Available fields: customer_name, order_total, signature_date_signed.
202	```
203	
204	---
205	
206	## Structured output
207	
208	Prefer JSON / CSV / TSV / NDJSON over whitespace-aligned columns. Structured
209	output is parseable by both the agent and standard tools (`jq`, `cut`, `awk`).
210	
211	```
212	# Bad
213	NAME          STATUS    CREATED
214	my-service    running   2025-01-15
215	
216	# Good
217	{"name": "my-service", "status": "running", "created": "2025-01-15"}
218	```
219	
220	**Separate data from diagnostics.** Send structured data to stdout; send
221	progress, warnings, debug logs to stderr. The agent can then `jq` stdout
222	cleanly while still seeing diagnostics if it wants.
223	
224	Bash convention:
225	
226	```bash
227	log() { printf '%s\n' "$*" >&2; }   # diagnostics → stderr
228	log "Loading config from $CONFIG"
229	printf '{"status":"ok"}\n'           # data → stdout
230	```
231	
232	---
233	
234	## Idempotency, dry-run, exit codes
235	
236	### Idempotency
237	
238	Agents retry. "Create if not exists" beats "create and fail on duplicate".
239	"Apply migration if not applied" beats "apply migration".
240	
241	### `--dry-run`
242	
243	For destructive or stateful operations, `--dry-run` lets the agent preview
244	and the user confirm. Implement it as a real preview (show what would change),
245	not a no-op:
246	
247	```
248	$ scripts/deploy.sh --dry-run --env staging --tag v1.2.3
249	[dry-run] Would deploy v1.2.3 to staging.
250	[dry-run] Would update 3 services: api, worker, scheduler.
251	[dry-run] Would run post-deploy hook: scripts/healthcheck.sh.
252	```
253	
254	### Exit codes
255	
256	Use distinct codes for distinct failure types. Document them in `--help`.
257	This lets the agent branch retry/recover behavior:
258	
259	| Code | Meaning |
260	|---|---|
261	| 0 | success |
262	| 1 | invalid arguments / usage |
263	| 2 | required input missing or not found |
264	| 3 | external system failure (network, auth, dependency) |
265	| 4 | validation failed |
266	| ≥10 | reserved for skill-specific conditions |
267	
268	### Predictable output size
269	
270	Many agent harnesses truncate tool output past ~10-30K characters. If your
271	script can produce large output:
272	
273	- Default to a summary or a sane limit
274	- Provide `--offset` / `--limit` for pagination
275	- Or require `--output FILE` so the agent has to opt in to stdout
276	
277	---
278	
279	## Bash 3.2 compatibility (macOS)
280	
281	Stock macOS ships bash 3.2. If the script may run on macOS without Homebrew
282	bash, avoid:
283	
284	| Don't use | Use instead |
285	|---|---|
286	| `mapfile -t arr < file` | `while IFS= read -r line; do arr+=("$line"); done < file` |
287	| `${var,,}` (lowercase) | `tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]' <<< "$var"` |
288	| `${var^^}` (uppercase) | `tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]' <<< "$var"` |
289	| `[[ -v VAR ]]` | `[ "${VAR+x}" = "x" ]` |
290	| Associative arrays `declare -A` | indexed array + key parser, or switch to Python |
291	| `wait -n` (wait for any) | `wait` (waits for all) or track PIDs manually |
292	| `&>` redirection | `>file 2>&1` |
293	
294	Lead every script with:
295	
296	```bash
297	#!/usr/bin/env bash
298	set -euo pipefail
299	```
300	
301	`set -u` catches typos in variable names. `set -e` aborts on first error.
302	`set -o pipefail` makes pipelines fail if any stage fails (otherwise only the
303	last stage's exit code matters).
304	
305	If you need bash 4+ features, either:
306	
307	- Switch to Python with PEP 723 (recommended for anything non-trivial).
308	- Add an explicit version check at the top:
309	
310	```bash
311	if (( BASH_VERSINFO[0] < 4 )); then
312	  echo "Error: requires bash >= 4. macOS ships 3.2; install via 'brew install bash'." >&2
313	  exit 1
314	fi
315	```
316	
317	---
318	
319	## Quick script checklist
320	
321	- [ ] Has `#!/usr/bin/env bash` (or equivalent) shebang
322	- [ ] Is `chmod +x`
323	- [ ] Starts with `set -euo pipefail` (bash) or equivalent strict mode
324	- [ ] Responds to `--help` with usage + flags + examples + exit codes
325	- [ ] No interactive prompts; all input via flags / env / stdin
326	- [ ] Errors say *what + expected + try this*
327	- [ ] Data → stdout (structured), diagnostics → stderr
328	- [ ] `--dry-run` for any destructive operation
329	- [ ] Exit codes are distinct and documented
330	- [ ] Pinned versions for any `uvx` / `npx` / `pipx` invocations
331	- [ ] Python helpers use PEP 723 inline deps (not external `requirements.txt`)
332	- [ ] Bash 3.2 compatible if it might run on stock macOS
333	- [ ] Idempotent where possible
334
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	---
2	name: pueue-job-queue
3	description: Drive Nukesor/pueue (https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) for queued, parallel, scheduled, and lightly-DAG'd shell jobs — wraps `pueue add --after`, `pueue status --json`, `pueue log --json`, group-level parallelism, and `pueued` daemon health. Use when the user wants to background long-running shell commands across reboots, queue dozens of jobs with capped parallelism, run a fan-out / fan-in pipeline of shell steps, says "pueue", "pueued", "pueue add", "pueue queue", "pueue group", "task queue for shell", "background this job", or asks how to schedule/parallelize CLI work without a real orchestrator (Airflow/Prefect/Dagster). Good fit for ML sweeps, long-running data pipelines, batched evaluations, scheduled `--delay` jobs, "wait for X then run Y" sequences.
4	---
5	
6	# pueue job queue
7	
8	Pueue is a daemon-backed shell job queue. The daemon (`pueued`) accepts tasks
9	via the `pueue` CLI, runs them across parallelism-capped **groups**, persists
10	state across reboots, and exposes status / logs as JSON. This skill teaches
11	the agent to drive pueue end-to-end: submit single tasks or whole DAGs, cap
12	parallelism per group, block until completion, retrieve logs, and retry.
13	
14	The skill is a **CLI bridge**, not a scheduler. Pueue's `--after` is **AND-only**
15	and **success-only** — that maps cleanly to declarative DAGs and not much
16	beyond. For OR-deps, conditional branching, retry-with-backoff, or distributed
17	scheduling, escalate to a real orchestrator (see "When NOT to use").
18	
19	## When to use
20	
21	- "Run these 30 commands, max 4 at a time" → `pueue group add ml && pueue parallel 4 --group ml` then loop `submit.sh --group ml`.
22	- "Kick off a long training job and let me close my laptop" → `submit.sh -- ./train.sh` (pueue persists across reboots).
23	- "Run task B only after task A finishes successfully" → `submit.sh --after $A_ID -- ./b.sh`.
24	- "Fan out 4 trainings, then evaluate" → `submit-dag.py dag.yaml`.
25	- "Schedule this for tonight" → `submit.sh --delay 6h -- ./nightly.sh`.
26	- "Block until task 17 is done, then tell me what happened" → `wait.py --ids 17`.
27	- The user mentions pueue, pueued, the pueue CLI, or asks about a "task queue for shell jobs".
28	
29	## When NOT to use
30	
31	- **One short shell command** the user wants to run right now. Just run it. Pueue adds daemon overhead for nothing.
32	- **Cross-host *scheduling*** (jobs distributed across N machines) → Airflow / Dagster / Prefect / Slurm. Note this is not the same as driving a *single* remote daemon, which pueue does support — see `references/remote-daemon.md`.
33	- **Conditional / OR / retry-with-backoff dependencies** → real orchestrator. Pueue's `--after` is AND-only and success-only.
34	- **Typed task IO and artifact tracking** (data lineage, cached intermediate outputs) → DVC (`dvc exp run --queue`), Prefect, Airflow.
35	- **Long-running services** (web servers, daemons) → systemd, launchd, supervisord. Pueue is for finite tasks.
36	
37	## Authoritative sources
38	
39	- Repo: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue
40	- Wiki: https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue/wiki
41	- `pueue --help`, `pueue <subcommand> --help`, `man pueue`
42	
43	## Mental model
44	
45	| Concept | What it is | How to interact |
46	|---|---|---|
47	| **Daemon** (`pueued`) | Long-running process holding queue state. Required. | `pueued -d` to start. `pueue shutdown` to stop. |
48	| **Task** | One shell command, identified by integer id. | `pueue add ...`, `pueue status`, `pueue kill`, `pueue remove`. |
49	| **Group** | Named queue with its own parallelism limit. `default` always exists. | `pueue group add <name>`, `pueue parallel N --group <name>`. |
50	| **Dependency** | Task waits for one or more parents to **succeed** before running. | `pueue add --after <id> --after <id> -- <cmd>`. AND-only, success-only. |
51	| **Status** | Tagged enum: `Queued`, `Running`, `Stashed`, `Paused`, `Locked`, `Done`. `Done` carries a `result` (`Success`, `Killed`, `DependencyFailed`, or `{"Failed": <exit_code>}`). | `pueue status --json`. |
52	
53	## Setup quickstart
54	
55	```bash
56	# 1. Verify daemon is healthy. Auto-start if missing.
57	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/check-daemon.sh --start --json | jq
58	
59	# 2. (Optional) Create a group with 4 parallel slots.
60	pueue group add ml
61	pueue parallel 4 --group ml
62	```
63	
64	For per-OS daemon paths and launchd/systemd setup, read
65	`references/daemon-and-config.md`.
66	
67	## Always pass a label
68	
69	`pueue status` shows the **label** column before the command. In a busy
70	queue, scanning labels is the only way to tell `train.py` runs apart at a
71	glance. **Always pass `--label`** when submitting, and bias toward names
72	that distinguish *this* task from its siblings.
73	
74	Convention:
75	
76	- Shape: `<verb>-<subject>-<key>` (≤30 chars). `verb` = action,
77	  `subject` = artifact, `key` = the variable that distinguishes this run.
78	- Encode the discriminator: seed, dataset slice, model variant, date, host.
79	- Don't restate the command — `train.py --seed 1` becomes label
80	  `train-baseline-seed1`, not `python-train-py-seed-1`.
81	- For DAGs, `submit-dag.py --label-prefix <run>-` makes every task labeled
82	  `<run>-<task_name>` so `wait.py --label-prefix <run>-` selects the whole
83	  graph and `pueue clean` can be filtered later.
84	
85	| Good | Bad |
86	|---|---|
87	| `train-baseline-seed1` | `task1` (no metadata) |
88	| `eval-prod-2026q1` | `python eval.py --quarter 2026q1` (restates cmd) |
89	| `fetch-prices-AAPL` | `fetch-data` (multiple identical labels) |
90	| `nightly-featurize` (DAG) | `step-2-of-5` (rename a step → label rots) |
91	
92	## Workflow A — submit one task
93	
94	```bash
95	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
96	  --label train-baseline --group ml \
97	  -- python train.py --seed 1
98	# stdout: {"task_id":17,"label":"train-baseline","group":"ml","after":[],...}
99	# stderr: submitted task 17 (group=ml, label=train-baseline)
100	```
101	
102	Capture the id with `jq -r .task_id`. The script wraps `pueue add
103	--print-task-id` and falls back to a status-by-label lookup if the id parse
104	fails (defensive against future format changes).
105	
106	## Workflow B — batched runs with capped parallelism
107	
108	```bash
109	# One-time: create + size the group
110	pueue group add sweep
111	pueue parallel 4 --group sweep
112	
113	# Loop: submit 30 tasks; pueue runs at most 4 at a time
114	for SEED in $(seq 1 30); do
115	  bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit.sh \
116	    --label "sweep-$SEED" --group sweep \
117	    -- python train.py --seed "$SEED"
118	done
119	
120	# Block until all sweep-* tasks are done
121	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py \
122	  --label-prefix sweep- --group sweep
123	```
124	
125	Group parallelism is the parallelism primitive in pueue — there is no
126	per-task pool. Set it once, submit freely.
127	
128	## Workflow C — fan-out / fan-in DAG
129	
130	For multi-task pipelines with success-only dependencies, write a YAML spec
131	and submit it declaratively. **Prefer `--isolated-group`** — it creates a
132	fresh group sized to the DAG's fan-out width and leaves your other groups
133	(especially `default`) untouched:
134	
135	```bash
136	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/submit-dag.py \
137	  skills/local/pueue-job-queue/assets/dag.example.yaml \
138	  --label-prefix nightly- --isolated-group
139	# stderr: isolated-group: created 'dag-dcda9347' with parallel_tasks=2
140	# stdout: {"tasks":{"fetch":17,...},
141	#          "topo_order":[...],
142	#          "width_per_group":{"dag-dcda9347":2},
143	#          "isolated_group":"dag-dcda9347"}
144	```
145	
146	Each task gets the label `<--label-prefix><task_name>` so you can
147	`wait.py --label-prefix nightly-` later. After the run, clean up with
148	`pueue group remove <name>` (or run `cleanup.sh --remove-empty-groups`).
149	
150	The submitter topo-sorts, validates the graph (cycle detection, unknown
151	references, missing `cmd:`), computes the **DAG width per group** (the
152	minimum `parallel_tasks` needed for fan-out to actually run in parallel),
153	then submits in order — wiring `--after` from the in-flight name→id map.
154	**No partial submits**: validation fails loud before any `pueue add` runs.
155	
156	Three parallelism modes, in order of recommendation:
157	
158	1. **`--isolated-group [NAME]`** (recommended). Fresh group, sized to width,
159	   no side effects on other groups. NAME auto-generates from spec hash if
160	   omitted. Mutually exclusive with `--default-group`.
161	2. **`--auto-parallel`**. Mutates `pueue parallel` on the target group in
162	   place. Use this when the DAG is meant to live in a long-lived shared
163	   group (e.g. `ml`) and that group's parallelism should permanently grow.
164	3. **No flag**. Only warns (in stderr + JSON's `parallelism_warnings`).
165	   Useful in `--dry-run` planning.
166	
167	See `assets/dag.example.yaml` for a 5-task fan-out/fan-in template and
168	`references/dag-patterns.md` for more shapes.
169	
170	## Workflow D — block until tasks reach terminal state
171	
172	```bash
173	# Wait for specific ids
174	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --ids 17,18,19 --timeout-seconds 300
175	
176	# Wait for everything in a group
177	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --group ml
178	
179	# Wait for a label prefix (e.g. all tasks the DAG submitter created)
180	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/wait.py --label-prefix nightly-
181	```
182	
183	Output is a JSON summary on stdout:
184	
185	```json
186	{"summary": {"total": 4, "success": 3, "failed": 1, "killed": 0, "dependency_failed": 0},
187	 "tasks": [{"id": 17, "status": "Done", "result": "Success", "exit_code": 0,
188	            "label": "nightly-fetch", "group": "ml",
189	            "start": "...", "end": "..."}],
190	 "elapsed_seconds": 42.3}
191	```
192	
193	Exit codes: `0` all succeeded, `5` ≥1 task failed/killed/dependency-failed,
194	`6` timeout. The agent can branch on exit code instead of parsing JSON.
195	
196	## Workflow E — logs, retry, kill
197	
198	One-line `pueue` calls (full list in `references/cli-cheatsheet.md`):
199	
200	```bash
201	pueue log --json --full 17        # full stdout/stderr as JSON
202	pueue restart --in-place 17       # retry in-place (overwrites old log)
203	pueue kill 17 && pueue remove 17  # kill + drop from queue
204	```
205	
206	For ad-hoc filtering, prefer pueue's built-in QUERY DSL over piping
207	through `jq` — it's faster (server-side filter) and shorter:
208	
209	```bash
210	pueue status --json 'status=Failed order_by end desc first 10'
211	pueue status --json 'label %= sweep-'   # substring match
212	```
213	
214	See `references/json-schema.md` for the QUERY grammar + jq fallbacks.
215	
216	## Workflow F — periodic cleanup
217	
218	Pueue's task list grows unbounded. `pueue status --json` walks the whole
219	table, so a queue with thousands of completed tasks slows down everything
220	that touches status. Run `cleanup.sh` weekly:
221	
222	```bash
223	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/scripts/cleanup.sh \
224	  --successful-only --remove-empty-groups --logs-older-than 30
225	# stdout: {"cleaned_tasks":[...], "removed_groups":["dag-abc12345"],
226	#          "deleted_logs":[...], "kept_running":[...], ...}
227	```
228	
229	`--successful-only` keeps failures around for inspection; drop the flag
230	for a full sweep. Pair with the agent's existing weekly maintenance habit
231	(or `/schedule` an agent to run it).
232	
233	## Available scripts
234	
235	- **`scripts/check-daemon.sh`** — Single-shot daemon health + version + log-dir check, with optional auto-start. Outputs JSON to stdout.
236	  - Flags: `--start`, `--json` (default on), `--help`.
237	  - Exit: `0` healthy, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable, `4` client/daemon version mismatch.
238	- **`scripts/submit.sh`** — Submit ONE task, return clean JSON `{task_id, group, label, after, ...}`. Wraps `pueue add --print-task-id` with defensive id parsing. Auto-creates the group if missing.
239	  - Flags: `--label`, `--group`, `--after` (repeatable), `--immediate`, `--stashed`, `--delay`, `--priority`, `--working-dir`, `--escape`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
240	  - Exit: `0` ok, `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` `pueue add` failed, `4` daemon unreachable.
241	- **`scripts/wait.py`** — Block until selected tasks reach terminal status; emit a JSON summary. Selectors: `--ids`, `--label`, `--label-prefix`, `--group`. Quiet by default — emits only one initial line + state-change events on stderr; pass `--verbose` for per-tick output.
242	  - Flags: `--ids`, `--label` (repeatable), `--label-prefix`, `--group`, `--poll-seconds`, `--timeout-seconds`, `--fail-fast`, `--verbose`, `--help`.
243	  - Exit: `0` all succeeded, `1` arg error, `4` daemon unreachable, `5` ≥1 failed/killed/dependency-failed, `6` timeout.
244	- **`scripts/submit-dag.py`** — Declarative DAG submitter. Reads YAML or JSON (file path or `-` for stdin), topo-sorts, validates, submits with wired `--after`, returns `{name → id, topo_order, width_per_group, isolated_group?}`. Computes DAG fan-out width per group; with `--isolated-group [NAME]` creates a fresh dedicated group sized to the width (preferred — leaves user's other groups untouched). With `--auto-parallel` mutates target groups in place. Without either, only warns.
245	  - Flags: `--format`, `--default-group`, `--label-prefix`, `--dry-run`, `--print-graph`, `--auto-parallel`, `--isolated-group [NAME]`, `--help`.
246	  - Exit: `0` all submitted, `1` schema/cycle/unknown-ref/conflicting flags, `2` pueue not installed, `3` mid-run pueue failure (stdout still emits IDs that DID submit, for cleanup).
247	- **`scripts/cleanup.sh`** — Prune pueue task history, empty groups, and old log files. Wraps `pueue clean` + `pueue group remove` for empty non-default groups + optional log-file mtime pruning. Emits a JSON report. Run weekly to keep `pueue status --json` fast.
248	  - Flags: `--successful-only`, `--group GROUP`, `--remove-empty-groups`, `--logs-older-than N`, `--dry-run`, `--help`.
249	  - Exit: `0` ok (or dry-run), `1` bad args, `2` pueue not installed, `3` daemon unreachable.
250	
251	## Bundled assets
252	
253	- `assets/dag.example.yaml` — 5-task fan-out/fan-in (`fetch → featurize → {train_a, train_b} → evaluate`). Pass it to `submit-dag.py` with `--dry-run` first to see the topo order.
254	- `assets/pueue.yml.example` — Config snippet showing `pause_group_on_failure: true`, `default_parallel_tasks`, and a sample `groups:` block. The header comment names the platform-specific destination paths.
255	
256	## Reference files
257	
258	- `references/cli-cheatsheet.md` — Read **when** the task needs `pueue follow`, `pueue log`, `pueue restart`, `pueue kill`, `pueue clean`, `pueue group/parallel`, `pueue pause/start`, `pueue reset`, `pueue edit`, `pueue env`, or any other un-wrapped `pueue` subcommand. Has a one-line "when to use" for each.
259	- `references/json-schema.md` — Read **when** writing custom `jq` queries against `pueue status --json` or `pueue log --json`, or when a script's JSON parsing surprises you. Documents the observed schema on pueue 4.0.2 with concrete examples for each status variant.
260	- `references/dag-patterns.md` — Read **when** the user asks for shapes beyond fan-out/fan-in (mixed sequential+parallel, diamond, etc.) or hits the AND-only / success-only limitation. Has examples and a "when to escalate to a real orchestrator" decision table.
261	- `references/daemon-and-config.md` — Read **when** setting up `pueued` for the first time, configuring per-OS paths, picking config knobs (`pause_group_on_failure`, `default_parallel_tasks`), or wiring up launchd / systemd-user.
262	- `references/remote-daemon.md` — Read **when** the daemon is on another machine: SSH unix-socket forwarding (recommended, needs no server change), direct TCP + TLS, and the working-directory trap that makes cross-platform remote *submission* impractical. Short version: `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client to read/control.
263	
264	## See also
265	
266	- `long-running-jobs` — pueue is one *implementation* of "let the queue own the
267	  chain" (`--after`) and "block once" (`wait.py`). That skill owns the prior
268	  question: **which** of those an agent should reach for, when a scheduled
269	  check-in is ever justified, and how to record completion durably so a run
270	  survives losing the session. Read it if you are tempted to poll
271	  `pueue status` on a timer.
272	- `slurm-hpc` — the cluster-side equivalent when jobs leave this machine.
273	
274	## Gotchas
275	
276	- **DAG fan-out is gated by `parallel_tasks` per group.** Even when two siblings both depend only on `A` and the DAG allows them to run in parallel, they will *serialize* if their group's `parallel_tasks=1`. Pueue's parallelism primitive is the group, not the dependency graph. `submit-dag.py` warns when DAG width exceeds the group's slots and suggests the exact `pueue parallel N --group G` command; pass `--auto-parallel` to apply it.
277	- **`pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does not preserve quoting.** Pueue joins all `<COMMAND>` args and re-shells. The single-quoted `'sleep 60'` is unwrapped by *your* shell before pueue sees it, then pueue re-splits. Quote the **whole** command as one arg: `pueue add 'sleep 60'` or `submit.sh -- 'bash -c "sleep 60 && echo done"'`.
278	- **`--after` is AND-only and success-only.** Failed parent → dependent's `status.Done.result` becomes `"DependencyFailed"` and it never runs. There is no OR, no run-on-failure, no retry-on-failure. If you need that, you need a real orchestrator.
279	- **Pueue does NOT auto-create groups.** `pueue add --group new_name` exits 1 with `"Group new_name doesn't exists. Use one of these: [...]"`. `submit.sh` calls `pueue group add` first if the group is missing.
280	- **`pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW task id.** The old id stays in history with its result. To retry in-place (reusing the id, overwriting the log), pass `--in-place`. Choose deliberately — agent users often want `--in-place` for "retry this".
281	- **`pause_group_on_failure` is config-only, no CLI flag.** Set it in `pueue.yml`; reload with `pueue reset` or restart `pueued`.
282	- **Logs live in platform-specific dirs**, not your CWD. macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/logs/`. Linux: `~/.local/share/pueue/logs/`. Windows: `%APPDATA%\pueue\logs\`. `pueue log --json --full <id>` reads them for you.
283	- **`pueue wait` returns 0 even if the waited-on tasks failed.** It blocks until terminal, period. To know success/failure, query `pueue status --json` afterward (or use `wait.py`, which does this for you and returns a non-zero exit on failures).
284	- **`pueue remove` requires each id as a separate positional arg** (not a space-joined string from a subshell). Use bash arrays: `IDS=($(...)) && pueue remove "${IDS[@]}"`.
285	- **`pueue clean --successful-only` is a flag, not the default.** Plain `pueue clean` removes ALL finished tasks (including failures, which you may want to keep for debugging). Be deliberate.
286	- **`pueue add --print-task-id` writes the bare integer to stdout.** No JSON, no prose. `submit.sh` parses with a regex that tolerates future format changes; if you bypass `submit.sh`, capture with `ID=$(pueue add --print-task-id ... )` directly.
287	- **A terminal result that isn't `Success` is a failure — don't enumerate the bad ones.** `result` is a tagged enum, and `{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}` is dict-shaped, not the bare string older notes implied. Matching a known-bad list let it fall through as success, so `wait.py` returned `0` for a task that never started. It now allowlists `Success` and fails closed on anything else.
288	- **Driving a remote daemon: the working directory is resolved on the CLIENT.** `pueue add` records and canonicalizes the cwd locally, so submitting to a remote daemon fails three different ways — local cwd sent (task ends `FailedToSpawn`), remote-only path rejected outright (`Failed to canonicalize given working directory path`), or a macOS symlink silently rewritten (`/tmp` → `/private/tmp`). Use `ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit; a forwarded client is for reading and control. See `references/remote-daemon.md`.
289
```
</details></tool-use>

```text
1	# pueue-job-queue
2	
3	Drive [Nukesor/pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) — a daemon-backed
4	shell job queue — for queued, parallel, scheduled, and lightly-DAG'd shell
5	work. The skill is a **CLI bridge**, not a custom scheduler: it wraps
6	`pueue add --after`, `pueue status --json`, and `pueue log --json` so an
7	agent can submit, batch, chain, wait, and retry without losing track of
8	what's running.
9	
10	| Surface | Question it answers |
11	|---|---|
12	| `check-daemon.sh` | "Is `pueued` running, and where do logs live on this OS?" |
13	| `submit.sh` | "Submit one task and give me a parseable `{task_id, label, group, after}`." |
14	| `submit-dag.py` | "Submit this whole fan-out / fan-in pipeline with deps wired — in a fresh isolated group sized to the DAG width." |
15	| `wait.py` | "Block until these tasks finish, then summarize success/failure." |
16	| `cleanup.sh` | "Reclaim disk + status latency: prune old tasks, empty groups, log files." |
17	| [`references/cli-cheatsheet.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/cli-cheatsheet.md) | "What un-wrapped `pueue` subcommand do I reach for?" |
18	| [`references/json-schema.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/json-schema.md) | "What does `pueue status --json` actually look like? What's the QUERY DSL syntax?" |
19	| [`references/dag-patterns.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/dag-patterns.md) | "How do I express fan-out / fan-in / diamond shapes?" |
20	| [`references/daemon-and-config.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/daemon-and-config.md) | "How do I auto-start `pueued` on macOS / Linux?" |
21	| [`references/remote-daemon.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/remote-daemon.md) | "The daemon is on another machine — can I drive it, and should I?" |
22	
23	The skill exists to keep three things out of an agent's way:
24	
25	1. **Bookkeeping** — task ids, dependency wiring, group autocreate, defensive
26	   id parsing of `pueue add --print-task-id`.
27	2. **Schema drift** — `pueue status --json` uses serde tagged enums
28	   (`{"Done": {"result": "Success" | "DependencyFailed" | "Killed" | {"Failed": <int>}}}`).
29	   `wait.py` classifies all variants and returns predictable exit codes
30	   (`0` ok, `5` any failure, `6` timeout).
31	3. **Footguns** — `pueue add -- bash -c 'sleep 60'` does NOT preserve the
32	   inner quote (pueue re-shells); `pueue kill --all` also pauses every
33	   group; `pueue restart` (default) creates a NEW id; `pueue clean`
34	   (default) wipes failures too. The SKILL.md has a 10-item gotcha list
35	   covering each of these.
36	
37	## When the skill triggers
38	
39	- "Run these 30 commands, max 4 at a time" → set group parallelism, loop
40	  `submit.sh --group sweep`.
41	- "Kick off a long training job and let me close my laptop" → `submit.sh
42	  -- ./train.sh` (pueue persists across reboots).
43	- "Run task B only after task A succeeds" → `submit.sh --after $A_ID -- ./b.sh`.
44	- "Fan out 4 trainings, then evaluate" → `submit-dag.py dag.yaml`.
45	- "Schedule this for tonight" → `submit.sh --delay 6h -- ./nightly.sh`.
46	- The user says **pueue / pueued / pueue add / pueue queue / pueue group**
47	  or asks about a "task queue for shell jobs".
48	
49	## When it doesn't
50	
51	- One short shell command — just run it. Pueue adds daemon overhead.
52	- Cross-host scheduling, OR-deps, conditional branching, retry-with-backoff,
53	  typed task IO — escalate to **Airflow / Prefect / Dagster / DVC / Slurm**.
54	  [`references/dag-patterns.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/dag-patterns.md) has a decision table.
55	- Long-running services — that's `systemd` / `launchd`.
56	
57	## Structure
58	
59	```
60	skills/local/pueue-job-queue/
61	├── SKILL.md                                  # ~275 lines
62	├── scripts/
63	│   ├── check-daemon.sh                       # bash; daemon health + auto-start
64	│   ├── submit.sh                             # bash; submit-one wrapper, JSON out, group autocreate
65	│   ├── wait.py                               # PEP 723; block until terminal, state-change events, JSON summary
66	│   ├── submit-dag.py                         # PEP 723 (pyyaml); DAG submitter with --isolated-group / --auto-parallel
67	│   └── cleanup.sh                            # bash; prune tasks + empty groups + old log files
68	├── references/
69	│   ├── cli-cheatsheet.md                     # un-wrapped commands
70	│   ├── json-schema.md                        # observed status --json shape (4.0.2) + QUERY DSL + jq recipes
71	│   ├── dag-patterns.md                       # fan-out / fan-in / diamond + escalation table
72	│   ├── daemon-and-config.md                  # pueued setup per OS, config knobs, log paths
73	│   └── remote-daemon.md                      # SSH socket forwarding, TCP+TLS, the client-resolved-cwd trap
74	├── assets/
75	│   ├── dag.example.yaml                      # 5-task fan-out / fan-in fixture
76	│   └── pueue.yml.example                     # config with `pause_group_on_failure: true`
77	└── tests/
78	    ├── conftest.py                           # isolated pueued fixture, skip if pueue absent
79	    ├── test_submit.py                        # submit.sh paths + dependency failure
80	    ├── test_dag.py                           # topo invariant, cycle/unknown/missing-cmd, isolated-group
81	    ├── test_wait.py                          # success/failure/timeout exit codes
82	    ├── test_contracts.sh                     # bash --help/error-code contract
83	    └── fixtures/simple-dag.yaml              # 4-task diamond
84	```
85	
86	## Always pass a label
87	
88	`pueue status` shows the **label** column before the command. In a busy
89	queue, scanning labels is the only way to tell `train.py` runs apart at a
90	glance. The skill's gotchas section opens with:
91	
92	> Always pass `--label` when submitting, and bias toward names that
93	> distinguish *this* task from its siblings.
94	
95	Convention: `<verb>-<subject>-<key>` (≤30 chars). Encode the discriminator
96	(seed, dataset slice, model variant) — not the command:
97	
98	| Good | Bad |
99	|---|---|
100	| `train-baseline-seed1` | `task1` |
101	| `eval-prod-2026q1` | `python eval.py --quarter 2026q1` |
102	| `nightly-featurize` (DAG) | `step-2-of-5` |
103	
104	`submit-dag.py --label-prefix <run>-` produces `<run>-<task_name>` so
105	`wait.py --label-prefix <run>-` selects the whole graph and `pueue clean`
106	can be filtered later.
107	
108	## Empirical schema
109	
110	Pueue's JSON output isn't formally documented in the wiki. The skill ships
111	the observed shape on **pueue 4.0.2** in [`references/json-schema.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/json-schema.md),
112	including the diagnostic snippet to re-verify on a different major. Key
113	shape:
114	
115	```json
116	{
117	  "tasks": {
118	    "<id>": {
119	      "id": 17,
120	      "label": "train-baseline-seed1",
121	      "group": "ml",
122	      "dependencies": [12, 14],
123	      "status": {
124	        "Done": {
125	          "enqueued_at": "...", "start": "...", "end": "...",
126	          "result": "Success"            // or "DependencyFailed" | "Killed" | {"Failed": 1}
127	        }
128	      }
129	    }
130	  },
131	  "groups": {
132	    "default": {"status": "Running", "parallel_tasks": 1}
133	  }
134	}
135	```
136	
137	`wait.py` classifies every variant; if a future pueue release adds one
138	(say `Suspended`), the test suite catches it before the skill goes silent.
139	
140	## Verification
141	
142	The skill ships **22 pytest cases** that spin up an isolated `pueued`
143	under a tempdir-scoped config — your real queue is never touched — plus a
144	bash exit-code contract test. Both auto-skip if `pueue` / `pueued` aren't
145	on `PATH`. `lint-skill --strict` is clean (0 errors, 0 warnings).
146	
147	```bash
148	uv run --extra dev pytest skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/ -q
149	bash skills/local/pueue-job-queue/tests/test_contracts.sh
150	bash skills/local/skill-author/scripts/lint-skill.sh skills/local/pueue-job-queue --strict
151	```
152	
153	The pytest fixture uses `pueue reset --force` between tests because plain
154	`pueue kill --all` also pauses every group — a non-obvious failure mode
155	worth documenting (see SKILL.md gotchas).
156	
157	## Remote daemons: yes, but submit over SSH
158	
159	Pueue can't schedule *across* hosts, but a local client **can** drive a single
160	remote `pueued` — with full control (`add`, `kill`, `log`, `follow`), not just
161	status. [`references/remote-daemon.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/skills/local/pueue-job-queue/references/remote-daemon.md) covers the setup; the short version is
162	that the recommended path changes nothing on the server:
163	
164	```bash
165	# forward the daemon's own unix socket — no server reconfiguration, no TLS
166	ssh -f -N -L ~/.config/pueue/remote/remote.sock:/run/user/1000/pueue_you.socket myhost
167	pueue -c ~/.config/pueue/remote/client.yml status
168	```
169	
170	Verified end to end with a macOS client (4.0.4) against a Linux daemon (4.0.2).
171	Findings worth knowing before you try it:
172	
173	- **`read_local_logs: false` is mandatory** on the client, or `log` / `follow`
174	  look for the daemon's logs on your own disk and find nothing.
175	- **A version mismatch warns but works** — `Different protocol version detected
176	  '0.30.1'` on every command, then normal behaviour. Filter it from stderr;
177	  stdout JSON stays clean.
178	- **Submitting is the part that doesn't travel.** `pueue add` records the
179	  working directory and canonicalizes it *on the client*, so a remote submit
180	  fails three ways: the local cwd gets sent and the task ends `FailedToSpawn`;
181	  a remote-only path is rejected outright (`Failed to canonicalize given
182	  working directory path`); and on macOS `/tmp` is silently rewritten to
183	  `/private/tmp`. Only a path that exists and resolves identically on both
184	  machines works.
185	
186	So the honest split is **`ssh host 'pueue add ...'` to submit, forwarded client
187	to read and control.**
188	
189	That investigation also surfaced a real bug in this skill, now fixed: pueue's
190	`result` is a tagged enum and `FailedToSpawn` is dict-shaped
191	(`{"FailedToSpawn": "<os error>"}`), but `wait.py` matched against an
192	enumerated list of *bad* variants — so it fell through and **`wait.py` returned
193	exit 0 for a task that never started**. It now allowlists `Success` and fails
194	closed on anything else, which also makes it safe against future pueue
195	variants. See
196	[the pitfall](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/agent-skills/blob/main/pitfalls/pueue-remote-add-fails-to-spawn-on-client-resolved-cwd.md).
197
```

# Tasks shown as Running after the daemon stopped

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
Failed to fetch latest data
Failed to initialize client.
```

The Tasks list keeps showing a plausible queue — tasks marked **Running**, with
durations — while `pueued` is not running at all. The only hint is a one-line
toast at the bottom of the window, which scrolls away.

## Cause

`useCachedPromise` keeps serving its last successful result when a fetch fails.
That is the right default for a flaky read; it is the wrong default when the
failure is *structural*, because then the cached data isn't a moment stale — it
is a snapshot of a queue nobody can see any more.

Found by actually running `brew services stop pueue` and looking, rather than by
reading the code: the list cheerfully rendered a `sleep 300` task as Running
minutes after the process had died.

## Fix

Structural failures — binary missing, daemon unreachable — get a row of their
own at the top of the list, carrying the same recovery actions as the
full-screen view:

```tsx
const stale = error !== undefined && describeError(error).structural;
…
{stale ? (
  <List.Section title="Connection">
    <StaleBannerItem error={error} onRetry={reload} />
  </List.Section>
) : null}
```

Transient failures still use the toast. The full-screen `ErrorEmptyView` is
reserved for a failed *first* read, when there is nothing to show beside it.

## Sizing note

The banner needs its own short title. With the detail pane open the list column
is about a third of the window, and the full titles truncated to nonsense:

```text
Pueu...  Showing...  Not...ected
```

Hence `ErrorDescriptor.shortTitle` — "Daemon not running", plus a `cached`
accessory, and no subtitle.

## Related

The same principle drives the menu bar's `Updated HH:MM` row. Raycast restores a
menu bar item from its database on restart rather than by re-running the
command, so a stale render can outlive a restart with nothing to indicate it.
Showing *when* the data was read turns an invisible problem into a visible one.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/daemon-state-lags-one-poll-after-a-mutation.md
# A killed task flips back to Running, then to Done a moment later

## Symptoms (grep this section)

An action appears to work, undo itself, then work again:

- kill a task → the row shows **Killed** → snaps back to **Running** → becomes
  **Killed** again a second or a minute later
- pause a group → the tag flickers Paused → Running → Paused
- generally: any optimistic update visibly reverting

## Cause

**The pueue daemon acknowledges a request before its own update loop applies
it.** `useCachedPromise`'s `mutate()` revalidates immediately on success by
default, so the follow-up read lands in that window and returns pre-change
state — which overwrites the optimistic update with the truth-as-of-a-moment-ago.

Measured on this machine: kill a running task, then poll `status --json` until
it reports `Done`, five trials.

```text
min 278 ms   median 284 ms   max 297 ms
```

The `kill` call itself returns in ~22 ms. So there is a reliable ~280 ms window
in which the daemon has said yes and still reports the old state.

## Fix

`src/lib/actions.tsx`:

```ts
await state.mutate(runMutation(mutation), {
  optimisticUpdate: (data) => optimistic(data, mutation),
  rollbackOnError: true,
  shouldRevalidateAfter: false,   // the load-bearing line
});

setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_DELAY_MS);   // 400 ms
setTimeout(() => state.revalidate(), RECONCILE_SETTLE_MS);  // 1500 ms
```

Two reads rather than one pessimistic read: 400 ms clears the measured worst
case and keeps actions feeling immediate, and 1500 ms covers a loaded daemon so
a mis-tuned first delay never becomes visible.

The menu bar nudge is delayed by the same 400 ms, for the same reason — a
`launchCommand` fired immediately would have the menu bar re-read exactly the
stale state we just worked around.

## If it flickers anyway

Raise `RECONCILE_DELAY_MS`. Re-measure first rather than guessing; the script
that produced the numbers above is a loop of `pueue add 'sleep 300'`, wait for
Running, `pueue kill`, then poll `status --json` at 20 ms until the status
changes.

## Corollary

`applyMutation` must not predict what it cannot know. Starting a *queued* task
depends on the scheduler finding a free slot; a non-in-place restart mints an id
only the daemon knows; `add` likewise. All three return the state unchanged —
a wrong prediction is worse than none, because it flickers too.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/pueue-color-flag-must-precede-subcommand.md
# `error: unexpected argument '--color' found`, exit code 2

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
error: unexpected argument '--color' found

  tip: to pass '--color' as a value, use '-- --color'

Usage: pueue status [OPTIONS] [QUERY]...
```

Exit code **2**, and the extension reports a generic "Pueue command failed".

## Cause

`--color`, `--config`, `--profile`, and `--verbose` are **global** options on
`pueue`, not per-subcommand ones. Clap rejects them after the subcommand.

```console
$ pueue status --color never --json    # exit 2
$ pueue --color never status --json    # exit 0
```

## Fix

`globalArgs()` in `src/lib/pueue/cli-transport.ts` is prepended, never appended:

```ts
const argv = [...globalArgs(), ...args];
```

## Two things this teaches beyond the flag itself

1. **Exit codes are 0, 1, and 2** — not 0/1 as pueue's own behaviour otherwise
   suggests. `classify()` treats exit 2 with a leading `error:` as
   `bad-arguments`, which is always an extension bug and is surfaced verbatim
   rather than dressed up.
2. `--color never` does **nothing** for stderr. Error reports come from
   `color_eyre`, which writes SGR escapes even to a pipe and ignores both
   `--color` and `NO_COLOR`. The flag is still worth passing because it cleans
   up the prose *stdout* of the mutation commands, which reaches toasts.

## Guard

`just verify` builds argv for all fifteen mutation variants and checks every
long flag it emits against the real `pueue <subcommand> --help`. A flag in the
wrong place, or one that doesn't exist, fails there instead of at runtime.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/pueue-log-json-hides-errors-in-output.md
# A Rust I/O error rendered as if the task had printed it

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
(Pueue error) Failed to get log file handle: I/O error at path
"/Users/you/Library/Application Support/pueue/task_logs/1.log"
while getting log file handle:
No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

…shown in the task's **Output** pane, as though the command had written it.

## Cause

`pueue log <id> --json` does not fail when the log file is missing. It exits
**0** and puts its own error message in the `output` field, where the task's
output belongs:

```console
$ pueue log 1 --json          # task 1 is stashed and has never run
{"1":{"task":{…},"output":"(Pueue error) Failed to get log file handle: …"}}
$ echo $?
0
```

There is no exit code, no separate field, and no `error` key to branch on.

## Fix

Two levels, because either alone is insufficient:

1. **Don't ask.** `hasEverRun(task)` is false when the status carries no `start`,
   so stashed and queued tasks never trigger the call at all. This also saves a
   subprocess spawn per selection change.
2. **Detect it anyway.** `cleanLogOutput()` treats an output beginning with
   `(Pueue error)` as absent. Needed because a log can also be cleaned away
   underneath a task that *did* run, which level 1 doesn't cover.

The UI then distinguishes the two honestly: *"This task hasn't run yet."* versus
*"No output."*

## Note

The detection is a prefix check, not a substring one — a build log that happens
to contain the words "(Pueue error)" mid-stream is still real output, and there
is an assertion for exactly that case.

## Related

`pueue log <unknown-id> --json` is `{}` with exit 0 too. Empty is not an error.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/pueue-status-enum-is-externally-tagged.md
# `task.status` is an object, and `status.Done.result` is sometimes a string

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
task.status.toLowerCase is not a function
Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'result')
status shows "[object Object]"
a stashed task's date renders as 1/1/1970
every finished task looks successful
```

## Cause

pueue **4.0.0 moved task timestamps and results inside the status enum**, and
serialises it with serde's default external tagging. There is no flat
`"status": "Running"` anywhere in v4 — every v3-era example online is wrong.

```jsonc
{"Queued":  {"enqueued_at": "..."}}
{"Running": {"enqueued_at": "...", "start": "..."}}
{"Done":    {"enqueued_at": "...", "start": "...", "end": "...", "result": <TaskResult>}}
{"Locked":  {"previous_status": { /* another TaskStatus */ }}}
{"Stashed": {"enqueue_at": null}}
```

Four separate traps live in that block:

1. **`Locked` is recursive.** It wraps the status the task returns to when the
   edit finishes. Anything that filters on status must unwrap first, or a locked
   running task disappears from the Running section.
2. **`enqueue_at` vs `enqueued_at`.** `Stashed` uses the first — nullable, and
   pointing *forwards* to when the task will be enqueued. Every other variant
   uses the second, pointing backwards. A one-letter typo yields `undefined`
   silently.
3. **`new Date(null)` returns 1970-01-01, not `Invalid Date`.** Combined with
   trap 2, an unguarded parse renders every plain stashed task as 1970.
4. **`TaskResult` mixes bare strings with single-field objects** — `"Success"`
   and `"Killed"` but `{"Failed": 127}` and `{"FailedToSpawn": "..."}`. Reading
   `result` as a string works for exactly half the cases.

## Fix

Nothing outside `src/lib/pueue/normalize.ts` touches the raw enum.
`underlyingKind()` unwraps `Locked`; `parseTs()` guards the null; `enqueuedAt()`
handles the spelling split; `resultKind()` handles both result shapes.

**Failure detection is an allowlist** — anything terminal that isn't `"Success"`:

```ts
export function isFailed(t: Task): boolean {
  const k = resultKind(taskResult(t.status));
  return k !== undefined && k !== "success";
}
```

A denylist of `["Failed", "Killed"]` misses `FailedToSpawn`, `Errored`,
`DependencyFailed`, and whatever pueue adds next.

`statusKind()` returns `"unknown"` rather than throwing on an unrecognised tag,
so a future pueue degrades instead of crashing.

## Guard

`src/lib/fixtures/state.json` carries one task per variant, **including a
`Locked` wrapping a `Done` with `{"Failed": 127}`**, and `just verify` asserts
every accessor against it.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md
# `ray build` succeeds on code that `tsc` rejects

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
ready  - built extension successfully
```

…on a file with genuine type errors. Then, at runtime, a component receives the
wrong shape and either renders nothing or throws something unrelated-looking.

## Cause

`ray build` bundles with esbuild. esbuild **strips types without checking
them**. It reports success for anything syntactically valid.

Two real errors shipped past it in this repo:

1. The Groups view passed a `MutatePromise<GroupMap>` to an `act()` typed for
   `MutatePromise<State>`. At runtime its optimistic update would have replaced
   the group map with a task state — the list would have emptied on every
   action.
2. `@raycast/api` bundles **its own copy of `@types/react`**, so the root
   `React.ReactNode` is a structurally different type that silently fails to
   match `ActionPanel`'s children.

Neither produced a single line of output from `ray build`.

## Fix

```make
typecheck:
    npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json

check: typecheck verify lint build
```

`just check` is the gate. `ray build` alone proves only that the bundle exists.

## The React types clash specifically

When a prop needs to hold JSX, type it as an element rather than a node:

```ts
function logActions(task: Task, extra?: React.JSX.Element | null) { … }
```

`React.ReactNode` resolves to the *root* `@types/react`, which is not the copy
`@raycast/api`'s components are typed against.

## Note

`ray lint` doesn't typecheck either — it runs ESLint and Prettier. It does catch
things `tsc` won't, including reserved-shortcut collisions (`⌘K` and `⌘P` are
Raycast's own and are silently ignored if you bind them), so both are needed.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/raycast-launchd-path-pueue-not-found.md
# `pueue` not found from Raycast, but works in the terminal

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
Error: spawn pueue ENOENT
pueue CLI not found
```

The extension shows **"Pueue CLI not found"** while `which pueue` in your
terminal answers immediately.

## Cause

Raycast runs extensions in a managed Node process under **launchd**, which never
sources `~/.zshrc`, `~/.zprofile`, or any other shell rc. Homebrew's `bin` and
`~/.cargo/bin` are added to `PATH` *by those files*, so the extension's `PATH` is
roughly `/usr/bin:/bin` and a bare `pueue` cannot be found.

## Fix

Never invoke a bare binary name. `src/lib/pueue/binary.ts` resolves an absolute
path: the `pueuePath` preference first (validated with `existsSync`, so a stale
value falls through), then a probe of

```text
/opt/homebrew/bin   Apple Silicon Homebrew
/usr/local/bin      Intel Homebrew — and this machine, where /opt/homebrew does not exist
~/.cargo/bin
~/.local/bin
/usr/bin  /bin
```

Both Homebrew prefixes must be probed. Hardcoding either breaks half of all Macs.

## The part that makes this expensive to find

**A terminal hides the bug completely.** `npm run dev`'s console inherits your
full interactive `PATH`, so anything you test from there works, including a
`resolveBinary` that would fail in production.

Every PATH-related change must be exercised **from Raycast** — root search or the
menu bar — not from the dev terminal.

## Related

The same launchd environment problem, one level out: a `pueued` started as a
child of a GUI process hands its stripped environment to every task it ever runs.
That's why the one-click *Start Daemon* action only appears when `brew services`
manages the daemon — see `src/lib/error-states.tsx`.
=============== /Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/pitfalls/raycast-preferences-cannot-be-multiline.md
# A multi-value preference can only hold one line

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
must be equal to one of the allowed values
```

…from `ray lint` when a preference uses `type: "textarea"`.

Or, with no error at all: a preference documented as "one entry per line"
accepts only the first entry, because the user cannot type a newline into it.

## Cause

**Raycast has no multi-line preference type.** The allowed set is exactly:

```text
appPicker | checkbox | dropdown | password | textfield | file | directory
```

`Form.TextArea` exists, but that is a *form* component inside a command — it has
nothing to do with `preferences[]` in the manifest. A `textfield` preference
renders as a single-line input, so a newline is not enterable.

Verified twice: the type union in `@raycast/api`'s `Preference` interface, and
empirically — setting `"type": "textarea"` on a preference makes `ray lint` fail
with `must be equal to one of the allowed values`.

## Why this is easy to miss

The parser works fine. Assertions over a `"a | h1\nb | h2"` fixture pass. The
docs read sensibly. Nothing fails — the feature simply cannot be *configured*
past one entry, and only a user with a second remote ever finds out.

Documenting a newline-separated format is untestable-by-assertion in the way
that matters: the constraint lives in the settings UI, not in the code.

## Fix

Pick a separator that survives a single line. This extension uses `;` between
connections and `|` between fields within one:

```text
lab | local_ubuntu | ~/.cargo/bin/pueue ; gpu | gpu.example.com ; nas | ts_nas
```

`connections.ts` splits on `/[\n;]/` — newlines are still accepted, because a
value set by other means may contain them, but the UI can only ever produce
semicolons.

Say *why* in the user-facing docs. A reader who doesn't know Raycast
preferences are single-line will assume the semicolon is an arbitrary taste
and reach for a newline.

## Related

The same "it parses, so it must work" gap produced
the connection line that vanished silently — a
malformed entry was dropped without complaint, which is indistinguishable from
the feature being broken. Both are failures of the *configuration* surface
rather than the code, and neither shows up in a build or a test.

# A remote task ends as FailedToSpawn and never runs

## Symptoms (grep this section)

```text
FailedToSpawn
{"FailedToSpawn": "No such file or directory (os error 2)"}
Failed to canonicalize given working directory path
```

A task submitted to a **remote** daemon finishes instantly having produced
nothing — or the client refuses to submit it at all.

## Cause

pueue records a task's working directory at submit time and **canonicalises it
on whichever machine the client runs on**. Against a remote daemon that is the
wrong machine, and it fails in three distinct ways:

| Submitted with | Result |
|---|---|
| a local directory that exists here | The local path is sent; it doesn't exist on the daemon → `FailedToSpawn` |
| a remote-only path | The **local** client refuses: `Failed to canonicalize given working directory path` |
| `/tmp`, from macOS | Silently rewritten to `/private/tmp` (a macOS symlink) → fails on Linux |

Only a path existing *and canonicalising identically on both machines* works —
`/usr` does, your project directory does not. This makes cross-platform remote
submission impractical by the obvious route.

## Fix

Give the connection an SSH host, and submission runs the client on the far side
where the paths are real:

```text
gpu-box | ~/.config/pueue/remote/client.yml | myhost
```

Add Task then submits with `ssh myhost 'pueue add …'`. Reads and control
commands still use the forwarded socket — SSH is only for submission, because
submission is the only operation that resolves a path.

Without an SSH host the working-directory field says so rather than letting you
submit a job that can only fail.

## Two things this drags along

1. **The whole command has to survive one more shell.** `ssh host '<cmd>'` hands
   its argument to the *remote* shell, so everything is POSIX single-quoted
   (`'\''` for embedded quotes) in `src/lib/pueue/ssh.ts`. This is separate from
   `argvFor`, which is deliberately quote-free because `execFile` needs none.
2. **`FailedToSpawn` is `Done`, not `Failed`,** and its result is dict-shaped
   rather than a bare string. A denylist of failure results misses it and reports
   a job that never started as a success — which is why `isFailed` is an
   allowlist of "terminal and not Success".

## Related

- [`../docs/remote.md`](../docs/remote.md) — full setup
- `read_local_logs: false` is a separate hard requirement; without it a remote
  task's log read returns a *local* task's output under the same id.
```

```text
1	# Raycast surfaces, as they exist in 2026
2	
3	Why this extension is shaped the way it is. Written after checking the live
4	docs, because the answer to "can Raycast do X" is frequently no in a way that is
5	hard to confirm from search results.
6	
7	## There is no widget API
8	
9	The complete list of extension entry points:
10	
11	| Entry point | Manifest | Notes |
12	| --- | --- | --- |
13	| View command | `"mode": "view"` | pushes a view onto the navigation stack |
14	| No-view command | `"mode": "no-view"` | runs and exits, no UI |
15	| **Menu bar command** | `"mode": "menu-bar"` | returns a `MenuBarExtra`. **macOS only** |
16	| AI tools | `"tools": [...]` | invoked by Raycast AI, **Pro-gated** |
17	| Script commands | separate repo | shell scripts, not TS extensions |
18	
19	That's it. No desktop widget surface, no Notification Center or Control Center
20	extension point, no Live-Activity equivalent, no floating window API. Nothing
21	widget-shaped shipped for extensions in "The New Raycast" (May 2026) or Glaze
22	(July 2026), and the "Widgets & Controls" pages on raycast.com are **iOS only**.
23	
24	**So a `mode: "menu-bar"` command is the only way to show something without
25	opening Raycast**, and that is what `src/queue-menu.tsx` is.
26	
27	## Menu bar constraints
28	
29	### There is no badge API
30	
31	The count *is* the `title`, and `undefined` removes it. Verified live: with
32	nothing running the number disappears and only the glyph remains.
33	
34	```tsx
35	title={running > 0 ? String(running) : undefined}
36	```
37	
38	This is the same idiom Homebrew's `services-menu` uses — the closest structural
39	precedent in the store, and worth reading.
40	
41	### `isLoading` is a contract
42	
43	From the docs, marked "danger": either never set it — in which case Raycast
44	renders and **immediately unloads** — or set it `true` during async work and
45	`false` when done. For a `menu-bar` command the whole React tree re-runs on
46	every tick until it goes false.
47	
48	### `interval` is manifest-only
49	
50	A preference cannot change it. Raycast renders its own refresh-interval control
51	in the command's settings. Brew hardcodes `"interval": "1m"` and ships no
52	interval preference; shipping one would be a lie.
53	
54	The docs contradict themselves on the floor — the background-refresh page says
55	`10s`, the manifest page says `1m`. `1m` is the safe value.
56	
57	Verified live: with three tasks started and **no** trigger from the extension,
58	the menu bar count updated on its own within 75 seconds.
59	
60	### Background refresh is off by default for store installs
61	
62	Until the user runs the command once or enables it in settings, a freshly
63	installed menu bar command shows **nothing**. This is the single most likely
64	"it's broken" report, so it's near the top of the README.
65	
66	### Restart restores from a database, not by re-running
67	
68	A stale render can outlive a Raycast restart, and there are open upstream issues
69	about stuck menu bar icons. The mitigation here is the `Updated HH:MM` row —
70	it makes staleness visible rather than misleading.
71	
72	### `confirmAlert` is unavailable in practice
73	
74	It presents in the Raycast window, which is closed when the menu is open. Rather
75	than risk a silently swallowed confirmation on a destructive action, destructive
76	menu bar items sit behind `⌥` and `Reset` / `Remove Group` aren't offered there
77	at all.
78	
79	### Identical sibling items misfire
80	
81	The docs warn that two identical `MenuBarExtra.Item`s at the same level get
82	their `onAction` handlers crossed. Every task row is prefixed with its id, which
83	makes collisions impossible.
84	
85	## Deeplinks prompt when triggered externally
86	
87	`open "raycast://extensions/<author>/<ext>/<command>"` shows:
88	
89	> **Request to open ‹Command›** — The command was triggered from outside of
90	> Raycast. If you did not do this, please cancel the operation.
91	
92	Per-command trust. It matters for two reasons: it's why an external nudge is a
93	poor substitute for `launchCommand` (see
94	[`../backlog/callback-notifications.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/blob/main/backlog/callback-notifications.md)),
95	and it's why some verification during development needs a real keypress rather
96	than a deeplink.
97	
98	`launchCommand` **from inside** an extension does not prompt, and
99	`LaunchType.Background` is the documented way to force a sibling command's
100	refresh — which is what every mutation does to the menu bar.
101	
102	## Reserved shortcuts
103	
104	`⌘K` (OpenActionPanel) and `⌘P` (OpenSearchBarDropdown) are Raycast's own. Bind
105	them and they are **silently ignored**. `ray lint` catches this; `tsc` does not.
106	
107	## What `ray` actually checks
108	
109	| Command | Checks |
110	| --- | --- |
111	| `ray build` | bundles with esbuild — **does not typecheck** |
112	| `ray lint` | ESLint + Prettier + manifest + icons — does not typecheck |
113	| `tsc --noEmit` | types |
114	
115	All three are needed. See
116	[`../pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md`](https://github.com/daviddwlee84/Pueue-Raycast-Extension/blob/main/pitfalls/ray-build-does-not-typecheck.md).
117
```

# Store screenshots

Raycast requires **3–6 PNGs at 2000×1250** (16:10) here before publishing.

Use Raycast's **Window Capture**, which writes correctly-sized files straight
into this folder — don't use `screencapture`, which photographs your whole
desktop.

1. Give Window Capture a hotkey: Raycast Settings → Advanced → Window Capture
   (the docs suggest `⌘⇧⌥M`), or set a hotkey on the **Capture Window** command.
2. Open the extension command you want to shoot, under `just dev`.
3. Press the hotkey, **tick "Save to Metadata"**, then click the camera button.

The "Save to Metadata" option only appears when a `metadata` folder already
exists — it does, because of this file.

Suggested set:

1. **Tasks** — the list with several statuses (running, stashed, failed)
2. **Tasks** — the detail pane open on a failed task, showing the exit code and log
3. **Add Task** — the form with the advanced options revealed (⌘⇧A)
4. **Groups** — two or three groups with different parallelism and pause states
5. **Queue Menu Bar** — the menu open, showing the Running / Failed sections

`just fixtures` seeds a queue that covers most of these states.

This directory is the last unchecked item in

=========== backlog/store-publishing.md
# Publishing to the public Raycast store

**Status:** `P?` · decision deferred by design

## Where things stand

The repo is built store-ready. Everything on Raycast's checklist is done except
screenshots:

- [x] `author` is a registered Raycast username (`da-wei_lee`), MIT `LICENSE`,
      `license` field, categories, one-sentence description, `platforms`
- [x] committed `package-lock.json` (`npm ci` works from a clean checkout)
- [x] 512×512 PNG icon that reads on light and dark
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` opening with `## [Initial Version] - {PR_MERGE_DATE}`
- [x] `README.md` covering install, daemon start, and the background-refresh
      default
- [x] `ray lint` and `ray build` clean, plus `tsc --noEmit`
- [x] graceful onboarding for both structural failures
- [ ] **3–6 screenshots at 2000×1250**, captured with Raycast's *Save Screenshot*

## The reviewable question

Store guidance says:

> "Avoid asking users to perform additional downloads and try to automate as
> much as possible from the extension, especially if you are targeting
> non-developers."

but also explicitly allows:

> "✅ Calling known system binaries"

A Homebrew-installed `pueue` is the second. The guidance is soft ("try to",
"especially if…") and there is shipping precedent for requiring a pre-installed
CLI or daemon: **brew** (which itself ships a `menu-bar` command at
`interval: 1m`), **colima**, **orbstack**, and **yabai**.

What a reviewer looks for is graceful degradation rather than a raw error, which
is what `src/lib/error-states.tsx` is.

## Publishing mechanics

`npm run publish` (= `npx @raycast/api@latest publish`) authenticates with
GitHub and opens a pull request against `raycast/extensions`. CI runs, then the
Raycast team reviews. Turnaround is days, not seconds. This is closer to
Homebrew core than to PyPI.

## One wrinkle

`npm run publish` uploads the extension directory, which here is the repo root —
so `backlog/`, `pitfalls/`, `TODO.md`, and the `Justfile` would ride along and
add review noise. They're small and harmless, and a reviewer is unlikely to
care.

If one does, the escape hatch is a `just store-export` recipe that rsyncs a
clean subset to a temp directory and publishes from there. Not worth building
pre-emptively.

## What would have to be true

Screenshots taken, and a decision that this should be public rather than
personal. Local `ray develop` already persists the extension in root search
after dev stops, so nothing is blocked on publishing.

=========== backlog/ai-tools.md
# AI tools

**Status:** `P?` · **Effort:** `[M]` · not started

## What

A `tools[]` array in the manifest turns the extension into an AI Extension.
Tools don't appear in root search; Raycast AI calls them, using each tool's
`description` to decide when.

Natural candidates, all of which map onto existing transport calls:

| Tool | Maps to |
| --- | --- |
| what's running | `status()` filtered to running |
| queue this | `mutate({op: "add", …})` |
| why did task N fail | `status()` + `readLogText(N)` |
| kill everything in group X | `mutate({op: "kill", group: X})` |

The transport already returns structured data, so a tool is a thin wrapper — the
work is prompt-shaped, not code-shaped.

## Why it isn't done

**AI Extensions require Raycast Pro.** From
[developers.raycast.com/ai/getting-started](https://developers.raycast.com/ai/getting-started):

> "To use AI APIs or AI Extensions, you need to subscribe to Raycast Pro."

So this can only ever be an additive layer for Pro subscribers, never the
primary way to use the extension. Everything it would offer already exists as a
command.

## Caution if it is built

Mutating tools are the risk. An AI that decides "kill everything in the default
group" from an ambiguous sentence is worse than no tool, and there is no
confirmation surface in an AI tool call comparable to `confirmAlert`. If this
ships, the first version should be **read-only** — status, logs, why-did-this-
fail — with `add` at most, and nothing destructive.

## What would have to be true

A Pro subscription to test against, and a decision that read-only tools are
worth the manifest surface.
```

63	 * producing an unexplained ENOENT.
64	 */

```text
1	# Pueue Raycast Extension
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	You asked whether a Raycast "widget" for [Pueue](https://github.com/Nukesor/pueue) is feasible. Two premises needed correcting before designing anything:
6	
7	1. **Raycast has no widget API.** The complete list of extension entry points in 2026 is `mode: "view"`, `mode: "no-view"`, `mode: "menu-bar"` (macOS-only), AI `tools[]` (Raycast **Pro**-gated), and Script Commands. Nothing widget-shaped shipped in "The New Raycast" (May 2026) or Glaze (July 2026); the "Widgets" pages on raycast.com are iOS-only. **The real target is a `mode: "menu-bar"` command** (`MenuBarExtra` + a manifest `interval`).
8	2. **Nobody has built this.** Verified four ways — `gh search code repo:raycast/extensions`, repo search, Raycast store search, web search. `jakevossen5/pueue-bar` (2021) is an empty repo with a one-line README. There is also no xbar/SwiftBar plugin and no Alfred workflow. This would be the first.
9	
10	**Outcome:** a standalone, store-ready Raycast extension at `/Users/david/Documents/Program/Pueue-Raycast-Extension` (currently an empty git repo, zero commits) that shells out to the `pueue` CLI. A menu-bar command gives the glanceable surface; view commands (Tasks, Add Task, Groups, Quick Add) are where work happens.
11	
12	**Decisions taken:** menu bar + full command set · shell out to `pueue --json` (CBOR socket transport is backlog, behind one file boundary) · build store-ready but defer `publish` · document the `daemon.callback` notification recipe, **never write to the user's `pueue.yml`**.
13	
14	The closest structural precedent is Homebrew's `services-menu` in `raycast/extensions` (menu-bar, `interval: 1m`, count in `title`, optimistic refresh after each action). Its own header comment states our exact constraint: no push notification of state changes, so poll.
15	
16	## Constraints verified on this machine
17	
18	Pueue **v4.0.4**, Homebrew at `/usr/local/bin/pueue` (Intel prefix — `/opt/homebrew/bin` does not exist here), daemon under `brew services`/launchd, config at `~/Library/Application Support/pueue/pueue.yml` (*not* `~/.config/pueue/`). `pueue status --json` measures **22–44 ms** (median 28 ms). Raycast runs extensions on its own bundled **Node 22**.
19	
20	These traps are load-bearing — each one is a bug if missed:
21	
22	| # | Trap | Consequence |
23	|---|---|---|
24	| 1 | `--color` is a **global** flag. `pueue status --color never` → **exit 2**, clap error. Correct: `pueue --color never status --json`. | Exit codes are **0/1/2**, not 0/1. |
25	| 2 | `color_eyre` writes **ANSI to stderr even when piped**; neither `--color never` nor `NO_COLOR=1` suppresses it. | Any surfaced stderr must be ANSI-stripped, plus `Location:`/backtrace lines dropped. |
26	| 3 | `status` is a **nested externally-tagged enum**. There is no flat `"status":"Running"`. `Locked` is **recursive**. `TaskResult` mixes bare strings (`"Success"`) with objects (`{"Failed":127}`). | Every v3-era example online is wrong. |
27	| 4 | `Stashed` carries `enqueue_at`; every other variant carries `enqueue**d**_at`. | One-letter typo → silently undefined. |
28	| 5 | `new Date(null)` returns **1970-01-01**, not `Invalid Date`, and `Stashed.enqueue_at` is nullable. | Renders "1970" instead of "—" without a guard. |
29	| 6 | `group --json` returns the **inner map** (`{"default":{…}}`), a different top level from `status --json` (`{"tasks":…,"groups":…}`). | Sharing one parser is the easiest bug in the codebase. |
30	| 7 | `envs` is a **full snapshot of the submitting shell's environment**, present in `status --json` (~2 MB for 400 tasks upstream) and may contain secrets. | Must be stripped at the parse boundary before anything caches it to disk. |
31	| 8 | The daemon acks a request **before** its update loop applies it. | An immediate revalidate reads pre-change state and visually undoes the optimistic update. |
32	| 9 | `pueue kill -g GROUP` **also pauses the group**; `-a` pauses all. `pueue group remove NAME` **moves its tasks to `default`**. | Confirmation copy must say so. |
33	| 10 | `pueue parallel` with no args is broken (logs "Received unhandled response message", exits 0, prints nothing). | Read parallelism from `group --json`. |
34	| 11 | `pueue log <bad-id> --json` → `{}` with **exit 0**. | Empty ≠ error. |
35	| 12 | `interval` is a **manifest field**; a preference cannot change it. Brew hardcodes `"interval": "1m"` with no interval preference (verified in its installed manifest). Raycast renders its own refresh control in command settings. | Do not ship an interval preference. |
36	| 13 | Background refresh is **disabled by default for store installs** until the command is run once. | A fresh install shows nothing in the menu bar. Top README item. |
37	| 14 | On Raycast restart the menu-bar item is **restored from Raycast's database**, not by re-running the command. | Stale renders survive restarts (upstream #14250, #20031, #14659). |
38	| 15 | Raycast runs under launchd with no shell rc, so bare `pueue` throws `ENOENT` — **but a terminal hides this**, because `npm run dev`'s console inherits your full PATH. | Every PATH-related test must be run *from Raycast*. |
39	
40	Only three commands emit JSON: `status`, `log`, `group`. All 15 mutations are exit-code + prose only. `status` accepts a client-side query DSL that composes with `--json` (`status=failed order_by id desc first 20`); note `columns=id,status` — the brackets in the grammar docs are meta-notation, `columns=[id]` fails.
41	
42	## Repo layout — extension at the root
43	
44	Not a subdirectory: `ray build`/`develop`/`lint` all resolve `./package.json` and write `./raycast-env.d.ts` relative to cwd, and `npm run publish` copies the extension directory verbatim into `extensions/pueue/`. The reference repo uses `raycast/extension/` only because its primary artifact is a Go CLI; here the extension *is* the repo.
45	
46	```
47	package.json · package-lock.json (committed) · tsconfig.json · eslint.config.js
48	raycast-env.d.ts (generated, committed) · README.md · CHANGELOG.md · LICENSE · Justfile · TODO.md

54	src/

56	  lib/

59	      types.ts                wire types, no I/O
